4.138.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
puṇyā mahānavamyasti tithīnāṃ pravarā tithiḥ .
sānuṣṭheyā suraiḥ sarvaiḥ prajāpālairviśeṣataḥ . . 1
4.138.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
पुण्या महानवम्यस्ति तिथीनां प्रवरा तिथिः ।
सानुष्ठेया सुरैः सर्वैः प्रजापालैर्विशेषतः ॥ 1

4.138.s:
bhavānutthāpayetpārtha samvatsarasukhāya vai .
bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ prītyarthaṃ cotsavāya vā . . 2
4.138.d:
भवानुत्थापयेत्पार्थ सम्वत्सरसुखाय वै ।
भूतप्रेतपिशाचानां प्रीत्यर्थं चोत्सवाय वा ॥ 2
4.138.m:
You should celebrate it, O son of Pṛthā, indeed for happiness throughout the year,
for the pleasure of ghosts, pretas, and piśācas, or as a festival.

4.138.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca
kasmātkālātpravṛtteyaṃ navamī mahaśabdayuk .
kimādāvupapanno'sti bhagavannavamīvidhiḥ . . 3
4.138.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच
कस्मात्कालात्प्रवृत्तेयं नवमी महशब्दयुक् ।
किमादावुपपन्नोऽस्ति भगवन्नवमीविधिः ॥ 3
4.138.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
From what time did this navamī, joined with the word 'mahā-', begin?
At what origin, O Lord, did the ordinance of the navamī come about?

4.138.s:
yaśodāgarbhasambhūteruta yātrā pravartate .
utāho pūrvamevāsītkṛtatretāyugādiṣu . . 4
4.138.d:
यशोदागर्भसम्भूतेरुत यात्रा प्रवर्तते ।
उताहो पूर्वमेवासीत्कृतत्रेतायुगादिषु ॥ 4
4.138.m:
Did the procession begin from her birth from the womb of Yaśodā,
or did it exist even earlier, at the beginning of the Kṛta and Tretā yugas?

4.138.s:
yadasyāṃ prāṇinaḥ kecinmanyante ghātayanti ca .
hatānāṃ prāṇināṃ teṣāṃ kā gatiḥ pāralaukikī . . 5
4.138.d:
यदस्यां प्राणिनः केचिन्मन्यन्ते घातयन्ति च ।
हतानां प्राणिनां तेषां का गतिः पारलौकिकी ॥ 5
4.138.m:
Since on this day some people vow [offerings of] living beings and slaughter them,
what is the otherworldly destiny of those creatures who are slain?

4.138.s:
svayaṃ ghnatāṃ ghātayatāmanumodayatāṃ tathā .
etanme saṃśayaṃ pūrvaṃ vaktumarhasi keśava . . 6
4.138.d:
स्वयं घ्नतां घातयतामनुमोदयतां तथा ।
एतन्मे संशयं पूर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि केशव ॥ 6
4.138.m:
And what of those who kill themselves, cause others to kill, and likewise applaud it?
You should first resolve this doubt of mine, O Keśava.

4.138.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
pārtha yā paramā śaktiranantā lokaviśrutā .
ādyā sarvagatā śuddhā bhāvagamyā manoharā . . 7
4.138.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
पार्थ या परमा शक्तिरनन्ता लोकविश्रुता ।
आद्या सर्वगता शुद्धा भावगम्या मनोहरा ॥ 7
4.138.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O son of Pṛthā, that supreme power which is endless, renowned in the world,
primordial, all-pervading, pure, accessible through devotion, and captivating—

4.138.s:
ādyāṣṭamī kalākālī dvitīyā sarvamaṅgalā .
māyā kātyāyanī durgā cāmuṇḍā śaṅkarapriyā . . 8
4.138.d:
आद्याष्टमी कलाकाली द्वितीया सर्वमङ्गला ।
माया कात्यायनी दुर्गा चामुण्डा शङ्करप्रिया ॥ 8
4.138.m:
the primordial aṣṭamī, Kālī of the arts, the second, Sarvamaṅgalā,
Māyā, Kātyāyanī, Durgā, Cāmuṇḍā, the beloved of Śaṅkara;

4.138.s:
dhyāyanti yāṃ yogaratāṃ sā devī parameśvarī .
rūpabhedairnāmabhedairbhavānī pūjyate śivā . . 9
4.138.d:
ध्यायन्ति यां योगरतां सा देवी परमेश्वरी ।
रूपभेदैर्नामभेदैर्भवानी पूज्यते शिवा ॥ 9
4.138.m:
she whom those intent on yoga contemplate, she is the goddess Parameśvarī;
through various forms and various names, Bhavānī, Śivā, is worshipped.

4.138.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ tu navamyāṃ tu devadānavarākṣasaiḥ .
gandharvairuragairyajñaiḥ pūjyate kinnarairnaraiḥ . . 4.138.10
4.138.d:
अष्टम्यां तु नवम्यां तु देवदानवराक्षसैः ।
गन्धर्वैरुरगैर्यज्ञैः पूज्यते किन्नरैर्नरैः ॥ 4.138.10
4.138.m:
On the aṣṭamī and on the navamī, by gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas,
by gandharvas, serpents, spirits, by kinnaras and humans, she is worshipped.

4.138.s:
anyeṣvapi yugeṣvādau sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ pradarśitā .
pūjyateyaṃ purā devī tebhyaḥ pūrvataraiḥ śubhaiḥ . . 11
4.138.d:
अन्येष्वपि युगेष्वादौ सृष्टेः पूर्वं प्रदर्शिता ।
पूज्यतेयं पुरा देवी तेभ्यः पूर्वतरैः शुभैः ॥ 11
4.138.m:
In other yugas as well, she was manifested in the beginning, before creation;
formerly this goddess was worshipped by auspicious beings even earlier than them.

4.138.s:
āśvayukchuklapakṣe ca yāṣṭamī mūlasaṃyutā .
sā mahānavamī nāma trailokye'pi sudurlabhā . . 12
4.138.d:
आश्वयुक्छुक्लपक्षे च याष्टमी मूलसंयुता ।
सा महानवमी नाम त्रैलोक्येऽपि सुदुर्लभा ॥ 12
4.138.m:
And in the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja, that aṣṭamī conjoined with Mūla
is indeed called Mahānavamī, very difficult to obtain even in the three worlds.

4.138.s:
kanyāgate savitari śuklapakṣe'ṣṭamī tu yā .
mūlanakṣatrasaṃyuktā sā mahānavamī smṛtā . . 13
4.138.d:
कन्यागते सवितरि शुक्लपक्षेऽष्टमी तु या ।
मूलनक्षत्रसंयुक्ता सा महानवमी स्मृता ॥ 13
4.138.m:
When the sun enters Virgo, that aṣṭamī in the bright fortnight
joined with the asterism Mūla is known as Mahānavamī.

4.138.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ ca navamyāṃ ca jaganmātaramambikām .
pūjayityā''śvine māsi viśoko jayati dviṣaḥ . . 14
4.138.d:
अष्टम्यां च नवम्यां च जगन्मातरमम्बिकाम् ।
पूजयित्या'ऽश्विने मासि विशोको जयति द्विषः ॥ 14
4.138.m:
Having worshipped the mother of the world, Ambikā, on the aṣṭamī and navamī
in the month of Āśvina, one conquers enemies free from sorrow.

4.138.s:
santarjayantī huṃkāraiḥ khaḍgādibhiraharniśam .
navamyāṃ pūjitā devī dadāti navamaṃ phalam . . 15
4.138.d:
सन्तर्जयन्ती हुंकारैः खड्गादिभिरहर्निशम् ।
नवम्यां पूजिता देवी ददाति नवमं फलम् ॥ 15
4.138.m:
Frightening [enemies] with roars, day and night, with swords and other weapons,
the goddess, worshipped on the navamī, grants the ninth fruit.

4.138.s:
sā puṇyā sā pavitrā ca sā dharmasukhadāyinī .
tasmātsadā pūjanīyā cāmuṇḍāmuṇḍamālinī . . 16
4.138.d:
सा पुण्या सा पवित्रा च सा धर्मसुखदायिनी ।
तस्मात्सदा पूजनीया चामुण्डामुण्डमालिनी ॥ 16
4.138.m:
She is meritorious, she is pure, she is the giver of virtue and happiness;
therefore Cāmuṇḍā, garlanded with human heads, is always to be worshipped.

4.138.s:
tasyāṃ yadyupayujyante prāṇino mahiṣādayaḥ .
sarve te svargatiṃ yānti ghnatāṃ pāpaṃ na vidyate . . 17
4.138.d:
तस्यां यद्युपयुज्यन्ते प्राणिनो महिषादयः ।
सर्वे ते स्वर्गतिं यान्ति घ्नतां पापं न विद्यते ॥ 17
4.138.m:
If on that [day] living creatures such as buffaloes are employed [in sacrifice],
they all go to heaven, and no sin accrues to those who slaughter them.

4.138.s:
na tathā balidānena puṣpadhūpavilepanaiḥ .
yathā saṃtuṣyate loke mahiṣairvindhyavāsinī . . 18
4.138.d:
न तथा बलिदानेन पुष्पधूपविलेपनैः ।
यथा संतुष्यते लोके महिषैर्विन्ध्यवासिनी ॥ 18
4.138.m:
Not by animal sacrifice [of other kinds], nor by flowers, incense, and ointments,
is Vindhyavāsinī pleased in the world as she is by buffaloes.

4.138.s:
uddiśya durgāṃ hanyante vidhānādye'tra jantavaḥ .
svargaṃ te yānti kaunteya ghātayanto'pi bhaktitaḥ . . 19
4.138.d:
उद्दिश्य दुर्गां हन्यन्ते विधानाद्येऽत्र जन्तवः ।
स्वर्गं ते यान्ति कौन्तेय घातयन्तोऽपि भक्तितः ॥ 19
4.138.m:
Whatever creatures are slain here according to the ordinance, destined for Durgā,
they go to heaven, O son of Kuntī, as do those who slaughter them with devotion.

4.138.s:
bhavānīprāṅgaṇe prāṇā yeṣāṃ yātā yudhiṣṭhira .
teṣāṃ svarge dhruvaṃ vāso varāste'psarasāṃ priyāḥ . . 4.138.20
4.138.d:
भवानीप्राङ्गणे प्राणा येषां याता युधिष्ठिर ।
तेषां स्वर्गे ध्रुवं वासो वरास्तेऽप्सरसां प्रियाः ॥ 4.138.20
4.138.m:
Those whose lives depart in the courtyard of Bhavānī, O Yudhiṣṭhira,
their dwelling is surely in heaven; they are excellent, beloved of apsarases.

4.138.s:
manvantareṣu sarveṣu kalpeṣu kurunandana .
teṣu sarveṣu caivāsīnnavamīyaṃ purārcitā .. 21 ..
4.138.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु कल्पेषु कुरुनन्दन ।
तेषु सर्वेषु चैवासीन्नवमीयं पुरार्चिता ॥ 21 ॥
4.138.m:
In all the manvantaras and kalpas, O delight of the Kurus,
throughout all of them this navamī was formerly worshipped.

4.138.s:
prasiddhānādinidhanā varṣevarṣe yudhiṣṭhira ..
bhūyobhūyo'vatāraiśca bhavānī pūjyate suraiḥ .. 22 ..
4.138.d:
प्रसिद्धानादिनिधना वर्षेवर्षे युधिष्ठिर ॥
भूयोभूयोऽवतारैश्च भवानी पूज्यते सुरैः ॥ 22 ॥
4.138.m:
Celebrated, without beginning or end, year after year, O Yudhiṣṭhira,
Bhavānī is worshipped by the gods through her repeated incarnations.

4.138.s:
avatīrṇā bhuvi sadā nityaṃ daityanibarhiṇī ..
svargapātālamartyeṣu karoti sthitipālanam .. 23 ..
4.138.d:
अवतीर्णा भुवि सदा नित्यं दैत्यनिबर्हिणी ॥
स्वर्गपातालमर्त्येषु करोति स्थितिपालनम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.138.m:
Having descended to earth perpetually, ever the destroyer of Daityas,
she maintains the preservation of order in heaven, the netherworld, and the mortal realm.

4.138.s:
punaścaiṣā mahādevī yaśodā garbhasaṃbhavā ..
kaṃsāsurasyottamāṅge pādaṃ dattvā gatāyuṣaḥ .. 24 ..
4.138.d:
पुनश्चैषा महादेवी यशोदा गर्भसंभवा ॥
कंसासुरस्योत्तमाङ्गे पादं दत्त्वा गतायुषः ॥ 24 ॥
4.138.m:
And again this great goddess, born of the womb of Yaśodā,
placed her foot on the head of the asura Kaṃsa whose lifespan had run out.

4.138.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti lokeṣu yaśodānaṃdadāyinīm ..
viṃdhyācale sthāpayitvā punaḥ pūjā pravartitā .. 25 ..
4.138.d:
ततः प्रभृति लोकेषु यशोदानंददायिनीम् ॥
विंध्याचले स्थापयित्वा पुनः पूजा प्रवर्तिता ॥ 25 ॥
4.138.m:
From then on in the worlds, having established her who brought joy to Yaśodā
upon the Vindhya mountain, her worship was initiated again.

4.138.s:
pūrvapravṛddho'pi punarbhaginyā mahimā kṛtaḥ ..
bhuvi sarvopakārāya sarvopadravaśāṃtaye .. 26 ..
4.138.d:
पूर्वप्रवृद्धोऽपि पुनर्भगिन्या महिमा कृतः ॥
भुवि सर्वोपकाराय सर्वोपद्रवशांतये ॥ 26 ॥
4.138.m:
Though previously established, the sister's greatness was celebrated once more
for the benefit of all and for the pacification of all afflictions on earth.

4.138.s:
evaṃ viṃdhyopavāsinyā navarātropavāsinaḥ ..
ekarātreṇa naktena svaśaktyā'yācitena vā .. 27 ..
4.138.d:
एवं विंध्योपवासिन्या नवरात्रोपवासिनः ॥
एकरात्रेण नक्तेन स्वशक्त्याऽयाचितेन वा ॥ 27 ॥
4.138.m:
Thus, fasting for the Navarātra for Vindhyavāsinī,
by a single night's [fast], by a nocturnal meal, according to one's capacity, or by unasked-for food,

4.138.s:
yajanairyājanairdevāḥ sthānesthāne purepure ..
gṛhegṛhe bhaktipare grāmegrāme vanevane .. 28 ..
4.138.d:
यजनैर्याजनैर्देवाः स्थानेस्थाने पुरेपुरे ॥
गृहेगृहे भक्तिपरे ग्रामेग्रामे वनेवने ॥ 28 ॥
4.138.m:
through sacrifices and officiating at sacrifices, the gods [are worshipped] in every place, every city,
every house devoted to worship, every village, and every forest,

4.138.s:
snātaiḥ pramuditairhṛṣṭairbrāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairnṛpaiḥ ..
vaiśyaiḥ śūdrairbhakticitrairmlecchairanyaiśca mānavaiḥ .. 29 ..
4.138.d:
स्नातैः प्रमुदितैर्हृष्टैर्ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्नृपैः ॥
वैश्यैः शूद्रैर्भक्तिचित्रैर्म्लेच्छैरन्यैश्च मानवैः ॥ 29 ॥
4.138.m:
by Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, kings, who have bathed, are joyous, and glad,
by Vaiśyas, Śūdras filled with various kinds of devotion, by mlecchas, and other men,

4.138.s:
strībhiśca kuruśārdūla tadvidhānamidaṃ śṛṇu ..
jayābhilāṣī nṛpatiḥ pratipatprabhṛtikramāt .. 4.138.30 ..
4.138.d:
स्त्रीभिश्च कुरुशार्दूल तद्विधानमिदं शृणु ॥
जयाभिलाषी नृपतिः प्रतिपत्प्रभृतिक्रमात् ॥ 4.138.30 ॥
4.138.m:
and by women, O tiger among the Kurus; hear this procedure for it.
A king desiring victory, in sequence beginning with the first lunar day,

4.138.s:
lohābhihārikaṃ karma kārayedyāvadaṣṭami ..
prāgudakpravaṇe deśe patākābhiralaṃkṛtam .. 31 ..
4.138.d:
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कारयेद्यावदष्टमि ॥
प्रागुदक्प्रवणे देशे पताकाभिरलंकृतम् ॥ 31 ॥
4.138.m:
should have the iron-lustration rite performed until the aṣṭamī.
In a region sloping to the east or north, decorated with banners,

4.138.s:
maṇḍapaṃ kārayeddivyaṃ navasaptakaraṃ varam..
āgneyyāṃ kārayetkuṇḍaṃ hastamātraṃ suśobhanam .. 32 ..
4.138.d:
मण्डपं कारयेद्दिव्यं नवसप्तकरं वरम्॥
आग्नेय्यां कारयेत्कुण्डं हस्तमात्रं सुशोभनम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.138.m:
he should have a divine, excellent pavilion built, nine by seven cubits.
In the south-east he should make a very beautiful sacrificial pit, just one cubit [in size],

4.138.s:
mekhalātrayasaṃ yuktaṃ yonyaśvatthadalābhayā ..
rājacihnāni sarvāṇi śastrāṇyastrāṇi yāni ca .. 33 ..
4.138.d:
मेखलात्रयसं युक्तं योन्यश्वत्थदलाभया ॥
राजचिह्नानि सर्वाणि शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि यानि च ॥ 33 ॥
4.138.m:
endowed with three tiers, with a vulva shaped like an aśvattha leaf.
All the insignia of royalty and whatever weapons and missiles there are,

4.138.s:
ānīya maṇḍape tāni sarvāṇyevādhivāsayet ..
tatastu brāhmaṇaḥ snātaḥ śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuciḥ .. 34 ..
4.138.d:
आनीय मण्डपे तानि सर्वाण्येवाधिवासयेत् ॥
ततस्तु ब्राह्मणः स्नातः शुक्लांबरधरः शुचिः ॥ 34 ॥
4.138.m:
having brought all of them into the pavilion, he should consecrate them.
Then a Brahmin, bathed, wearing white garments, pure,

4.138.s:
oṃkārarapūrvakairmantraistalliṃgairjuhuyād ghṛtam..
lohanāmābhavatpūrvaṃ dānavastu mahābalaḥ .. 35 ..
4.138.d:
ओंकाररपूर्वकैर्मन्त्रैस्तल्लिंगैर्जुहुयाद् घृतम्॥
लोहनामाभवत्पूर्वं दानवस्तु महाबलः ॥ 35 ॥
4.138.m:
should offer clarified butter with mantras preceded by the syllable Om containing their characteristic marks.
Formerly there was a very powerful dānava named Loha.

4.138.s:
sa devaiḥ samare kruddhairbahudhā śakalīkṛtaḥ ..
tadaṃgasambhavaṃ lohaṃ yatsarvaṃ dṛśyate kṣitau .. 36 ..
4.138.d:
स देवैः समरे क्रुद्धैर्बहुधा शकलीकृतः ॥
तदंगसम्भवं लोहं यत्सर्वं दृश्यते क्षितौ ॥ 36 ॥
4.138.m:
In battle he was cut into many pieces by the enraged gods;
all the iron that is seen on the earth arose from his limbs.

4.138.s:
śastrāstramantrairhotavyaṃ pāyasaṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam ..
hutaśeṣaṃ turaṃgāṇāṃ gajānāmupahārayet .. 37 ..
4.138.d:
शस्त्रास्त्रमन्त्रैर्होतव्यं पायसं घृतसंयुतम् ॥
हुतशेषं तुरंगाणां गजानामुपहारयेत् ॥ 37 ॥
4.138.m:
One should offer milk-rice mixed with clarified butter with the mantras of weapons and missiles;
he should present the remnants of the oblation to the horses and elephants.

4.138.s:
lohābhihārikaṃ karma tenaitadṛṣibhiḥ smṛtam ..
baddhapratiśaravyaṃ ca gajāśvasamalaṃkṛtam .. 38 ..
4.138.d:
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म तेनैतदृषिभिः स्मृतम् ॥
बद्धप्रतिशरव्यं च गजाश्वसमलंकृतम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.138.m:
Therefore this iron-lustration rite was remembered by the seers.
With an attached target-dummy and adorned with elephants and horses,

4.138.s:
bhrāmayennagare nityaṃ naṃdighoṣapurassaram ..
pratyahaṃ nṛpatiḥ snātvā saṃpūjya pitṛdevatāḥ .. 39 ..
4.138.d:
भ्रामयेन्नगरे नित्यं नंदिघोषपुरस्सरम् ॥
प्रत्यहं नृपतिः स्नात्वा संपूज्य पितृदेवताः ॥ 39 ॥
4.138.m:
he should process through the city daily, preceded by auspicious joyful shouts.
Every day the king, having bathed and worshipped the ancestral deities,

4.138.s:
pūjayedrājacihnāni phalamālyānulepanaiḥ ..
hutaśeṣaṃ pradātavyamaupanāyanike dvije .. 4.138.40 ..
4.138.d:
पूजयेद्राजचिह्नानि फलमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥
हुतशेषं प्रदातव्यमौपनायनिके द्विजे ॥ 4.138.40 ॥
4.138.m:
should worship the insignia of royalty with fruits, garlands, and ointments.
The remnants of the oblation should be given to a Brahmin who performs the sacred thread investiture.

4.138.s:
tasyābhiharaṇādrājño vijayaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ ..
pūjāmaṃtrānpravakṣyāmi purāṇoktānahaṃ tava .. 41 ..
4.138.d:
तस्याभिहरणाद्राज्ञो विजयः समुदाहृतः ॥
पूजामंत्रान्प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणोक्तानहं तव ॥ 41 ॥
4.138.m: From performing that lustration, victory is declared for the king. / I shall tell you the worship mantras proclaimed in the Purāṇas,

4.138.s:
yaiḥ pūjitāḥ prayacchanti kīrtimāyur yaśobalam ..
yathāṃbudaśchādayati śivāyemāṃ vasundharām .. 42 ..
4.138.d:
यैः पूजिताः प्रयच्छन्ति कीर्तिमायुर् यशोबलम् ॥
यथांबुदश्छादयति शिवायेमां वसुन्धराम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.138.m: Worshipped with which they grant fame, long life, glory, and strength. / Just as a cloud covers this earth for its welfare,

4.138.s:
tathācchādaya rājānaṃ vijayārogyavṛddhaye .. (iti chatramantraḥ) ..
gandharva kulajātastvaṃ mā bhūyāḥ kuladūṣakaḥ .. 43 ..
4.138.d:
तथाच्छादय राजानं विजयारोग्यवृद्धये ॥ (इति छत्रमन्त्रः) ॥
गन्धर्व कुलजातस्त्वं मा भूयाः कुलदूषकः ॥ 43 ॥
4.138.m: Even so cover the king, for the increase of victory and health. (Thus the mantra for the royal parasol.) / You are born in the lineage of the Gandharvas; do not be a defiler of your family.

4.138.s:
brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca ..
prabhāvācca hutāśasya varddhasva tvaṃ turaṃgama .. 44 ..
4.138.d:
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च ॥
प्रभावाच्च हुताशस्य वर्द्धस्व त्वं तुरंगम ॥ 44 ॥
4.138.m: By the true word of Brahmā, and of Soma and Varuṇa, / And by the power of the Fire-god, flourish, O horse!

4.138.s:
tejasā caiva sūryasya munīnāṃ tapasā yathā ..
rudrasya brahmacaryeṇa pavanasya balena ca.. 45 ..
4.138.d:
तेजसा चैव सूर्यस्य मुनीनां तपसा यथा ॥
रुद्रस्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पवनस्य बलेन च॥ 45 ॥
4.138.m: By the brilliance of the sun, and as by the asceticism of the sages, / By the chastity of Rudra, and by the power of the wind,

4.138.s:
smara tvaṃ rājaputro'si kaustubhaṃ ca maṇiṃ smara ..
yāṃ gatiṃ brahmahā gacchetpitṛhā mātṛhā tathā .. 46 ..
4.138.d:
स्मर त्वं राजपुत्रोऽसि कौस्तुभं च मणिं स्मर ॥
यां गतिं ब्रह्महा गच्छेत्पितृहा मातृहा तथा ॥ 46 ॥
4.138.m: Remember that you are a prince, and remember the Kaustubha jewel! / The destination reached by a killer of a brāhmaṇa, a killer of a father, and a killer of a mother,

4.138.s:
bhūmyarthenṛtavādī ca kṣatriyaśca parāṅmukhaḥ ..
sūryācandramasau vāyuḥ pāvakaśca na yatra vai .. 47 ..
4.138.d:
भूम्यर्थेनृतवादी च क्षत्रियश्च पराङ्मुखः ॥
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुः पावकश्च न यत्र वै ॥ 47 ॥
4.138.m: And by one who speaks untruth for the sake of land, and by a kṣatriya who turns his back [in battle], / Where indeed there is neither sun nor moon, nor wind nor fire—

4.138.s:
vrajecca tāṃ gatiṃ kṣipraṃ tacca pāpaṃ bhavetkila ..
vikṛtiṃ yadi gacchestvaṃ yuddhedhvani turaṃgama ..
ripūnvijitya samare saha bhartrā sukhī bhava .. 48 .. .. ( ityaśvamaṃtraḥ) .. ..
4.138.d:
व्रजेच्च तां गतिं क्षिप्रं तच्च पापं भवेत्किल ॥
विकृतिं यदि गच्छेस्त्वं युद्धेध्वनि तुरंगम ॥
रिपून्विजित्य समरे सह भर्त्रा सुखी भव ॥ 48 ॥ ॥ ( इत्यश्वमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
4.138.m: To that destination may he swiftly go, and may that sin indeed be yours, / If you should falter in battle on the road, O horse! / Having conquered the enemies in combat, be happy along with your master! (Thus the mantra for the horse.)

4.138.s:
śakraketo mahāvīrya suparṇastvayyupasthitaḥ ..
patatrirāḍvainateyastathā nārāyaṇadhvajaḥ .. 49 ..
4.138.d:
शक्रकेतो महावीर्य सुपर्णस्त्वय्युपस्थितः ॥
पतत्रिराड्वैनतेयस्तथा नारायणध्वजः ॥ 49 ॥
4.138.m: O standard of Indra, of great valour! The fair-winged one is stationed upon you, / The king of birds, the son of Vinatā, and the banner of Nārāyaṇa,

4.138.s:
kāśyapeyo'mṛto jñeyo nāgārirviṣṇuvāhanaḥ ..
aprameyo durādharṣo devaśatruniṣūdanaḥ .. 4.138.50 ..
4.138.d:
काश्यपेयोऽमृतो ज्ञेयो नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः ॥
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो देवशत्रुनिषूदनः ॥ 4.138.50 ॥
4.138.m: The son of Kaśyapa, known as immortal, the enemy of serpents, the mount of Viṣṇu, / Immeasurable, unconquerable, the destroyer of the enemies of the gods,

4.138.s:
garutmānmārutagatistvayi sannihitaḥ sthitaḥ ..
śastravarmāyudhānyodhānrakṣā smāṃśca ripūndaha .. 51 .. .. (iti dhvajamaṃtraḥ) .. ..
4.138.d:
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिस्त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः ॥
शस्त्रवर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षा स्मांश्च रिपून्दह ॥ 51 ॥ ॥ (इति ध्वजमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
4.138.m: Garutmān, who moves like the wind, is stationed right upon you. / Protect our weapons, armour, and warriors, and burn our enemies! (Thus the mantra for the banner.)

4.138.s:
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadaṃto'tha vāmanaḥ ..
supratīkoñjano nīla ete'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ ... .. 52 ..
4.138.d:
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदंतोऽथ वामनः ॥
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नील एतेऽष्टौ देवयोनयः ॥॥। 52 ॥
4.138.m: Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—these eight are of divine origin.

4.138.s:
eteṣāṃ putrapautrāśca balānyaṣṭau samāśritāḥ ..
bhadro mandro mṛgaścaiva gajaḥ saṃkīrṇa eva ca ..
vanevane prasūtāste kariyoniṃ mahāgajāḥ..53..
4.138.d:
एतेषां पुत्रपौत्राश्च बलान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः ॥
भद्रो मन्द्रो मृगश्चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च ॥
वनेवने प्रसूतास्ते करियोनिं महागजाः॥53॥
4.138.m: And their sons and grandsons have resorted to their eight strengths: / The bhadra, the mandra, the mṛga, and the saṃkīrṇa elephant. / Born in forest after forest, these great elephants belong to the elephant species.

4.138.s:
pāṃtu tvāṃ vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ ..
bhartāraṃ rakṣa nāgendra samayaṃ pratipālayan .. 54 ..
4.138.d:
पांतु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः ॥
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयं प्रतिपालयन् ॥ 54 ॥
4.138.m: May the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas along with the troops of Maruts protect you! / Protect your master, O lord of elephants, maintaining your allegiance!

4.138.s:
avāpurhi jayaṃ yuddhe gamane svasti no vraja ..
śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavonilāt..
sthairyaṃ merorjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devātpuraṃdarāt .. 55 ..
4.138.d:
अवापुर्हि जयं युद्धे गमने स्वस्ति नो व्रज ॥
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवोनिलात्॥
स्थैर्यं मेरोर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात्पुरंदरात् ॥ 55 ॥
4.138.m: May they indeed attain victory in battle; proceed on our march to our welfare! / May your splendour be from Soma, your strength from Viṣṇu, your brilliance from the sun, your speed from the wind, / Your steadfastness from Meru, your victory from Rudra, and your glory from the god Indra!

4.138.s:
yuddhe rakṣaṃtu nāgāstvāṃ diśaśca saha daivataiḥ ..
aśvinau saha gaṃdharvaiḥ pāṃtu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā .. 56 .. ( iti hastimaṃtraḥ ..)
4.138.d:
युद्धे रक्षंतु नागास्त्वां दिशश्च सह दैवतैः ॥
अश्विनौ सह गंधर्वैः पांतु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥ 56 ॥ ( इति हस्तिमंत्रः ॥)
4.138.m: In battle may the elephants and the quarters along with their deities protect you! / May the two Aśvins along with the Gandharvas protect you always on all sides! (Thus the mantra for the elephant.)

4.138.s:
hutabhugvasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ ..
nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣa bhūtagaṇāgrahāḥ .. 57 ..
4.138.d:
हुतभुग्वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः ॥
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयक्ष भूतगणाग्रहाः ॥ 57 ॥
4.138.m: The Fire-god, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Wind-god, Soma, the great seers, / Serpents, kinnaras, gandharvas, yakṣas, and the hosts of ghosts and planets,

4.138.s:
pramathāśca sahādityairbhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha ..
śakrasenāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritāstvayi .. 58 ..
4.138.d:
प्रमथाश्च सहादित्यैर्भूतेशो मातृभिः सह ॥
शक्रसेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितास्त्वयि ॥ 58 ॥
4.138.m: The pramathas together with the Ādityas, the Lord of ghosts together with the Mothers, / Skanda the general of Indra's army, and Varuṇa—all have taken their abode in you.

4.138.s:
pradahaṃtu ripūnsarvānrājā vijayamṛcchatu ..
yāni prayuktānyaribhirdūṣaṇāni samaṃtataḥ .. 59 ..
4.138.d:
प्रदहंतु रिपून्सर्वान्राजा विजयमृच्छतु ॥
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्दूषणानि समंततः ॥ 59 ॥
4.138.m: May they utterly burn all enemies! May the king attain victory! / Whatever malignant spells have been cast by enemies on all sides,

4.138.s:
etāni paraśatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā ..
kālanemivadhe yuddhe yuddhe tripura ghātane .. 4.138.60 ..
4.138.d:
एतानि परशत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा ॥
कालनेमिवधे युद्धे युद्धे त्रिपुर घातने ॥ 4.138.60 ॥
4.138.m: These have been struck down by your brilliance against the enemies! / In the battle for the slaying of Kālanemi, in the battle for the destruction of Tripura,

4.138.s:
hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe yuddhe devāsure tathā ..
śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhamānāstu bhūpateḥ .. 61 ..
4.138.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोर्युद्धे युद्धे देवासुरे तथा ॥
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभमानास्तु भूपतेः ॥ 61 ॥
4.138.m: In the battle of Hiraṇyakaśipu, and likewise in the battle between the gods and asuras, / You were adorned; likewise today, shine forth for the king!

4.138.s:
nīlāṃ śvetāmimāṃ dṛṣṭvā naśyaṃtvadya nṛpārayaḥ ..
vyādhibhirvividhairghoraiḥ śastraiśca yudhi nirjitāḥ .. 62 ..
4.138.d:
नीलां श्वेतामिमां दृष्ट्वा नश्यंत्वद्य नृपारयः ॥
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर्घोरैः शस्त्रैश्च युधि निर्जिताः ॥ 62 ॥
4.138.m: Seeing this dark and white one, may the enemies of the king perish today, / Conquered in combat by dread diverse diseases and by weapons!

4.138.s: sadyaḥ svasthā bhavaṃti sma tvadvātenāpamārjitāḥ .. 63 ..
4.138.d: सद्यः स्वस्था भवंति स्म त्वद्वातेनापमार्जिताः ॥ 63 ॥
4.138.m: They became well at once, swept over by your breeze. 63.

4.138.s:
pūtanā revatī nāmnā kālarātrīti yā smṛtā ..
dahaṃtvāśu ripūnsarvānpatāke tvāmupāgatāḥ .. 64 .. (iti patākāmantraḥ ..)
4.138.d:
पूतना रेवती नाम्ना कालरात्रीति या स्मृता ॥
दहंत्वाशु रिपून्सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपागताः ॥ 64 ॥ (इति पताकामन्त्रः ॥)
4.138.m: Pūtanā, by name Revatī, and she who is remembered as Kālarātrī— / Having approached you, O standard, may they swiftly burn all enemies! (Thus the mantra for the standard.)

4.138.s:
asiśca ripuhā khaḍgastīkṣṇakarmā durāsadaḥ ..
śrīgarbho vijayaścaiva dharmadhārastathaiva ca .. 65 ..
4.138.d:
असिश्च रिपुहा खड्गस्तीक्ष्णकर्मा दुरासदः ॥
श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्मधारस्तथैव च ॥ 65 ॥
4.138.m: Asi (sword), Ripuhā (slayer of foes), Khaḍga (blade), Tīkṣṇakarmā (of sharp action), Durāsada (unassailable), / Śrīgarbha (womb of prosperity), Vijaya (victory), and likewise Dharmadhāra (supporter of righteousness)—

4.138.s:
ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni svayamuktāni vedhasā ..
nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ .. 66 ..
4.138.d:
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि स्वयमुक्तानि वेधसा ॥
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः ॥ 66 ॥
4.138.m: These eight are your names, spoken by the Creator himself. / Your constellation is Kṛttikā, and your guru is the god Maheśvara.

4.138.s:
hiraṇyaṃ ca śarīraṃ te dhātā devo janārdanaḥ ..
pitā pitāmaho devastvaṃ māṃ pālaya sarvadā .. 67 .. (iti khaḍgamantraḥ ..)
4.138.d:
हिरण्यं च शरीरं ते धाता देवो जनार्दनः ॥
पिता पितामहो देवस्त्वं मां पालय सर्वदा ॥ 67 ॥ (इति खड्गमन्त्रः ॥)
4.138.m: Your body is gold, and your creator is the god Janārdana. / You are the father and grandfather of the god; protect me always! (Thus the mantra for the sword.)

4.138.s:
śarmapradastvaṃ samare varma sarvāyaso hyasi ..
rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo'haṃ tava varmannamo'stu te .. 68 .. ( iti varmamantraḥ ..) ..
4.138.d:
शर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे वर्म सर्वायसो ह्यसि ॥
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयोऽहं तव वर्मन्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 68 ॥ ( इति वर्ममन्त्रः ॥) ॥
4.138.m: You bestow comfort in battle, for you are armour made entirely of iron. / Protect me, for I am to be protected by you, O armour! Homage to you! (Thus the mantra for the armour.)

4.138.s:
dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ ghoṣāddhṛdayakampana ..
bhava bhūmipa sainyānāṃ tathā vijayavarddhanaḥ .. 69 ..
4.138.d:
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां घोषाद्धृदयकम्पन ॥
भव भूमिप सैन्यानां तथा विजयवर्द्धनः ॥ 69 ॥
4.138.m: O war drum, you cause the hearts of rivals to tremble with your sound! / Become likewise the enhancer of victory for the armies of the king!

4.138.s:
yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyaṃti varavāraṇāḥ ..
tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo'smākaṃ mudāvahaḥ ..4.138.70..
4.138.d:
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यंति वरवारणाः ॥
तथास्तु तव शब्देन हर्षोऽस्माकं मुदावहः ॥4.138.70॥
4.138.m: Just as excellent elephants rejoice at the thundering of a cloud, / So may our joy, bringing delight, arise at your sound!

4.138.s:
yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso'bhijāyate ..
tathā ca tava śabdena trasyaṃtvasmaddviṣo raṇe..71.. ( iti duṃdubhimaṃtraḥ .. )
4.138.d:
यथा जीमूतशब्देन स्त्रीणां त्रासोऽभिजायते ॥
तथा च तव शब्देन त्रस्यंत्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे॥71॥ ( इति दुंदुभिमंत्रः ॥ )
4.138.m: Just as terror arises in women from the sound of thunder, / Even so may our enemies in battle tremble at your sound! (Thus the mantra for the war drum.)

4.138.s:
sarvāyudha mahāmātra sarvadevārisūdana ..
cāpa māṃ sarvadā rakṣa sākaṃ sāyakasattamaiḥ .. 72.. ( iti cāpamantraḥ..)
4.138.d:
सर्वायुध महामात्र सर्वदेवारिसूदन ॥
चाप मां सर्वदा रक्ष साकं सायकसत्तमैः ॥ 72॥ ( इति चापमन्त्रः॥)
4.138.m: O grand officer among all weapons, slayer of all enemies of the gods! / O bow, protect me always together with the best of arrows! (Thus the mantra for the bow.)

4.138.s:
puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṣpāṇāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam ..
viṣṇunā vidhṛto nityaṃ manaḥśāṃtiprado bhava .. 73 .. ( iti śaṅkhamantraḥ ..)
4.138.d:
पुण्यस्त्वं शङ्ख पुष्पाणां मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ॥
विष्णुना विधृतो नित्यं मनःशांतिप्रदो भव ॥ 73 ॥ ( इति शङ्खमन्त्रः ॥)
4.138.m: You are auspicious, O conch, the flower and the blessing of all blessings! / Held constantly by Viṣṇu, be the bestower of peace of mind! (Thus the mantra for the conch.)

4.138.s:
śaśāṃkakarasaṃkāśa himaḍiṃḍīrapāṃḍura ..
protsārayāśu duritaṃ cāmarāmaravallabha .. 74 .. ( iti cāmaramaṃtraḥ ..)
4.138.d:
शशांककरसंकाश हिमडिंडीरपांडुर ॥
प्रोत्सारयाशु दुरितं चामरामरवल्लभ ॥ 74 ॥ ( इति चामरमंत्रः ॥)
4.138.m: Resembling the rays of the moon, white as snow and sea-foam, / Swiftly drive away misfortune, O chowrie, beloved of the immortals! (Thus the mantra for the chowrie.)

4.138.s:
sarvāyudhānāṃ prathamā nirmitā'si pinākinā ..
śūlāyudhādviniṣkṛṣya kṛtvā muṣṭiparigraham .. 75 ..
4.138.d:
सर्वायुधानां प्रथमा निर्मिताऽसि पिनाकिना ॥
शूलायुधाद्विनिष्कृष्य कृत्वा मुष्टिपरिग्रहम् ॥ 75 ॥
4.138.m: You were fashioned as the foremost of all weapons by the Wielder of Pināka, / Drawing you forth from his trident weapon and making a grip for the fist.

4.138.s:
caṃḍikāyāḥ pradattāsi sarvaduṣṭanibarhiṇi ..
tathā vistāritā cāsi devānāṃ pratipāditā .. 76 ..
4.138.d:
चंडिकायाः प्रदत्तासि सर्वदुष्टनिबर्हिणि ॥
तथा विस्तारिता चासि देवानां प्रतिपादिता ॥ 76 ॥
4.138.m: You were given to Caṇḍikā, O destroyer of all evil ones! / Likewise you were expanded and presented to the gods.

4.138.s:
sarva sattvāṃgabhūtāsi sarvāśubhanivāriṇi ..
churike rakṣa māṃ nityaṃ śāntiṃ yaccha namo'stu te .. 77 .. ( iticchurikāmaṃtraḥ ..)
4.138.d:
सर्व सत्त्वांगभूतासि सर्वाशुभनिवारिणि ॥
छुरिके रक्ष मां नित्यं शान्तिं यच्छ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 77 ॥ ( इतिच्छुरिकामंत्रः ॥)
4.138.m: You constitute a limb of all beings, O warder-off of all inauspiciousness! / O dagger, protect me always, grant peace, homage to you! (Thus the mantra for the dagger.)

4.138.s:
protsāraṇāya duṣṭānāṃ mādhusaṃgrahaṇāya ca ..
brahmaṇā nirmitaścāsi vyavahāraprasiddhaye ..78..
4.138.d:
प्रोत्सारणाय दुष्टानां माधुसंग्रहणाय च ॥
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितश्चासि व्यवहारप्रसिद्धये ॥78॥
4.138.m: For driving away the wicked and for gathering sweetness, / You were fashioned by Brahmā for the establishment of proper conduct.

4.138.s:
yaśo dehi sukhaṃ dehi jayado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
tāḍayāśu ripūnsarvānhemadaṃḍa namostu te .. 79 .. ( iti kanakadaṇḍamantraḥ ..)
4.138.d:
यशो देहि सुखं देहि जयदो भव भूपतेः ॥
ताडयाशु रिपून्सर्वान्हेमदंड नमोस्तु ते ॥ 79 ॥ ( इति कनकदण्डमन्त्रः ॥)
4.138.m: Grant fame, grant happiness, be the bestower of victory to the king! / Strike swiftly all enemies, O golden sceptre, homage to you! (Thus the mantra for the golden sceptre.)

4.138.s:
vijayo jayado jetā ripughātī priyaṃkaraḥ ..
duḥkhahā dharmadaḥ śāṃtaḥ sarvāriṣṭavināśanaḥ ..4.138.80..
4.138.d:
विजयो जयदो जेता रिपुघाती प्रियंकरः ॥
दुःखहा धर्मदः शांतः सर्वारिष्टविनाशनः ॥4.138.80॥
4.138.m: Vijaya (Victorious), Jayada (Giver of victory), Jetā (Conqueror), Ripughātī (Slayer of foes), Priyaṃkara (Doer of pleasant things), / Duḥkhahā (Dispeller of sorrow), Dharmada (Giver of righteousness), Śānta (Peaceful), and Sarvāriṣṭavināśana (Destroyer of all misfortunes)—

4.138.s:
ete'ṣṭau saṃnidhau yasmāttava siṃhā mahābalā....
tena siṃhāsaneti tvaṃ viprairvedeṣu gīyase ..81..
4.138.d:
एतेऽष्टौ संनिधौ यस्मात्तव सिंहा महाबला॥॥
तेन सिंहासनेति त्वं विप्रैर्वेदेषु गीयसे ॥81॥
4.138.m: Because these eight lions of great strength are in your presence, / Therefore you are praised as siṃhāsana (lion-throne) by brāhmaṇas in the Vedas.

4.138.s:
tvayi sthitaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāttvayi śakrasureśvaraḥ..
tvayi sthito harirdevastvadarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ .. 82 ..
4.138.d:
त्वयि स्थितः शिवः साक्षात्त्वयि शक्रसुरेश्वरः॥
त्वयि स्थितो हरिर्देवस्त्वदर्थं तप्यते तपः ॥ 82 ॥
4.138.m: In you stands Śiva directly; in you stands Śakra, lord of the gods. / In you stands god Hari; for your sake asceticism is performed.

4.138.s:
namaste sarvatobhadra bhadrado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
trailokyajayasarvasva siṃhāsana namo'stu te .. 83 .. ( iti siṃhāsanamaṃtra ..)
4.138.d:
नमस्ते सर्वतोभद्र भद्रदो भव भूपतेः ॥
त्रैलोक्यजयसर्वस्व सिंहासन नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 83 ॥ ( इति सिंहासनमंत्र ॥)
4.138.m: Homage to you, Sarvatobhadra; bestow auspiciousness upon the king. / O throne, all-surpassing wealth of conquest over the three worlds, homage be to you! (Thus the mantra of the throne.)

4.138.s:
lohābhihārikaṃ karma kṛtvedaṃ maṃtrapūrvakam..
phalanaivedyakusumairdhūpadīpavilepanaiḥ ..84..
4.138.d:
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कृत्वेदं मंत्रपूर्वकम्॥
फलनैवेद्यकुसुमैर्धूपदीपविलेपनैः ॥84॥
4.138.m: Having performed this iron-lustration rite according to the mantras, / with fruits, food-offerings, flowers, incense, lamps, and ointments,

4.138.s: aṣṭamyāṃ dhāvanaṃ kṛtvā pūrvāhne snānamācaret.. .. 85 ..
4.138.d: अष्टम्यां धावनं कृत्वा पूर्वाह्ने स्नानमाचरेत्॥ ॥ 85 ॥
4.138.m: having cleansed [the teeth] on the aṣṭamī, one should bathe in the morning.

4.138.s:
( atha gadyam)
durgāṃ kāṃcanamūrtiṃ raupyāṃ vā paittalīṃ vārkṣī caitrīṃ tāmrīṃ vādhibhavataḥ kṛtvā dāruvicitratoraṇavinyastāṃ śobhane sthāne purato vinyastadṛṣṭāṃ vicitragṛhamadhyagāṃ snātāṃ kuṃkumacaṃdanagaṃdhaiścatuḥsamaiścīrapaṭṭaiścarcitagātrāṃ devīṃ kusumairabhyarcya tāṃ bahubhiḥ puṣyamāṇakīrtistairdvi jananairjanitaparitoṣairdivānvito naredraḥ svayaṃ prayacchetpurohitaiḥ sārdhaṃ bilvapatreṇārcanena maṃtreṇānena bhagavatyai .. ( iti gadyaṃ sampūrṇaṃ) ..
jayaṃtī maṃgalā kālī bhadrakālī kapālinī ..
durgā śivā kṣamā dhātrī svāhā svadhā namostu te .. 86 ..
4.138.d:
( अथ गद्यम्)
दुर्गां कांचनमूर्तिं रौप्यां वा पैत्तलीं वार्क्षी चैत्रीं ताम्रीं वाधिभवतः कृत्वा दारुविचित्रतोरणविन्यस्तां शोभने स्थाने पुरतो विन्यस्तदृष्टां विचित्रगृहमध्यगां स्नातां कुंकुमचंदनगंधैश्चतुःसमैश्चीरपट्टैश्चर्चितगात्रां देवीं कुसुमैरभ्यर्च्य तां बहुभिः पुष्यमाणकीर्तिस्तैर्द्वि जननैर्जनितपरितोषैर्दिवान्वितो नरेद्रः स्वयं प्रयच्छेत्पुरोहितैः सार्धं बिल्वपत्रेणार्चनेन मंत्रेणानेन भगवत्यै ॥ ( इति गद्यं सम्पूर्णं) ॥
जयंती मंगला काली भद्रकाली कपालिनी ॥
दुर्गा शिवा क्षमा धात्री स्वाहा स्वधा नमोस्तु ते ॥ 86 ॥
4.138.m:
(Now the prose:)
Having made an image of Durgā—either of gold, silver, brass, wood, clay, or copper, according to one's means—placed beneath an archway adorned with wood in a beautiful spot, with eyes looking forward, situated in the centre of a decorated pavilion, bathed, her limbs smeared with saffron, sandalwood paste, fragrant catus-sama unguent, and fine cloth, having worshipped that goddess with flowers, the king himself, accompanied by priests, his fame enhanced by many twice-born men whom he has gladdened by day, should present [an offering] to the goddess with a bilva leaf and worship, with this mantra: (Thus the prose is complete.)
"O Jayantī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, Kapālinī, / Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā, Svadhā, homage be to you!

4.138.s:
amṛtodbhavaḥ śrīvṛkṣo mahādevīpriyaḥ sadā ..
bilvapatraṃ prayacchāmi pavitraṃ te sureśvari .. 87 ..
4.138.d:
अमृतोद्भवः श्रीवृक्षो महादेवीप्रियः सदा ॥
बिल्वपत्रं प्रयच्छामि पवित्रं ते सुरेश्वरि ॥ 87 ॥
4.138.m: Born of ambrosia is the śrīvṛkṣa, ever dear to the Great Goddess. / I offer a pure bilva leaf to you, O queen of the gods!"

4.138.s:
durgā saṃpūjanīyā ca taddināddroṇapuṣpayā ..
sā cābhīṣṭā sureśānyāstathā rūḍhavraṇāyutaḥ ..88..
4.138.d:
दुर्गा संपूजनीया च तद्दिनाद्द्रोणपुष्पया ॥
सा चाभीष्टा सुरेशान्यास्तथा रूढव्रणायुतः ॥88॥
4.138.m: And from that day, Durgā should be worshipped with droṇapuṣpa flowers; / that is dear to the queen of gods, as well as to one afflicted with chronic sores.

4.138.s:
tataḥ khaḍgaṃ namaskṛtya śatrūṇāṃ mānamarddanam..
icchetsvavijayaṃ rājyaṃ subhikṣaṃ cātmano nṛpa .. 89 ..
4.138.d:
ततः खड्गं नमस्कृत्य शत्रूणां मानमर्द्दनम्॥
इच्छेत्स्वविजयं राज्यं सुभिक्षं चात्मनो नृप ॥ 89 ॥
4.138.m: Then, having bowed to the sword that crushes the pride of enemies, / the king should desire his own victory, kingdom, and plenty.

4.138.s:
punaḥ punaḥ praṇamyātha dhyāyecca hṛdaye śivām ..
mahiṣaghnīṃ bahubhujāṃ kumārīṃ siṃhavāhinīm .. 4.138.90 ..
4.138.d:
पुनः पुनः प्रणम्याथ ध्यायेच्च हृदये शिवाम् ॥
महिषघ्नीं बहुभुजां कुमारीं सिंहवाहिनीम् ॥ 4.138.90 ॥
4.138.m: Having bowed again and again, he should meditate in his heart upon Śivā, / the slayer of Mahiṣa, many-armed, the maiden who rides a lion,

4.138.s:
dānavāṃstarjayatī ca khaḍgoddhatakarāṃ śubhām ..
ghaṃṭākṣasragdharāṃ durgāṃ raṇāraṃbhe vyavasthitām .. 91 ..
4.138.d:
दानवांस्तर्जयती च खड्गोद्धतकरां शुभाम् ॥
घंटाक्षस्रग्धरां दुर्गां रणारंभे व्यवस्थिताम् ॥ 91 ॥
4.138.m: threatening the Dānavas, her hand raised with a sword, auspicious, / holding a bell and an akṣa rosary, Durgā standing at the onset of battle.

4.138.s: tato jayajayākāraiḥ stavaṃ kuryādimaṃ tataḥ .. 92..
4.138.d: ततो जयजयाकारैः स्तवं कुर्यादिमं ततः ॥ 92॥
4.138.m: Then, with shouts of "Victory! Victory!", he should recite this hymn:

4.138.s:
sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye śive sarvārthasādhike ..
śaraṇye tryaṃbake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te .. 93 ..
4.138.d:
सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके ॥
शरण्ये त्र्यंबके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 93 ॥
4.138.m: "O most auspicious of all auspicious things, O Śivā, achiever of all goals, / O refuge, three-eyed Gauri, Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you!

4.138.s:
kuṃkumena samālabdhe candanena vilepite ..
bilvapatrakṛtāmāle durge'haṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ..94..
4.138.d:
कुंकुमेन समालब्धे चन्दनेन विलेपिते ॥
बिल्वपत्रकृतामाले दुर्गेऽहं शरणं गतः ॥94॥
4.138.m: Smeared with saffron, anointed with sandalwood paste, / garlanded with bilva leaves, O Durgā, I have taken refuge [in you]!"

4.138.s:
kṛtvaivamarccāṃ kauravya aṣṭamyāṃ jāgaraṃ niśi ..
naṭanartanagītaiśca kārayettu mahotsavam ..95..
4.138.d:
कृत्वैवमर्च्चां कौरव्य अष्टम्यां जागरं निशि ॥
नटनर्तनगीतैश्च कारयेत्तु महोत्सवम् ॥95॥
4.138.m: Having thus performed worship, O Kaurava, one should keep vigil at night on the aṣṭamī / and hold a great festival with actors, dancing, and songs.

4.138.s:
evaṃ hṛṣṭairniśāṃ nītvā prabhāte cāruṇodaye ..
pātayenmahiṣānmeṣānagrato natakandharān ..96..
4.138.d:
एवं हृष्टैर्निशां नीत्वा प्रभाते चारुणोदये ॥
पातयेन्महिषान्मेषानग्रतो नतकन्धरान् ॥96॥
4.138.m: Having thus passed the night with rejoicings, at dawn at the rising of the red sun, / he should fell buffalos and rams, their necks bent down before [her].

4.138.s:
śataṃ cāpi śatārdhaṃ vā tadarddhaṃ vā yathecchayā ..
surāsavabhṛtaiḥ kuṃbhaistarpayetparameśvarīm .. 97 ..
4.138.d:
शतं चापि शतार्धं वा तदर्द्धं वा यथेच्छया ॥
सुरासवभृतैः कुंभैस्तर्पयेत्परमेश्वरीम् ॥ 97 ॥
4.138.m: A hundred, or fifty, or twenty-five, according to his wish, / with jars filled with spirituous liquor he should gratify Parameśvarī.

4.138.s:
kāpālikebhyastaddeyaṃ dāsīdāsajanaistathā ..
vibhajya sarvaṃ kauṃteya suhṛtsaṃbaṃdhibaṃdhuṣu ..98..
4.138.d:
कापालिकेभ्यस्तद्देयं दासीदासजनैस्तथा ॥
विभज्य सर्वं कौंतेय सुहृत्संबंधिबंधुषु ॥98॥
4.138.m: That should be given to the Kāpālikas, and likewise by female and male servants; / having distributed everything, O son of Kuntī, among friends, relatives, and kinsmen,

4.138.s:
tatoparāhṇasamaye navamyāṃ syaṃdane sthitām ..
bhavānīṃ bhrāmayedrāṣṭre svayaṃ rājā sasainyavān ..99..
4.138.d:
ततोपराह्णसमये नवम्यां स्यंदने स्थिताम् ॥
भवानीं भ्रामयेद्राष्ट्रे स्वयं राजा ससैन्यवान् ॥99॥
4.138.m: then in the afternoon on the navamī, the king himself, accompanied by his army, / should conduct Bhavānī, mounted on a chariot, on a procession through the realm,

4.138.s:
sahasraiḥ puruṣairvāpi rathayuktaiḥ suśikṣitaiḥ ..
śanaiḥ śanairadhikayā dīptyā prajvaladīpakaiḥ ..4.138.100..
4.138.d:
सहस्रैः पुरुषैर्वापि रथयुक्तैः सुशिक्षितैः ॥
शनैः शनैरधिकया दीप्त्या प्रज्वलदीपकैः ॥4.138.100॥
4.138.m: either drawn by thousands of men or harnessed with well-trained chariot-horses, / slowly, with brilliant luster from blazing lamps,

4.138.s:
ākṛṣṭakhaḍgairvīraiśca dhāturaktairgajaistathā ..
nadadbhiḥ śaṃkhapaṭahairnṛtyadbhi rvārayauvataiḥ ..
alaṃkṛtābhirnārībhirbālakaiḥ suvibhūṣitaiḥ ..101..
4.138.d:
आकृष्टखड्गैर्वीरैश्च धातुरक्तैर्गजैस्तथा ॥

येन विघ्ना न जायंते यात्रा संपूर्णतां व्रजेत्॥1 09॥
एवं ये कुर्वते यात्रां राजानोऽन्येऽपि मानवाः॥
महानवम्यां नंदायां पुत्रका हृष्टमानसाः ॥4.138.11 0॥
ते सर्वे पापनिर्मुक्ता यांति भागवतीं पुरीम् ॥1 11॥
4.138.m:
the śākinīs, the yakṣas and vetālas, the yoginīs, the pūtanās, the jackals, / the Jṛmbhakas, the Siddhas and Gandharvas, the snakes, the Vidyādharas, the earth-dwellers,
the guardians of the directions, the world protectors, and those who are obstacle-making vināyakas, / the peacemakers of the worlds, and the great sages beginning with Brahmā!
May my sins be pacified along with obstacles, O adversaries! / Gratified, may the ghosts and pretas become gentle and bring happiness!"
In this manner he should take goddess Durgā on a procession through the realm mounted on a chariot, / or in a palanquin, O Pārtha; then he should conclude it without obstacle.
Then, among the Brahmins who are present, he should perform the pacification of spirits, / by which obstacles do not arise, and the procession attains completion.
Those kings and other men who thus perform the procession / on Mahānavamī, the Nandā tithi, O son, with joyful hearts,
they all, freed from sin, go to the city of the Goddess.

4.138.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Mahānavamī Vrata', in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira, in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa. 138
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / The sacred Mahānavamī is the most excellent of lunar days; / it should be observed by all gods, and especially by rulers of subjects.
You should inaugurate it, O Pārtha, for the welfare of the year, / and for the pleasure of ghosts, pretas, and piśācas, or as a festival.
Yudhiṣṭhira said: / From what time did this navamī bearing the word "mahā" begin? / From what beginning, O Lord, did the ritual of the navamī arise?
Does this procession proceed from the birth from Yaśodā's womb, / or did it exist previously, in the Kṛta and Tretā yugas and so forth?
Since on this [day] some people respect living beings and [others] slaughter them, / what is the post-mortem destiny of those creatures who are killed?
[and] for those who kill them themselves, cause them to be killed, or consent to it.
You ought first, Keśava, to tell me [the answer to] this doubt of mine.

॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पार्थ या परमा शक्तिरनंता लोकविश्रुता ॥
आद्या सर्वगता शुद्धा भाव गम्या मनोहरा ॥ 7 ॥
आद्याष्टमी कलाकाली द्वितीया सर्वमंगला ॥
माया कात्यायनी दुर्गा चामुंडा शंकरप्रिया ॥ 8 ॥
ध्यायंति यां योगरतां सा देवी परमेश्वरी ॥
रूपभेदैर्नामभेदैर्भवानी पूज्यते शिवा॥9॥
अष्टम्यां तु नवम्यां तु देवदानवराक्षसैः॥
गंधर्वैरुरगैर्यज्ञैः पूज्यते किन्नरैर्नरैः॥10॥
अन्येष्वपि युगेष्वादौ सृष्टेः पूर्वं प्रदर्शिता॥
पूज्यतेयं पुरा देवी तेभ्यः पूर्वतरैः शुभैः॥11॥
आश्वयुक्शुक्लपक्षे च याष्टमी मूल संयुता ॥
सा महानवमी नाम त्रैलोक्येऽपि सुदुर्लभा ॥ 12 ॥
कन्यागते सवितरि शुक्लपक्षेऽष्टमी तु या ॥
मूलनक्षत्रसंयुक्ता सा महानवमी स्मृता ॥ 13 ॥
4.138.m:
The Blessed Kṛṣṇa said:
O Pārtha, that supreme power is infinite and renowned throughout the worlds;
primordial, all-pervading, pure, reachable through devotion, and captivating.
She is Ādyāṣṭamī, Kalākālī, the second is Sarvamaṅgalā,
Māyā, Kātyāyanī, Durgā, Cāmuṇḍā, beloved of Śaṅkara.
She upon whom those intent on yoga meditate is that goddess, Parameśvarī;
under different forms and different names, Bhavānī, Śivā, is worshipped.
On the aṣṭamī and on the navamī she is worshipped by gods, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas,
by Gandharvas, serpents, Yakṣas, Kinnaras, and men.
In other ages also, revealed in the beginning before creation,
this goddess was worshipped in ancient times by those auspicious beings who came before them.
And in the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja, the aṣṭamī that is joined with Mūla—
that is called Mahānavamī, exceedingly difficult to obtain even in the three worlds.
When the sun has entered Virgo, the aṣṭamī in the bright fortnight
joined with the asterism Mūla is known as Mahānavamī.

अष्टम्यां च नवम्यां च जगन्मातरमम्बिकाम् ॥
पूजयित्वा'ऽश्विने मासि विशोको जयति द्विषः ॥ 14 ॥
संतर्जयंती हुंकारैः खड्गादिभिरहर्निशम् ॥
नवम्यां पूजिता देवी ददाति नवमं फलम् ॥ 15 ॥
सा पुण्या सा पवित्रा च सा धर्मसुखदायिनी ॥
तस्मात्सदा पूजनीया चामुंडा मुंडमालिनी ॥ 16 ॥
तस्यां यद्युपयुज्यंते प्राणिनो महिषादयः ॥
सर्वे ते स्वर्गतिं यांति घ्नतां पापं न विद्यते ॥ 17 ॥
न तथा बलिदानेन पुष्पधूपविलेपनैः ॥
यथा संतुष्यते लोके महिषैर्विंध्यवासिनी ॥ 18 ॥
उद्दिश्य दुर्गां हन्यंते विधानाद्येऽत्र जंतवः ॥
स्वर्गं ते यांति कौंतेय घातयंतोऽपि भक्तिः ॥ 19 ॥
भवानीप्राङ्गणे प्राणा येषां याता युधिष्ठिर ॥
तेषां स्वर्गे ध्रुवं वासो वरास्तेऽप्यरसां प्रियाः ॥ 20 ॥
4.138.m:
Having worshipped Ambikā, the mother of the universe, on the aṣṭamī and on the navamī
in the month of Āśvina, one conquers one’s foes free from sorrow.
Terrifying [enemies] day and night with hum-cries, swords, and the like,
the goddess, when worshipped on the navamī, grants the ninth fruit.
She is meritorious, she is pure, she is the giver of virtue and happiness;
therefore Cāmuṇḍā, garlanded with severed heads, is ever to be worshipped.
If on that day living beings such as buffaloes are employed [in sacrifice],
they all attain heaven, and no sin accrues to those who kill them.
Not by animal sacrifice [of other kinds], nor by flowers, incense, or unguents,
is Vindhyavāsinī so pleased in the world as she is by buffaloes.
Creatures here that are slaughtered according to the prescribed rule for the sake of Durgā—
they go to heaven, O son of Kuntī, and those who cause them to be killed [attain it] through devotion.
Those whose lives depart in the courtyard of Bhavānī, O Yudhiṣṭhira,
their dwelling is surely in heaven; they become excellent suitors beloved of the Apsarases.

4.138.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु कल्पेषु कुरुनदन ॥
तेषु सर्वेषु चैवासन्नवमीयं पुरार्चिता ॥ 21 ॥
प्रसिद्धानादिनिधना वर्षेवर्षे युधिष्ठिर ॥
भूयोभूयोऽवतारैश्च भवानीपूज्य तेसुरैः ॥ 22 ॥
अवतीर्णा भुवि सदा नित्यं दैत्यनिबर्हिणी ॥
स्वर्गपातालमर्त्येषु करोति स्थितिपालनम् ॥ 23 ॥
पुनश्चैषा महादेवी यशोदा गर्भसंभवा ॥
कंसासुरस्योत्तमाङ्गे पादं दत्त्वा गतायुषः ॥ 24 ॥
ततः प्रभृति लोकेषु यशोदानंददायिनीम् ॥
विंध्याचले स्थापयित्वा पुनः पूजा प्रवर्तिता ॥ 25 ॥
पूर्वप्रवृद्धोऽपि पुनर्भगिन्या महिमा कृतः ॥
भुवि सर्वोपकाराय सर्वोपद्रवशांतये ॥ 26 ॥
एवं विंध्योपवासिन्या नवरात्रोपवासिनः ॥
एकरात्रेण नक्तेन स्वशक्त्याऽयाचितेन वा ॥ 27 ॥
यजनैर्याजनैर्देवाः स्थानेस्थाने पुरेपुरे ॥
गृहेगृहे भक्तिपरे र्ग्रामेग्रामे वनेवने ॥ 28 ॥
4.138.m:
In all the Manvantaras and in all the Kalpas, O son of the Kurus—
in all of them this navamī was indeed worshipped in ancient times.
Renowned, without beginning or end, year after year, O Yudhiṣṭhira,
Bhavānī is worshipped again and again by the gods through her incarnations.
Ever descending to earth, perpetually destroying the Daityas,
she maintains order in heaven, the netherworld, and the realm of mortals.
And once again this great goddess was born from the womb of Yaśodā;
placing her foot upon the head of the demon Kaṃsa, whose life had run out,
from that time forth, having installed in the Vindhya mountains her who gives joy to Yaśodā,
her worship was once more set in motion among the worlds.
Though already great in the past, her majesty was once more manifested as [my] sister
for the benefit of all on earth and for the appeasement of all afflictions.
Thus, fasting for nine nights for the dweller of the Vindhya mountains,
[or] with a single night, a nocturnal meal, or unsolicited food according to one’s capacity,
the gods [are worshipped] by sacrifices and priestly rites in every place, every city,
every house devoted to piety, every village, and every forest,

4.138.d:
स्नातैः प्रमुदितैर्हृष्टैर्ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्नृपैः ॥
वैश्यैः शूद्रैर्भक्तिचित्रैर्म्लेच्छैरन्यैश्च मानवैः ॥ 29 ॥
स्त्रीभिश्च कुरुशार्दूल तद्विधानमिदं शृणु ॥
जयाभिलाषी नृपतिः प्रतिपत्प्रभृतिक्रमात् ॥ 30 ॥
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कारयेद्यावदष्टमि ॥
प्रागुदक्प्रवणे देशे पताकाभिरलंकृतम् ॥ 31 ॥
मण्डपं कारयेद्दिव्यं नवसप्तकरं वरम् ॥
आग्नेय्यां कारयेत्कुण्डं हस्तमात्रं सुशोभनम् ॥ 32 ॥
मेखलात्रयसं युक्तं योन्यश्वत्थदलाभया ॥
राजचिह्नानि सर्वाणि शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि यानि च ॥ 33 ॥
आनीय मण्डपे तानि सर्वाण्येवाधिवासयेत् ॥
ततस्तु ब्राह्मणः स्नातः शुक्लांबरधरः शुचिः॥ 34 ॥
ओंकारपूर्वकैर्मन्त्रैस्तल्लिंगैर्जुहुयाद्घृतम्॥
लोहनामाभवत्पूर्वं दानवस्तु महाबलः ॥ 35 ॥
4.138.m:
by brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, kings, vaiśyas, and śūdras, bathed, joyful, and glad,
by mlecchas varied in devotion, and by other men,
and by women, O tiger of the Kurus. Hear this procedure for it:
a king desiring victory, beginning with the first day in proper order,
should have the iron-lustration rite performed up until the aṣṭamī.
On a ground sloping towards the north-east, adorned with banners,
he should have a celestial pavilion made, measuring nine by seven cubits, [which is] excellent;
in the south-east he should have a very beautiful sacrificial pit made, measuring one cubit,
endowed with three terraces, shaped like a vulva and a leaf of the holy fig tree.
All the insignia of royalty, and whatever weapons and missiles there are,
having brought them all into the pavilion, he should consecrate them.
Then a brāhmaṇa, bathed, clad in white garments, and pure,
should offer clarified butter with mantras preceded by the syllable Oṃ and bearing their characteristic marks. (35cd)
Formerly there was an exceedingly powerful dānava named Loha. (36ab)

4.138.s:
sa devaiḥ samare kruddhairbahudhā śakalīkṛtaḥ ..
tadaṃgasambhavaṃ lohaṃ yatsarvaṃdṛśyate kṣitau .. 36 ..
śastrāstramantrairhotavyaṃ pāyasaṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam ..
hutaśeṣaṃ turaṃgāṇāṃ gajānāmupahārayet .. 37 ..

4.138.d:
स देवैः समरे क्रुद्धैर्बहुधा शकलीकृतः ॥
तदंगसम्भवं लोहं यत्सर्वंदृश्यते क्षितौ ॥ 36 ॥
शस्त्रास्त्रमन्त्रैर्होतव्यं पायसं घृतसंयुतम् ॥
हुतशेषं तुरंगाणां गजानामुपहारयेत् ॥ 37 ॥
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म तेनैतदृषिभिः स्मृतम् ॥
बद्धप्रतिशरव्यं च गजाश्वसमलंकृतम् ॥ 38 ॥
भ्रामयेन्नगरे नित्यं नंदि घोषपुरस्सरम्॥
प्रत्यहं नृपतिः स्नात्वा संपूज्य पितृदेवताः ॥ 39 ॥
पूजयेद्राजचिह्नानि फलमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥
हुतशेषं प्रदातव्यमौपनायनिके द्विजे ॥ 40 ॥
तस्याभिहरणाद्राज्ञो विजयः समुदाहृतः ॥
पूजामंत्रान्प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणोक्तानहं तव ॥ 41 ॥
यैः पूजिताः प्रयच्छन्ति कीर्तिमायु र्यशोबलम॥
यथांबुदश्छादयति शिवायेमां वसुन्धराम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.138.m:
He was cut into many pieces by the gods enraged in battle;
all the iron that is seen on earth was born from his body.
Rice-milk mixed with ghee should be offered into the fire with mantras for weapons and missiles;
the residue of the oblation should be presented to the horses and elephants.
Because of that, this rite was remembered by the sages as the iron-lustration rite.
Having bound an effigy of the target, adorned with elephants and horses,
he should parade it daily around the city, preceded by joyous shouts.
Every day the king, having bathed and worshipped the ancestors and deities,
should worship the insignia of royalty with fruits, garlands, and unguents.
The residue of the oblation should be given to an initiated twice-born man.
Victory for the king is proclaimed to come from its taking away.
I shall tell you the worship-mantras taught in the Purāṇas,
worshipped with which they bestow renown, longevity, fame, and strength:
Just as a cloud covers this earth for its welfare,

4.138.d:
तथाच्छादय राजानं विजयारोग्यवृद्धये ॥ ( इति छत्रमन्त्रः) ॥
गन्धर्व कुलजातस्त्वं माभूयाः कुलदूषकः ॥ 43 ॥
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च ॥
प्रभावाञ्च हुताशस्य वर्द्धस्व त्वं तुरंगम ॥ 44 ॥
तेजसा चैव सूर्यस्य मुनीनां तपसा यथा ॥
रुद्रस्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पवनस्य वलेन च॥ स्मृ ॥
स्मर त्वं राजपुत्रोऽसि कौस्तुभं च मणिं स्मर ॥
यां गतिं ब्रह्महा गच्छेत्पितृहा मातृहा तथा ॥ 46 ॥
भूम्यर्थेनृतवादी च क्षत्रियश्च पराङ्मुखः ॥
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुः पावकश्च न यत्र वै ॥ 47॥
व्रजेच्च तां गतिं क्षिप्रं तच्च पापं भवेत्किल ॥
विकृतिं यदि गच्छेस्त्वं युद्धेध्वनि तुरंगम ॥
रिपून्विजित्य समरे सह भर्त्रा सुखी भव ॥ 48 ॥॥ ॥ ( इत्यश्वमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
4.138.m:
so cover the king for the increase of victory and health. (Thus the parasol-mantra.)
You are born from the lineage of Gandharvas; do not be a defiler of your race.
By the truthful word of Brahmā, of Soma, and of Varuṇa,
and by the power of Agni, grow strong, O horse!
And by the splendour of the sun, as well as by the ascetic heat of the sages,
by the celibacy of Rudra, and by the strength of the wind—
Remember you are a prince, and remember the Kaustubha jewel.
The state to which a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, a slayer of a father, or a slayer of a mother would go,
as well as one who speaks falsely for the sake of land, and a kṣatriya who turns his back [in battle],
where indeed the sun and moon, the wind, and the sacred fire are not,
to that state may you go quickly, and that sin would surely be yours,
if you should become unruly in battle upon the road, O horse!
Having conquered the foes in battle, be happy together with your master! (Thus the horse-mantra.)

4.138.d:
शक्रकेतो महावीर्य सुपर्णस्त्वय्युपस्थितः ॥
पतत्रिराड्वैनतेयस्तथा नारायणध्वजः ॥ 49 ॥
काश्यपेयोऽमृतो ज्ञेयो नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः ॥
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो देवशत्रुनिषूदनः ॥ 50 ॥
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिस्त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः ॥
शस्त्रवर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षास्मांश्च रिपून्दह ॥ 51 ॥ ॥ (इति ध्वजमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदंतोऽथ वामनः ॥
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नील एतेऽष्टौ देवयोनयः ॥॥ 52 ॥
एतेषां पुत्रपौत्राश्च बलान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः ॥
भद्रो मन्द्रो मृगश्चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च ॥
वनेवने प्रसूतास्ते करियोनिं महागजाः॥53॥
पातु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः ॥
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयं प्रतिपालयन् ॥ 54 ॥
4.138.m:
O banner of Indra of great valour, the Fair-winged One is present on you,
the king of birds, son of Vinatā, and the emblem of Nārāyaṇa.
He should be known as the son of Kaśyapa, immortal, enemy of serpents, mount of Viṣṇu,
immeasurable, unassailable, and the destroyer of the enemies of the gods.
Garutmān, who moves as swift as the wind, is stationed close within you. / Protect the weapons, armour, arms, and warriors, protect us, and burn the enemies! (Thus the banner mantra.)
Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla: these are the eight of divine origin.
And their sons and grandsons have resorted to eight armies: / the bhadra, the mandra, the mṛga, the gaja, and the saṃkīrṇa. / Born in forest after forest, these great elephants belong to the elephant species.
May the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas along with the hosts of Maruts protect you! / Protect your master, lord of elephants, observing the pledge!

4.138.d:
अवापुर्हि जयं युद्धे गमने स्वस्ति नो व्रज ॥
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवोनिलात् ॥
स्थैर्यं मेरोर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात्पुरंदरात् ॥ 55 ॥
युद्धे रक्षंतु नागास्त्वां दिशश्च सह दैवतैः ॥
अश्विनौ सह गंधर्वैः पांतु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥ 56 ॥ ( इति हस्तिमंत्रः ॥)
हुतभुग्वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः ॥
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयक्ष भूतगणाग्रहाः ॥ 57 ॥
प्रमथाश्च सहादित्यैर्भूतेशो मातृभिः सह ॥
शक्रसेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितास्त्वयि ॥ 58 ॥
प्रदहंतु रिपून्सर्वान्राजा विजयमृच्छतु ॥
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्दूषणानि समंततः ॥ 59 ॥
एतानि परशत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा ॥
कालनेमिवधे युद्धे युद्धे त्रिपुरघातने ॥ 60 ॥
हिरण्यकशिपोर्युद्धे युद्धे देवासुरे तथा ॥
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभमानास्तु भूपतेः ॥ 61 ॥
4.138.m:
Indeed, they obtained victory in battle; on our departure, go with good fortune! / May your splendour come from Soma, your strength from Viṣṇu, your radiance from Sūrya, your speed from Vāyu, / your stability from Meru, your victory from Rudra, and your renown from the divine Puraṃdara!
May the elephants and the directions along with the deities protect you in battle! / May the two Aśvins along with the Gandharvas protect you on all sides at all times! (Thus the elephant mantra.)
The Fire-eater, the Vasus, the Rudras, Vāyu, Soma, the great sages, / nāgas, kinnaras, gandharvas, yakṣas, hosts of bhūtas, and the planets,
and the pramathas along with the Ādityas, the Lord of Bhūtas with the Mothers, / Indra’s army commander Skanda, and Varuṇa have taken refuge in you.
May they burn all enemies, and may the king obtain victory! / Whatever flaws have been employed on all sides by the enemies,
these of the foreign foes are struck down by your splendour! / In the battle at the slaying of Kālanemi, in the battle at the destruction of Tripura,
in the battle with Hiraṇyakaśipu, and likewise in the battle between gods and asuras, / you were adorned; even so, shining now, [stand] for the king!

4.138.s:
nīlāṃ śvetāmimāṃ dṛṣṭvā naśyaṃtvadya nṛpārayaḥ ..
vyādhibhirvividhairghoraiḥ śastraiśca yudhi nirjitāḥ .. 62 ..
sadyaḥ svasthā bhavaṃti sma tvadvātenāpamārjitāḥ .. 63 ..
pūtanā revatī nāmnā kālarātrīti yā smṛtā ..
dahaṃtvāśu ripūnsarvānpatāke tvāmupāgatāḥ .. 64 .. (iti patākāmantraḥ ..)
asiśca ripuhā khaḍgastīkṣṇakarmā durāsadaḥ ..
śrīgarbho vijayaścaiva dharmadhārastathaiva ca .. 69 ..
ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni svayamuktāni vedhasā ..
nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ .. 66 ..
hiraṇyaṃ ca śarīraṃte dhātā devojanārdanaḥ ..
pitā pitāmaho devastvaṃ māṃ pālaya sarvadā .. 67 .. (iti khaḍgamantraḥ ..)
śarmapradastvaṃ samare varma sarvāyaso hyasi ..
rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo'haṃ tava varmannamo'stu te .. 68 .. ( iti varmamantraḥ ..) ..
4.138.d:
नीलां श्वेतामिमां दृष्ट्वा नश्यंत्वद्य नृपारयः ॥
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर्घोरैः शस्त्रैश्च युधि निर्जिताः ॥ 62 ॥
सद्यः स्वस्था भवंति स्म त्वद्वातेनापमार्जिताः ॥ 63 ॥
पूतना रेवती नाम्ना कालरात्रीति या स्मृता ॥
दहंत्वाशु रिपून्सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपागताः ॥ 64 ॥ (इति पताकामन्त्रः ॥)
असिश्च रिपुहा खड्गस्तीक्ष्णकर्मा दुरासदः ॥
श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्मधारस्तथैव च ॥ 69 ॥
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि स्वयमुक्तानि वेधसा ॥
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः ॥ 66 ॥
हिरण्यं च शरीरंते धाता देवोजनार्दनः ॥
पिता पितामहो देवस्त्वं मां पालय सर्वदा ॥ 67 ॥ (इति खड्गमन्त्रः ॥)
शर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे वर्म सर्वायसो ह्यसि ॥
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयोऽहं तव वर्मन्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 68 ॥ ( इति वर्ममन्त्रः ॥) ॥
4.138.m:
Having seen this blue and white [flag], may the king’s enemies perish today, / struck down in battle by dreadful various diseases and by weapons!
They became well at once, swept over by your breeze. 63.
May those who are called Pūtanā, Revatī, and Kālarātrī, / who have approached you, O flag, swiftly burn all enemies! (Thus the flag mantra.)
Asi, foe-destroyer, khaḍga, performer of sharp deeds, unassailable, / Śrīgarbha, Vijaya, and likewise Dharmadhāra:
thus are your eight names spoken by the Creator himself. / Your nakṣatra is Kṛttikā, and your guru is the god Maheśvara.
Gold is your body, your creator is the god Janārdana, / the divine Grandfather is your father; protect me at all times! (Thus the sword mantra.)
You confer safety in battle, for you are armour made entirely of iron. / Protect me, I am to be protected by you, O armour! Homage to you! (Thus the armour mantra.)

4.138.s:
dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ .ghoṣāddhṛdayakampan ..
bhava bhūmipa sainyānāṃ tathā vijayavarddhanaḥ .. 69 ..
yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyaṃti varavāraṇāḥ ..
tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo'smākaṃ mudāvahaḥ ..70..
yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso'bhijāyate ..
tathā ca tava śabdena trasyaṃtvasmaddviṣo raṇe..71..( iti duṃdubhimaṃtraḥ ..)
sarvāyudha mahāmātra sarvadevārisūdana ..
cāpa māṃ sarvadā rakṣa sākaṃ sāyakasattamaiḥ .. 72.. ( iti cāpamantraḥ..)
puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṣpāṇāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam ..
viṣṇunā vidhṛto nityaṃ manaḥśāṃtiprado bhava .. 73 .. ( iti śaṅkhamantraḥ ..)
śaśāṃkakarasaṃkāśa hima ḍiṃḍīrapāṃḍura ..
protsārayāśu duritaṃ cāmarāmaravallabha .. 74 .. ( iti cāmaramaṃtraḥ ..)
sarvāyudhānāṃ prathamā nirmitā'si pinākinā ..
śūlāyudhādviniṣkṛṣya kṛtvā muṣṭiparigraham .. 75 ..
4.138.d:
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां ।घोषाद्धृदयकम्पन् ॥
भव भूमिप सैन्यानां तथा विजयवर्द्धनः ॥ 69 ॥
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यंति वरवारणाः ॥
तथास्तु तव शब्देन हर्षोऽस्माकं मुदावहः ॥70॥
यथा जीमूतशब्देन स्त्रीणां त्रासोऽभिजायते ॥
तथा च तव शब्देन त्रस्यंत्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे॥71॥( इति दुंदुभिमंत्रः ॥)
सर्वायुध महामात्र सर्वदेवारिसूदन ॥
चाप मां सर्वदा रक्ष साकं सायकसत्तमैः ॥ 72॥ ( इति चापमन्त्रः॥)
पुण्यस्त्वं शङ्ख पुष्पाणां मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ॥
विष्णुना विधृतो नित्यं मनःशांतिप्रदो भव ॥ 73 ॥ ( इति शङ्खमन्त्रः ॥)
शशांककरसंकाश हिम डिंडीरपांडुर ॥
प्रोत्सारयाशु दुरितं चामरामरवल्लभ ॥ 74 ॥ ( इति चामरमंत्रः ॥)
सर्वायुधानां प्रथमा निर्मिताऽसि पिनाकिना ॥
शूलायुधाद्विनिष्कृष्य कृत्वा मुष्टिपरिग्रहम् ॥ 75 ॥
4.138.m:
O dundubhi, causing the hearts of rivals to tremble with your sound, / become the enhancer of victory for the armies of the king!
Just as excellent elephants rejoice at the rumble of a raincloud, / even so may our joy be delighted with your sound!
Just as terror arises in women through the rumble of a raincloud, / even so, by your sound, may our enemies tremble in battle! (Thus the war drum mantra.)
High minister of all weapons, slayer of all enemies of the gods, / O cāpa, protect me at all times along with the best arrows! (Thus the bow mantra.)
You are holy, O śaṅkha, the auspicious of auspicious things, / always held by Viṣṇu: be the bestower of peace of mind! (Thus the conch mantra.)
Resembling moonbeams, white like snow and sea-foam, / drive away evil swiftly, O cāmara, beloved of the immortals! (Thus the chowrie mantra.)
You were created as the first among all weapons by the Wielder of Pināka, / having drawn you forth from the trident weapon and made a hilt-grip.

4.138.s:
caṃḍikāyāḥ pradattāsi sarvaduṣṭanibarhiṇi ..
tathā vistāritā cāsi devānāṃ pratipāditā .. 76 ..
sarva sattvāṃgabhūtāsi
sarvāśubhanivāriṇi ..
churike rakṣa māṃ nityaṃ śāntiṃ yaccha namo'stu te .. 77 .. ( iticchūrikāmaṃtraḥ ..)
protsāraṇāya duṣṭānāṃ sādhusaṃgrahaṇāya ca ..
brahmaṇā nirmitaścāsi vyavahāraprasiddhaye ..78..
yaśo dehi sukhaṃ dehi jagado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
tāḍayāśu ripūnsarvānhemadaṃḍa namostu te .. 70 .. ( iti kanakadaṇḍamantraḥ ..)
vijayo jayado jetā ripughātī priyaṃkaraḥ ..
duḥkhahā dharmadaḥ śāṃtaḥ sarvāriṣṭavināśanaḥ ..80..
ete'ṣṭausaṃnidhau yasmāttava siṃhā mahābalāḥ...
tena siṃhāsaneti tvaṃ viprairvedeṣu gīyase ..81..
tvayi sthitaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāttvayi śakraḥ sureśvaraḥ..
tvayi sthito harirdevastvadarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ .. 82 ..
4.138.d:
चंडिकायाः प्रदत्तासि सर्वदुष्टनिबर्हिणि ॥
तथा विस्तारिता चासि देवानां प्रतिपादिता ॥ 76 ॥
सर्व सत्त्वांगभूतासि
सर्वाशुभनिवारिणि ॥
छुरिके रक्ष मां नित्यं शान्तिं यच्छ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 77 ॥ ( इतिच्छूरिकामंत्रः ॥)
प्रोत्सारणाय दुष्टानां साधुसंग्रहणाय च ॥
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितश्चासि व्यवहारप्रसिद्धये ॥78॥
यशो देहि सुखं देहि जगदो भव भूपतेः ॥
ताडयाशु रिपून्सर्वान्हेमदंड नमोस्तु ते ॥ 70 ॥ ( इति कनकदण्डमन्त्रः ॥)
विजयो जयदो जेता रिपुघाती प्रियंकरः ॥
दुःखहा धर्मदः शांतः सर्वारिष्टविनाशनः ॥80॥
एतेऽष्टौसंनिधौ यस्मात्तव सिंहा महाबलाः॥।
तेन सिंहासनेति त्वं विप्रैर्वेदेषु गीयसे ॥81॥
त्वयि स्थितः शिवः साक्षात्त्वयि शक्रः सुरेश्वरः॥
त्वयि स्थितो हरिर्देवस्त्वदर्थं तप्यते तपः ॥ 82 ॥
4.138.m:
You were given to Caṇḍikā, O destroyer of all evil ones! / Likewise, you were expanded and presented to the gods.
You have become a part of the bodies of all beings, / O dispeller of all inauspiciousness! / O dagger, protect me perpetually and grant peace! Homage to you! 77. (Thus the dagger mantra.)
For driving away the wicked and for gathering the virtuous, / you were created by Brahmā for the accomplishment of worldly administration.
Grant fame, grant happiness, be the preserver of the earth for the king! / Strike swiftly all enemies, O golden sceptre, homage to you! (Thus the golden sceptre mantra.)
Victorious, victory-bestowing, conqueror, foe-slayer, delight-maker, / sorrow-destroyer, virtue-bestowing, tranquil, destroyer of all misfortunes:
because these eight exceedingly strong lions are in your presence, / therefore you are praised by the Brahmins in the Vedas as siṃhāsana.
Śiva in person is seated upon you; upon you is Śakra, lord of the gods; / upon you is seated the god Hari; austerity is practiced for your sake.

4.138.s:
namaste sarvato bhadra bhadrado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
trailokyajayasarvasva siṃhāsana namo'stu te .. 83 .. ( iti siṃhāsanamaṃtraḥ ..)
lohābhihārikaṃ karma kṛtvedaṃ maṃtrapūrvakam..
phalanaivedyakusumairdhūpadīpavilepanaiḥ ..84..
aṣṭamyāṃ dhāvanaṃ kṛtvā pūrvāhṇe snānamācaret.... 85 ..
4.138.d:
नमस्ते सर्वतो भद्र भद्रदो भव भूपतेः ॥
त्रैलोक्यजयसर्वस्व सिंहासन नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 83 ॥ ( इति सिंहासनमंत्रः ॥)
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कृत्वेदं मंत्रपूर्वकम्॥
फलनैवेद्यकुसुमैर्धूपदीपविलेपनैः ॥84॥
अष्टम्यां धावनं कृत्वा पूर्वाह्णे स्नानमाचरेत्॥॥ 85 ॥
4.138.m:
Homage to you, all-propitious one! Be the bestower of fortune upon the king! / O all-in-all of victory over the three worlds, O siṃhāsana, homage to you! (Thus the throne mantra.)
Having performed this iron-lustration rite preceded by mantras, / with fruits, food offerings, flowers, incenses, lamps, and ointments,
having performed teeth-cleaning on the aṣṭamī, one should bathe in the morning.

4.138.s:
( atha gadyam)
durgāṃ kāṃcanamūrtiṃ raupyāṃ vā paittalīṃ vārkṣī caitrīṃ tāmrīṃ vādhibhavataḥ kṛtvā
dāruvicitratoraṇavinyastāṃ śobhane sthāne purato vinyastadṛṣṭāṃ vicitragṛhamadhyagāṃ
snātāṃ kuṃkumacaṃdanagaṃdhaiścatuḥsamaiścīrapaṭṭaiścarcitagātrāṃ devīṃ kusumairabhyarcya
tāṃ bahubhiḥ puṣyamāṇakīrtistairdvijananairjanitaparitoṣairdivānvito nareṃdraḥ svayaṃ
prayacchetpurohitaiḥ sārdhaṃ bilvapatreṇārcanena maṃtreṇānena bhagavatyai ..
( iti gadyaṃ sampūrṇaṃ) ..
jayaṃtī maṃgalā kālī bhadrakālī kapālinī ..
durgā śivā kṣamā dhātrī svāhā svadhā namostu te .. 86 ..
amṛtodbhavaḥ śrīvṛkṣo mahādevīpriyaḥ sadā ..
bilvapatraṃ prayacchāmi pavitraṃ te sureśvari .. 87 ..
durgā saṃpūjanīyā ca taddināddroṇapuṣpayā ..
sā cābhīṣṭā sureśānyāstathā rūḍhavraṇāyutaḥ ...88...
4.138.d:
( अथ गद्यम्)
दुर्गां कांचनमूर्तिं रौप्यां वा पैत्तलीं वार्क्षी चैत्रीं ताम्रीं वाधिभवतः कृत्वा
दारुविचित्रतोरणविन्यस्तां शोभने स्थाने पुरतो विन्यस्तदृष्टां विचित्रगृहमध्यगां
स्नातां कुंकुमचंदनगंधैश्चतुःसमैश्चीरपट्टैश्चर्चितगात्रां देवीं कुसुमैरभ्यर्च्य
तां बहुभिः पुष्यमाणकीर्तिस्तैर्द्विजननैर्जनितपरितोषैर्दिवान्वितो नरेंद्रः स्वयं
प्रयच्छेत्पुरोहितैः सार्धं बिल्वपत्रेणार्चनेन मंत्रेणानेन भगवत्यै ॥
( इति गद्यं सम्पूर्णं) ॥
जयंती मंगला काली भद्रकाली कपालिनी ॥
दुर्गा शिवा क्षमा धात्री स्वाहा स्वधा नमोस्तु ते ॥ 86 ॥
अमृतोद्भवः श्रीवृक्षो महादेवीप्रियः सदा ॥
बिल्वपत्रं प्रयच्छामि पवित्रं ते सुरेश्वरि ॥ 87 ॥
दुर्गा संपूजनीया च तद्दिनाद्द्रोणपुष्पया ॥
सा चाभीष्टा सुरेशान्यास्तथा रूढव्रणायुतः ॥.88॥।
4.138.m:
(Now the prose)
Having made an image of Durgā—either of gold, or of silver, or of brass, or made of wood, or painted, or of copper, according to one's means—
placed beneath a variegated wooden archway, positioned in an auspicious location with its gaze directed forward, inside a decorated pavilion,
the king himself, whose fame is magnified by many, accompanied by those Brahmins whom he has satisfied during the day, having bathed and having anointed the limbs of the goddess with saffron, sandalwood, fourfold fragrant pastes, and garments of bark-silk, and having worshipped her with flowers,
should, together with the family priests, offer bilva leaves to the goddess while worshipping her with this mantra:
(Thus ends the prose.)
Jayantī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, Kapālinī, / Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā, Svadhā: homage to you!
The bilva tree, arisen from nectar, is ever dear to the Great Goddess. / I offer to you a holy bilva leaf, O sovereign of the gods!
And Durgā should be worshipped from that day on with droṇapuṣpa blossoms; / and that is pleasing to the Queen of the gods [...].

4.138.s:
tataḥ khaḍgaṃ namaskṛtya śatrūṇāṃ mānamarddanam ..
icchetsvavijayaṃ rājyaṃ subhikṣaṃ cātmano nṛpa .. 89 ..
punaḥ punaḥ praṇamyātha dhyāyecca hṛdaye śivām..
mahiṣaghrīṃ bahubhujāṃ kumārīṃ siṃhavāhinīm .. 90 ..
dānavāṃstarjayaṃtīṃ ca khaḍgoddhatakarāṃ śubhām ..
ghaṃṭākṣasragdharāṃ durgāṃ raṇāraṃbhe vyavasthitām .. 91 ..
tato jayajayākāraiḥ stavaṃ kuryādimaṃ tataḥ .. 92 ..
sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye śive sarvārthasādhike ..
śaraṇye tryaṃbake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te .. 93 ..
kuṃkumena samālabdhe candanena vilepite ..
bilvapatrakṛtāmāle durge'haṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ..94..
kṛtvaivamarccāṃ kauravya aṣṭamyāṃ jāgaraṃ niśi ..
naṭanartanagītaiśca kārayettu mahotsavam ..95..
evaṃ hṛṣṭairniśāṃ nītvā prabhāte cāruṇodaye ..
pātayenmahiṣānmeṣānagrato natakandharān ..96..
4.138.d:
ततः खड्गं नमस्कृत्य शत्रूणां मानमर्द्दनम् ॥
इच्छेत्स्वविजयं राज्यं सुभिक्षं चात्मनो नृप ॥ 89 ॥
पुनः पुनः प्रणम्याथ ध्यायेच्च हृदये शिवाम्॥
महिषघ्रीं बहुभुजां कुमारीं सिंहवाहिनीम् ॥ 90 ॥
दानवांस्तर्जयंतीं च खड्गोद्धतकरां शुभाम् ॥
घंटाक्षस्रग्धरां दुर्गां रणारंभे व्यवस्थिताम् ॥ 91 ॥
ततो जयजयाकारैः स्तवं कुर्यादिमं ततः ॥ 92 ॥
सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके ॥
शरण्ये त्र्यंबके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 93 ॥
कुंकुमेन समालब्धे चन्दनेन विलेपिते ॥
बिल्वपत्रकृतामाले दुर्गेऽहं शरणं गतः ॥94॥
कृत्वैवमर्च्चां कौरव्य अष्टम्यां जागरं निशि ॥
नटनर्तनगीतैश्च कारयेत्तु महोत्सवम् ॥95॥
एवं हृष्टैर्निशां नीत्वा प्रभाते चारुणोदये ॥
पातयेन्महिषान्मेषानग्रतो नतकन्धरान् ॥96॥
4.138.m:
Then, having bowed to the sword which crushes the pride of enemies, / the king should desire his own victory, kingdom, and plenty.
Then, bowing down again and again, he should meditate in his heart upon Śivā, / who slew the buffalo, who has many arms, who is a maiden, riding on a lion,
threatening the Dānavas, her hand raised with a sword, auspicious, / holding a bell and a rosary, Durgā standing at the onset of battle.
Then, with cries of 'Victory! Victory!', he should then make this praise:
'O auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, O Śivā, O accomplisher of all purposes, / O refuge, O three-eyed Gauri, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you!
Smeared with saffron, anointed with sandalwood, / garlanded with bilva leaves, O Durgā, I have come to you for refuge.'
Having thus performed the worship, O descendant of Kuru, [he should observe] a vigil at night on the aṣṭamī, / and should cause a great festival to be held with actors, dancing, and songs.
Having thus spent the night joyfully, at daybreak when the dawn is red, / he should bring down buffaloes and rams before [her], their necks bent down.

4.138.m:
A hundred, or half a hundred, or half of that, according to his wish, / he should gratify Parameśvarī with jars filled with spirituous liquor.
That should be given to Kāpālikas, and by female and male servants, / having distributed it all, O son of Kuntī, among friends, in-laws, and relatives.
Then, in the afternoon on the navamī, Bhavānī stationed on a chariot / the king himself, accompanied by his army, should cause to be paraded around his realm,
or by thousands of well-trained men yoked to the chariot, / slowly, slowly, with blazing lamps of intense brilliance,
and by heroes with drawn swords, by elephants red with mineral pigment, / with sounding conches and kettle-drums, with dancing courtesans, / with adorned women, and with well-decorated boys.
He should give an offering containing meat to the ghosts with this mantra, / accompanied by blood, accompanied by water, accompanied by cooked food, endowed with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken grains:
Three times each with a trident he should cast the offering in the cardinal and intermediate directions: / 'May the gods, the Ādityas, and likewise the Vasus accept this offering,

सविघ्नं मम पापं ते शाम्यंतु परिपन्थिनः॥
सौम्या भवंतु तृप्ताश्च भूताः प्रेताः सुखावहाः ॥107॥
इत्येवं भ्रामयेद्राष्ट्रे दुर्गां देवीं रथे स्थिताम्॥
नरयानेन वा पार्थ ततोऽविघ्नं समापयेत् ॥1 08॥
अथोत्पन्नेषु विघ्नेषु भूतशांतिं समाचरेत् ॥
येन विघ्ना न जायंते यात्रासंपूर्णतां व्रजेत्॥1 09॥
एवं ये कुर्वते यात्रां राजानोऽन्येऽपि मानवाः॥
महानवम्यां नंदायां पुत्रका हृष्टमानसाः ॥11 0॥
ते सर्वे पापनिर्मुक्ता यांति भागवतीं पुरीम् ॥1 11॥
न तेषां शावकोनाग्निर्न चौरा न विनायकाः ॥
विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति राजेन्द्र येषां तुष्टा महेश्वरी ॥ 112 ॥
नीरुजः सुखिनो भोगभोक्तारो भयवर्जिताः॥
भवंति भक्ताः पुरुषाः भगवत्याः किमुच्यते ॥ 113 ॥
इत्येष ते समाख्यातो दुर्गादेव्या महोत्सवः ॥
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव सर्वाशुभविनाशनः ॥ 114 ॥
4.138.m:
Together with obstacles, may these my sins, these adversaries, be pacified; / satisfied, may the ghosts and pretas become gentle and bring happiness!'
In this way he should cause the goddess Durgā, standing on a chariot, to be paraded through the realm, / or on a palanquin, O son of Pṛthā; then he should conclude it without obstacles.
Now, if obstacles arise, he should perform the pacification of ghosts, / by which obstacles do not arise and the procession reaches completion.
Those who carry out the procession in this way, whether kings or other mortals, / on the Mahānavamī, the joy-giving [lunar day], O children, with delighted minds—
they, freed from all sin, go to the city of the Lord.
Neither fire, nor thieves, nor vināyakas / cause obstacle for them, O best of kings, with whom Maheśvarī is pleased.
Free from disease, happy, enjoyers of pleasures, free from fear / become men who are devotees of the Goddess; what [more] need be said?
Thus has this great festival of the goddess Durgā been related to you, / which destroys all inauspiciousness for those who recite it and those who hear it.

4.138.m:
Having worshipped on the navamī Durgā, who stands upon the back of Mahiṣāsura pierced by the point of her trident, / whose arm-staffs have lovely armlets and a drawn sword, who is attended by the five-faced [lion], mortals cross over impassable thickets.
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Mahānavamī Vrata', in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira, in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa. 138
The venerable Kṛṣṇa said: / The sacred Mahānavamī is the foremost lunar day among lunar days; / it is to be observed by all gods, and especially by protectors of people.
You, O son of Pṛthā, should raise it up for the sake of happiness for the entire year, / or for a festival and for the gratification of ghosts, pretas, and piśācas.
Yudhiṣṭhira said: / From what time has this navamī bearing the word 'great' commenced? / Was the rule of the navamī instituted in the beginning, O Blessed One?
Does this procession proceed from the birth from Yaśodā's womb, / or did it exist previously, in the Kṛta, Tretā, and other yugas?

4.138.d:
यदस्यां प्राणिनः केचिन्मन्यंते घातयंति च ॥
हतानां प्राणिनां तेषां का गतिः पारलौकिकी ॥ 5 ॥
स्वयं घ्नतां घातयतामनुमोदयतां तथा ॥
एतन्मे संशयं पूर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि केशव ॥ 6 ॥
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पार्थ या परमा शक्तिरनंता लोकविश्रुता ॥
आद्या सर्वगता शुद्धा भाव गम्या मनोहरा ॥ 7 ॥
आद्याष्टमी कलाकाली द्वितीया सर्वमंगला ॥
माया कात्यायनी दुर्गा चामुंडा शंकरप्रिया ॥ 8 ॥
ध्यायंति यां योगरतां सा देवी परमेश्वरी ॥
रूपभेदैर्नामभेदैर्भवानी पूज्यते शिवा॥9॥
अष्टम्यां तु नवम्यां तु देवदानवराक्षसैः॥
गंधर्वैरुरगैर्यज्ञैः पूज्यते किन्नरैर्नरैः॥10॥
अन्येष्वपि युगेष्वादौ सृष्टेः पूर्वं प्रदर्शिता॥
पूज्यतेयं पुरा देवी तेभ्यः पूर्वतरैः शुभैः॥11॥
4.138.m:
Since on this [day] some people consecrate and slaughter living beings, / what is the destination in the next world of those slaughtered creatures?
And of those who slay them themselves, who cause them to be slain, and likewise who approve [of it]? / You ought first to explain this doubt of mine, O Keśava.
The venerable Kṛṣṇa said: / O son of Pṛthā, that supreme power which is endless, renowned in the world, / primeval, all-pervading, pure, accessible through devotion, captivating—
as Ādyā, Aṣṭamī, Kalā, Kālī, as the second, Sarvamaṅgalā, / Māyā, Kātyāyanī, Durgā, Cāmuṇḍā, beloved of Śaṅkara;
whom those devoted to yoga meditate upon—she is the goddess Parameśvarī. / With various forms and various names, Bhavānī, Śivā is worshipped.
On the aṣṭamī and on the navamī she is worshipped by gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas, / by gandharvas, uragas, yakṣas, by kinnaras and men.
In other yugas also, revealed at the beginning, prior to creation, / this goddess was worshipped of old by those even earlier and auspicious.

4.138.d:
आश्वयुक्शुक्लपक्षे च याष्टमी मूल संयुता ॥
सा महानवमी नाम त्रैलोक्येऽपि सुदुर्लभा ॥ 12 ॥
कन्यागते सवितरि शुक्लपक्षेऽष्टमी तु या ॥
मूलनक्षत्रसंयुक्ता सा महानवमी स्मृता ॥ 13 ॥
अष्टम्यां च नवम्यां च जगन्मातरमम्बिकाम् ॥
पूजयित्वा'ऽश्विने मासि विशोको जयति द्विषः ॥ 14 ॥
संतर्जयंती हुंकारैः खड्गादिभिरहर्निशम् ॥
नवम्यां पूजिता देवी ददाति नवमं फलम् ॥ 15 ॥
सा पुण्या सा पवित्रा च सा धर्मसुखदायिनी ॥
तस्मात्सदा पूजनीया चामुंडा मुंडमालिनी ॥ 16 ॥
तस्यां यद्युपयुज्यंते प्राणिनो महिषादयः ॥
सर्वे ते स्वर्गतिं यांति घ्नतां पापं न विद्यते ॥ 17 ॥
न तथा बलिदानेन पुष्पधूपविलेपनैः ॥
यथा संतुष्यते लोके महिषैर्विंध्यवासिनी ॥ 18 ॥
उद्दिश्य दुर्गां हन्यंते विधानाद्येऽत्र जंतवः ॥
स्वर्गं ते यांति कौंतेय घातयंतोऽपि भक्तिः ॥ 19 ॥
4.138.m:
And in the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja, the aṣṭamī that is conjoined with Mūla, / that is called Mahānavamī, exceedingly difficult to obtain even in the three worlds.
When the sun has entered Virgo, the aṣṭamī in the bright fortnight / conjoined with the lunar mansion Mūla is considered Mahānavamī.
Having worshipped the Mother of the Universe, Ambikā, on the aṣṭamī and on the navamī / in the month of Āśvina, free from sorrow, he conquers his enemies.
Threatening with huṃkāras and with swords and other weapons day and night, / the goddess, worshipped on the navamī, grants fresh fruit.
She is holy, she is pure, and she is the bestower of righteousness and happiness; / therefore Cāmuṇḍā, garlanded with severed heads, is ever to be worshipped.
If on that [day] creatures such as buffaloes are offered up, / they all go to heaven, and no sin accrues to those who slaughter them.
Not by animal sacrifice, [nor] with flowers, incense, and ointments / is Vindhyavāsinī so pleased in the world as she is with buffaloes.
Those creatures that are slain here according to the rule for the sake of Durgā / go to heaven, O son of Kuntī, as do those who cause them to be slain through devotion.

4.138.d:
भवानीप्राङ्गणे प्राणा येषां याता युधिष्ठिर ॥
तेषां स्वर्गे ध्रुवं वासो वरास्तेऽप्यरसां प्रियाः ॥ 20 ॥
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु कल्पेषु कुरुनदन ॥
तेषु सर्वेषु चैवासन्नवमीयं पुरार्चिता ॥ 21 ॥
प्रसिद्धानादिनिधना वर्षेवर्षे युधिष्ठिर ॥
भूयोभूयोऽवतारैश्च भवानीपूज्य तेसुरैः ॥ 22 ॥
अवतीर्णा भुवि सदा नित्यं दैत्यनिबर्हिणी ॥
स्वर्गपातालमर्त्येषु करोति स्थितिपालनम् ॥ 23 ॥
पुनश्चैषा महादेवी यशोदा गर्भसंभवा ॥
कंसासुरस्योत्तमाङ्गे पादं दत्त्वा गतायुषः ॥ 24 ॥
ततः प्रभृति लोकेषु यशोदानंददायिनीम् ॥
विंध्याचले स्थापयित्वा पुनः पूजा प्रवर्तिता ॥ 25 ॥
पूर्वप्रवृद्धोऽपि पुनर्भगिन्या महिमा कृतः ॥
भुवि सर्वोपकाराय सर्वोपद्रवशांतये ॥ 26 ॥
एवं विंध्योपवासिन्या नवरात्रोपवासिनः ॥
एकरात्रेण नक्तेन स्वशक्त्याऽयाचितेन वा ॥ 27 ॥
4.138.m:
Those whose lives depart in Bhavānī's courtyard, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / obtain a permanent dwelling in heaven; they become handsome lovers of apsarases.
In all manvantaras and in all kalpas, O delight of the Kurus, / in all of them this navamī was worshipped in ancient times.
Famed, without beginning or end, year after year, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / through her repeated incarnations, Bhavānī is worshipped by the gods.
Descended constantly to the earth, the perpetual slayer of Daityas / maintains order in heaven, the underworld, and the mortal realm.
And once again this great goddess was born from the womb of Yaśodā, / placing her foot on the head of the demon Kaṃsa whose lifespan had ended.
From that time forward, after installing her who brought joy to Yaśodā upon the Vindhya mountain, / her worship was instituted again in the worlds.
Though already great from ancient times, her greatness was manifested again as a sister / for the benefit of all on earth, for the pacification of every affliction.
Thus, fasting during the Navarātra for the dweller on the Vindhyas, / with a fast of one night, a nocturnal meal, or unsolicited food according to one's ability,

यजनैर्याजनैर्देवाः स्थानेस्थाने पुरेपुरे ॥
गृहेगृहे भक्तिपरे र्ग्रामेग्रामे वनेवने ॥ 28 ॥
स्नातैः प्रमुदितैर्हृष्टैर्ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्नृपैः ॥
वैश्यैः शूद्रैर्भक्तिचित्रैर्म्लेच्छैरन्यैश्च मानवैः ॥ 29 ॥
स्त्रीभिश्च कुरुशार्दूल तद्विधानमिदं शृणु ॥
जयाभिलाषी नृपतिः प्रतिपत्प्रभृतिक्रमात् ॥ 30 ॥
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कारयेद्यावदष्टमि ॥
प्रागुदक्प्रवणे देशे पताकाभिरलंकृतम् ॥ 31 ॥
मण्डपं कारयेद्दिव्यं नवसप्तकरं वरम् ॥
आग्नेय्यां कारयेत्कुण्डं हस्तमात्रं सुशोभनम् ॥ 32 ॥
मेखलात्रयसं युक्तं योन्यश्वत्थदलाभया ॥

आनीय मण्डपे तानि सर्वाण्येवाधिवासयेत् ॥
ततस्तु ब्राह्मणः स्नातः शुक्लांबरधरः शुचिः॥ 34 ॥
