4.138.m:
by sacrificing and by officiating at sacrifices to the gods in every place, every city, / every house, devoted, in every village, and in every forest,
by brāhmaṇas who have bathed, joyful and glad, by kṣatriyas, kings, / vaiśyas, and śūdras, with varied devotions, by mlecchas, and by other humans,
and by women, O tiger of the Kurus—hear this procedure for it: / A king desirous of victory, beginning from the pratipad in regular order,
should have the iron-lustration rite performed up to the aṣṭamī. / On ground sloping toward the east or north, decorated with banners,
he should have an excellent, splendid pavilion erected, sixteen cubits in size. / In the south-east he should have a very beautiful sacrificial pit made, measuring a cubit,
endowed with three rims, with a vulva shaped like an aśvattha leaf. / All the insignia of royalty and whatever weapons and missiles there are,
having brought them to the pavilion, he should consecrate them all. / Then a brāhmaṇa, having bathed, wearing white garments, pure,
should offer clarified butter with mantras preceded by the syllable Oṃ and bearing their characteristic marks. (35cd)

4.138.d:
लोहनामाभवत्पूर्वं दानवस्तु महाबलः ॥ 35 ॥
स देवैः समरे क्रुद्धैर्बहुधा शकलीकृतः ॥
तदंगसम्भवं लोहं यत्सर्वंदृश्यते क्षितौ ॥ 36 ॥
शस्त्रास्त्रमन्त्रैर्होतव्यं पायसं घृतसंयुतम् ॥
हुतशेषं तुरंगाणां गजानामुपहारयेत् ॥ 37 ॥
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म तेनैतदृषिभिः स्मृतम् ॥
बद्धप्रतिशरव्यं च गजाश्वसमलंकृतम् ॥ 38 ॥
भ्रामयेन्नगरे नित्यं नंदि घोषपुरस्सरम्॥
प्रत्यहं नृपतिः स्नात्वा संपूज्य पितृदेवताः ॥ 39 ॥
पूजयेद्राजचिह्नानि फलमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥
हुतशेषं प्रदातव्यमौपनायनिके द्विजे ॥ 40 ॥
तस्याभिहरणाद्राज्ञो विजयः समुदाहृतः ॥
पूजामंत्रान्प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणोक्तानहं तव ॥ 41 ॥
यैः पूजिताः प्रयच्छन्ति कीर्तिमायु र्यशोबलम॥
यथांबुदश्छादयति शिवायेमां वसुन्धराम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.138.m:
Formerly there was an exceedingly powerful dānava named Loha. (36ab)
[…] he was cut into many pieces in battle by the enraged gods; / all the iron seen on earth was produced from his body.
One should offer milk-rice mixed with ghee with the mantras for weapons and missiles; / the remainder of the offering he should present to the horses and elephants.
Therefore this rite is termed the iron-lustration rite by the sages. / Having targets bound to them and adorned with elephants and horses,
he should parade [the weapons] daily through the city, accompanied by the sounding of musical instruments. / Every day the king, having bathed and worshipped the ancestors and deities,
should worship the insignia of royalty with fruits, garlands, and unguents. / The remainder of the offering should be given to a brāhmaṇa who has undergone the upanayana.
By virtue of carrying it out, victory is proclaimed for the king. / I shall tell you the worship mantras taught in the Purāṇas,
worshipped with which they bestow renown, long life, fame, and strength. / Just as a cloud covers this earth for its welfare,

तथाच्छादय राजानं विजयारोग्यवृद्धये ॥ ( इति छत्रमन्त्रः) ॥
गन्धर्व कुलजातस्त्वं माभूयाः कुलदूषकः ॥ 43 ॥
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च ॥
प्रभावाञ्च हुताशस्य वर्द्धस्व त्वं तुरंगम ॥ 44 ॥
तेजसा चैव सूर्यस्य मुनीनां तपसा यथा ॥
रुद्रस्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पवनस्य वलेन च॥ स्मृ ॥
स्मर त्वं राजपुत्रोऽसि कौस्तुभं च मणिं स्मर ॥
यां गतिं ब्रह्महा गच्छेत्पितृहा मातृहा तथा ॥ 46 ॥
भूम्यर्थेनृतवादी च क्षत्रियश्च पराङ्मुखः ॥
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुः पावकश्च न यत्र वै ॥ 47॥
व्रजेच्च तां गतिं क्षिप्रं तच्च पापं भवेत्किल ॥
विकृतिं यदि गच्छेस्त्वं युद्धेध्वनि तुरंगम ॥
रिपून्विजित्य समरे सह भर्त्रा सुखी भव ॥ 48 ॥॥ ॥ ( इत्यश्वमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
4.138.m:
so do you cover the king, for the increase of victory and health. (Thus the parasol mantra.) / You are born in the family of the Gandharvas; do not become a disgrace to your line.
By the true word of Brahmā, and of Soma and Varuṇa, / and by the power of Agni, grow strong, O steed!
And by the splendour of the sun, as by the asceticism of the sages, / by the celibacy of Rudra, and by the strength of the wind— / remember, you are a king's son! And remember the Kaustubha gem! / That destination to which a killer of a brāhmaṇa, a father, or a mother goes,
or one who speaks falsely for the sake of land, or a kṣatriya who turns his back on battle, / where indeed the sun and moon, the wind, and fire do not exist,
to that destination indeed you would quickly go, and that sin would surely be yours, / if you should falter in battle or on the march, O horse! / Having conquered the enemies in battle, be happy along with your master! (Thus the horse mantra.)

शक्रकेतो महावीर्य सुपर्णस्त्वय्युपस्थितः ॥
पतत्रिराड्वैनतेयस्तथा नारायणध्वजः ॥ 49 ॥
काश्यपेयोऽमृतो ज्ञेयो नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः ॥
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो देवशत्रुनिषूदनः ॥ 50 ॥
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिस्त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः ॥
शस्त्रवर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षास्मांश्च रिपून्दह ॥ 51 ॥ ॥ (इति ध्वजमंत्रः) ॥ ॥
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदंतोऽथ वामनः ॥
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नील एतेऽष्टौ देवयोनयः ॥॥ 52 ॥
एतेषां पुत्रपौत्राश्च बलान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः ॥
भद्रो मन्द्रो मृगश्चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च ॥
वनेवने प्रसूतास्ते करियोनिं महागजाः॥53॥
पातु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः ॥
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयं प्रतिपालयन् ॥ 54 ॥
4.138.m:
O banner of Indra of great valour, the bird Garuḍa is present upon you; / the king of birds, the son of Vinatā, and the emblem of Nārāyaṇa,
the son of Kaśyapa, known as immortal, the enemy of serpents, the mount of Viṣṇu, / immeasurable, invincible, the slayer of the foes of the gods,
Garutmān, who moves like the wind, stands close at hand upon you. / Protect the weapons, armour, arms, and warriors, and burn our enemies! (Thus the banner mantra.)
Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—these eight are of divine origin.
Their sons and grandsons resorted to the eight army divisions: / bhadra, mandra, mṛga, and saṃkīrṇa elephants. / Born in every forest, they are the great elephants born of elephant stock.
May the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas together with the Marut hosts protect you! / Protect your master, O lord of elephants, observing your commitment!

4.138.s:
avāpurhi jayaṃ yuddhe gamane svasti no vraja ..
śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavonilāt ..
sthairyaṃ merorjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devātpuraṃdarāt .. 55 ..
yuddhe rakṣaṃtu nāgāstvāṃ diśaśca saha daivataiḥ ..
aśvinau saha gaṃdharvaiḥ pāṃtu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā .. 56 .. ( iti hastimaṃtraḥ ..)
hutabhugvasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ ..
nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣa bhūtagaṇāgrahāḥ .. 57 ..
pramathāśca sahādityairbhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha ..
śakrasenāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritāstvayi .. 58 ..
pradahaṃtu ripūnsarvānrājā vijayamṛcchatu ..
yāni prayuktānyaribhirdūṣaṇāni samaṃtataḥ .. 59 ..
etāni paraśatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā ..
kālanemivadhe yuddhe yuddhe tripuraghātane .. 60 ..
hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe yuddhe devāsure tathā ..
śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhamānāstu bhūpateḥ .. 61 ..
4.138.d:
अवापुर्हि जयं युद्धे गमने स्वस्ति नो व्रज ॥
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवोनिलात् ॥
स्थैर्यं मेरोर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात्पुरंदरात् ॥ 55 ॥
युद्धे रक्षंतु नागास्त्वां दिशश्च सह दैवतैः ॥
अश्विनौ सह गंधर्वैः पांतु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥ 56 ॥ ( इति हस्तिमंत्रः ॥)
हुतभुग्वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः ॥
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयक्ष भूतगणाग्रहाः ॥ 57 ॥
प्रमथाश्च सहादित्यैर्भूतेशो मातृभिः सह ॥
शक्रसेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितास्त्वयि ॥ 58 ॥
प्रदहंतु रिपून्सर्वान्राजा विजयमृच्छतु ॥
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्दूषणानि समंततः ॥ 59 ॥
एतानि परशत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा ॥
कालनेमिवधे युद्धे युद्धे त्रिपुरघातने ॥ 60 ॥
हिरण्यकशिपोर्युद्धे युद्धे देवासुरे तथा ॥
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभमानास्तु भूपतेः ॥ 61 ॥
4.138.m:
For they attained victory in battle; in marching out, proceed with welfare for us! / May your splendour be from Soma, strength from Viṣṇu, radiance from Sūrya, speed from the wind, / steadfastness from Meru, victory from Rudra, and glory from King Indra!
May the celestial serpents and the directions along with their deities protect you in battle! / May the two Aśvins along with the Gandharvas protect you on all sides always! (Thus the elephant mantra.)
The Fire, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Wind, Soma, the great sages, / the nāgas, kinnaras, gandharvas, yakṣas, bhūta hosts, and planets,
the pramathas together with the Ādityas, the Lord of Bhūtas with the Mothers, / Skanda the commander of Indra's army, and Varuṇa—all reside in you.
May they burn all enemies; may the king attain victory! / Whatever sorceries have been directed against us on all sides by the enemies,
these of the enemy adversaries are destroyed by your splendour! / In the battle for the slaying of Kālanemi, in the battle for the destruction of Tripura,
in the battle with Hiraṇyakaśipu, and likewise in the battle between the gods and asuras, / you shone forth; likewise today, shine forth for the king!

4.138.s:
nīlāṃ śvetāmimāṃ dṛṣṭvā naśyaṃtvadya nṛpārayaḥ ..
vyādhibhirvividhairghoraiḥ śastraiśca yudhi nirjitāḥ .. 62 ..
sadyaḥ svasthā bhavaṃti sma tvadvātenāpamārjitāḥ .. 63 ..
pūtanā revatī nāmnā kālarātrīti yā smṛtā ..
dahaṃtvāśu ripūnsarvānpatāke tvāmupāgatāḥ .. 64 .. (iti patākāmantraḥ ..)
asiśca ripuhā khaḍgastīkṣṇakarmā durāsadaḥ ..
śrīgarbho vijayaścaiva dharmadhārastathaiva ca .. 69 ..
ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni svayamuktāni vedhasā ..
nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ .. 66 ..
hiraṇyaṃ ca śarīraṃte dhātā devojanārdanaḥ ..
pitā pitāmaho devastvaṃ māṃ pālaya sarvadā .. 67 .. (iti khaḍgamantraḥ ..)
śarmapradastvaṃ samare varma sarvāyaso hyasi ..
rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo'haṃ tava varmannamo'stu te .. 68 .. ( iti varmamantraḥ ..) ..
4.138.d:
नीलां श्वेतामिमां दृष्ट्वा नश्यंत्वद्य नृपारयः ॥
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर्घोरैः शस्त्रैश्च युधि निर्जिताः ॥ 62 ॥
सद्यः स्वस्था भवंति स्म त्वद्वातेनापमार्जिताः ॥ 63 ॥
पूतना रेवती नाम्ना कालरात्रीति या स्मृता ॥
दहंत्वाशु रिपून्सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपागताः ॥ 64 ॥ (इति पताकामन्त्रः ॥)
असिश्च रिपुहा खड्गस्तीक्ष्णकर्मा दुरासदः ॥
श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्मधारस्तथैव च ॥ 69 ॥
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि स्वयमुक्तानि वेधसा ॥
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः ॥ 66 ॥
हिरण्यं च शरीरंते धाता देवोजनार्दनः ॥
पिता पितामहो देवस्त्वं मां पालय सर्वदा ॥ 67 ॥ (इति खड्गमन्त्रः ॥)
शर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे वर्म सर्वायसो ह्यसि ॥
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयोऽहं तव वर्मन्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 68 ॥ ( इति वर्ममन्त्रः ॥) ॥
4.138.m:
Having seen this blue and white [banner], may the king's enemies perish today, / vanquished in battle by dreadful, diverse afflictions and by weapons.
They became well at once, swept over by your breeze. 63.
She who is known as Pūtanā, Revatī by name, and Kālarātrī, / having approached you, O banner, may they swiftly burn all enemies. (Thus the mantra for the banner.)
Asi, Ripuhā, Khaḍga, Tīkṣṇakarmā, Durāsada, / Śrīgarbha, Vijaya, and also Dharmadhāra—
thus these eight names of yours were spoken by the Creator himself. / Your constellation is Kṛttikā, and your guru is the god Maheśvara.
Your body is gold, and your creator is the god Janārdana; / the god [Brahma], the Grandfather, is your father. Protect me always! (Thus the mantra for the sword.)
You grant peace in battle, for you are armour made entirely of iron. / Protect me, for I am to be protected by you; O armour, homage to you! (Thus the mantra for the armour.)

4.138.s:
dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ .ghoṣāddhṛdayakampan ..
bhava bhūmipa sainyānāṃ tathā vijayavarddhanaḥ .. 69 ..
yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyaṃti varavāraṇāḥ ..
tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo'smākaṃ mudāvahaḥ ..70..
yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso'bhijāyate ..
tathā ca tava śabdena trasyaṃtvasmaddviṣo raṇe..71..( iti duṃdubhimaṃtraḥ ..)
sarvāyudha mahāmātra sarvadevārisūdana ..
cāpa māṃ sarvadā rakṣa sākaṃ sāyakasattamaiḥ .. 72.. ( iti cāpamantraḥ..)
puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṣpāṇāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam ..
viṣṇunā vidhṛto nityaṃ manaḥśāṃtiprado bhava .. 73 .. ( iti śaṅkhamantraḥ ..)
śaśāṃkakarasaṃkāśa hima ḍiṃḍīrapāṃḍura ..
protsārayāśu duritaṃ cāmarāmaravallabha .. 74 .. ( iti cāmaramaṃtraḥ ..)
sarvāyudhānāṃ prathamā nirmitā'si pinākinā ..
śūlāyudhādviniṣkṛṣya kṛtvā muṣṭiparigraham .. 75 ..
4.138.d:
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां ।घोषाद्धृदयकम्पन् ॥
भव भूमिप सैन्यानां तथा विजयवर्द्धनः ॥ 69 ॥
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यंति वरवारणाः ॥
तथास्तु तव शब्देन हर्षोऽस्माकं मुदावहः ॥70॥
यथा जीमूतशब्देन स्त्रीणां त्रासोऽभिजायते ॥
तथा च तव शब्देन त्रस्यंत्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे॥71॥( इति दुंदुभिमंत्रः ॥)
सर्वायुध महामात्र सर्वदेवारिसूदन ॥
चाप मां सर्वदा रक्ष साकं सायकसत्तमैः ॥ 72॥ ( इति चापमन्त्रः॥)
पुण्यस्त्वं शङ्ख पुष्पाणां मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ॥
विष्णुना विधृतो नित्यं मनःशांतिप्रदो भव ॥ 73 ॥ ( इति शङ्खमन्त्रः ॥)
शशांककरसंकाश हिम डिंडीरपांडुर ॥
प्रोत्सारयाशु दुरितं चामरामरवल्लभ ॥ 74 ॥ ( इति चामरमंत्रः ॥)
सर्वायुधानां प्रथमा निर्मिताऽसि पिनाकिना ॥
शूलायुधाद्विनिष्कृष्य कृत्वा मुष्टिपरिग्रहम् ॥ 75 ॥
4.138.m:
O war drum, you who make the hearts of adversaries tremble by your roaring, / be the enhancer of victory for the armies of the king.
Just as excellent elephants rejoice at the roar of a raincloud, / so let our joy, bringing gladness, arise from your sound.
Just as terror arises in women at the sound of a raincloud, / even so let our enemies tremble in battle at your sound. (Thus the mantra for the war drum.)
O commander of all weapons, slayer of all the enemies of the gods, / O bow, protect me always together with the finest arrows! (Thus the mantra for the bow.)
You are holy, O conch, the flower of all auspicious things and the auspiciousness of auspicious things, / held perpetually by Viṣṇu: grant peace of mind! (Thus the mantra for the conch.)
Resembling the moon’s rays, white as snow and foam, / swiftly dispel misfortune, O chowrie, beloved of the immortals! (Thus the mantra for the chowrie.)
You were fashioned by Pinākin as the foremost of all weapons, / pulled forth from the trident-weapon and provided with a hilt.

4.138.s:
caṃḍikāyāḥ pradattāsi sarvaduṣṭanibarhiṇi ..
tathā vistāritā cāsi devānāṃ pratipāditā .. 76 ..
sarva sattvāṃgabhūtāsi
sarvāśubhanivāriṇi ..
churike rakṣa māṃ nityaṃ śāntiṃ yaccha namo'stu te .. 77 .. ( iticchūrikāmaṃtraḥ ..)
protsāraṇāya duṣṭānāṃ sādhusaṃgrahaṇāya ca ..
brahmaṇā nirmitaścāsi vyavahāraprasiddhaye ..78..
yaśo dehi sukhaṃ dehi jagado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
tāḍayāśu ripūnsarvānhemadaṃḍa namostu te .. 70 .. ( iti kanakadaṇḍamantraḥ ..)
vijayo jayado jetā ripughātī priyaṃkaraḥ ..
duḥkhahā dharmadaḥ śāṃtaḥ sarvāriṣṭavināśanaḥ ..80..
ete'ṣṭausaṃnidhau yasmāttava siṃhā mahābalāḥ...
tena siṃhāsaneti tvaṃ viprairvedeṣu gīyase ..81..
tvayi sthitaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāttvayi śakraḥ sureśvaraḥ..
tvayi sthito harirdevastvadarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ .. 82 ..
4.138.d:
चंडिकायाः प्रदत्तासि सर्वदुष्टनिबर्हिणि ॥
तथा विस्तारिता चासि देवानां प्रतिपादिता ॥ 76 ॥
सर्व सत्त्वांगभूतासि
सर्वाशुभनिवारिणि ॥
छुरिके रक्ष मां नित्यं शान्तिं यच्छ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 77 ॥ ( इतिच्छूरिकामंत्रः ॥)
प्रोत्सारणाय दुष्टानां साधुसंग्रहणाय च ॥
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितश्चासि व्यवहारप्रसिद्धये ॥78॥
यशो देहि सुखं देहि जगदो भव भूपतेः ॥
ताडयाशु रिपून्सर्वान्हेमदंड नमोस्तु ते ॥ 70 ॥ ( इति कनकदण्डमन्त्रः ॥)
विजयो जयदो जेता रिपुघाती प्रियंकरः ॥
दुःखहा धर्मदः शांतः सर्वारिष्टविनाशनः ॥80॥
एतेऽष्टौसंनिधौ यस्मात्तव सिंहा महाबलाः॥।
तेन सिंहासनेति त्वं विप्रैर्वेदेषु गीयसे ॥81॥
त्वयि स्थितः शिवः साक्षात्त्वयि शक्रः सुरेश्वरः॥
त्वयि स्थितो हरिर्देवस्त्वदर्थं तप्यते तपः ॥ 82 ॥
4.138.m:
You were given to Caṇḍikā, O destroyer of all evil ones, / and thus you were expanded and delivered to the gods.
You have become a part of the bodies of all beings, / O dispeller of all inauspiciousness! / O dagger, protect me perpetually and grant peace! Homage to you! 77. (Thus the dagger mantra.)
For driving away the wicked and for protecting the virtuous, / and for the accomplishment of statecraft, you were fashioned by Brahmā.
Give fame, give happiness, be the protector of the king; / strike down all enemies swiftly, O golden sceptre, homage to you! (Thus the mantra for the golden sceptre.)
Vijaya, Jayada, Jetā, Ripughātī, Priyaṃkara, / Duḥkhahā, Dharmada, Śānta, Sarvāriṣṭavināśana—
because these eight lions of great strength are present in you, / therefore you are celebrated as a throne by the brahmins in the Vedas.
In you Śiva himself is seated; in you is Śakra, lord of the gods; / in you the god Hari is seated; for your sake asceticism is performed.

4.138.s:
namaste sarvato bhadra bhadrado bhava bhūpateḥ ..
trailokyajayasarvasva siṃhāsana namo'stu te .. 83 .. ( iti siṃhāsanamaṃtraḥ ..)
lohābhihārikaṃ karma kṛtvedaṃ maṃtrapūrvakam..
phalanaivedyakusumairdhūpadīpavilepanaiḥ ..84..
aṣṭamyāṃ dhāvanaṃ kṛtvā pūrvāhṇe snānamācaret.... 85 ..
4.138.d:
नमस्ते सर्वतो भद्र भद्रदो भव भूपतेः ॥
त्रैलोक्यजयसर्वस्व सिंहासन नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 83 ॥ ( इति सिंहासनमंत्रः ॥)
लोहाभिहारिकं कर्म कृत्वेदं मंत्रपूर्वकम्॥
फलनैवेद्यकुसुमैर्धूपदीपविलेपनैः ॥84॥
अष्टम्यां धावनं कृत्वा पूर्वाह्णे स्नानमाचरेत्॥॥ 85 ॥
4.138.m:
Homage to you who are auspicious on every side! Be the bestower of auspiciousness upon the king; / O entire substance of victory over the three worlds, O throne, homage to you! (Thus the mantra for the throne.)
Having performed this iron-lustration rite accompanied by mantras, / with fruits, food offerings, flowers, incenses, lamps, and ointments,
and having cleansed oneself on the aṣṭamī, one should take a bath in the forenoon.

4.138.s:
( atha gadyam)
durgāṃ kāṃcanamūrtiṃ raupyāṃ vā paittalīṃ vārkṣī caitrīṃ tāmrīṃ vādhibhavataḥ kṛtvā
dāruvicitratoraṇavinyastāṃ śobhane sthāne purato vinyastadṛṣṭāṃ vicitragṛhamadhyagāṃ
snātāṃ kuṃkumacaṃdanagaṃdhaiścatuḥsamaiścīrapaṭṭaiścarcitagātrāṃ devīṃ kusumairabhyarcya
tāṃ bahubhiḥ puṣyamāṇakīrtistairdvijananairjanitaparitoṣairdivānvito nareṃdraḥ svayaṃ
prayacchetpurohitaiḥ sārdhaṃ bilvapatreṇārcanena maṃtreṇānena bhagavatyai ..
( iti gadyaṃ sampūrṇaṃ) ..
jayaṃtī maṃgalā kālī bhadrakālī kapālinī ..
durgā śivā kṣamā dhātrī svāhā svadhā namostu te .. 86 ..
amṛtodbhavaḥ śrīvṛkṣo mahādevīpriyaḥ sadā ..

4.138.m:
(Now the prose passage:)
Having had an image of Durgā fashioned according to his means—golden, silver, brass, wooden, painted, or copper—placed within an ornamental arch of wood in a beautiful spot, with eyes directed forward, set in the middle of an ornate pavilion, bathed and her limbs anointed with saffron, sandalwood, perfumes, the fourfold unguent, and silken garments, having worshipped the goddess with flowers, the king, accompanied by priests, his fame proclaimed by many and bringing satisfaction to the brahmins, should himself present worship to the goddess with a bilva leaf, [reciting] this mantra:
(Thus ends the prose passage.)
Jayaṃtī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, Kapālinī, / Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā, Svadhā: homage to you!
Born of ambrosia, the sacred bilva tree is ever dear to the Great Goddess. / I offer you this pure bilva leaf, O ruler of the gods!
Durgā should also be worshipped from that day on with droṇapuṣpa flowers, / for she is beloved of the ruler of the gods […].

4.138.m:
Then, having bowed to the sword that crushes the pride of enemies, / the king should desire his own victory, kingdom, and abundance of food.
Then, having bowed repeatedly, he should meditate in his heart upon Śivā, / slayer of the buffalo, many-armed, a maiden riding a lion,
terrifying the dānavas, her hand raised with a sword, auspicious, / holding a bell and a rosary, Durgā standing at the commencement of battle.
Then, with shouts of victory, he should next make this hymn of praise:
O auspiciousness of all auspicious things, O Śivā, accomplisher of all aims, / refuge, three-eyed one, Gaurī, Nārāyaṇī, homage to you!
Anointed with saffron, smeared with sandalwood, / garlanded with bilva leaves, O Durgā, I have taken refuge in you.
Having performed the worship thus, O descendant of Kuru, on the aṣṭamī night he should keep vigil, / and have a great festival celebrated with actors, dances, and songs.
Having spent the night with joyful people in this manner, at dawn, when the sun rises, / he should strike down buffaloes and rams before [her], their necks bowed low,

That should be given to the Kāpālikas and to the female and male servants, / having distributed it all among friends, associates, and kinsmen, O son of Kuntī.

as well as the Maruts, the two Aśvins, the Rudras, the birds, the serpents, the planets, / the asuras, the yātudhānas, the mothers, and the piśācas,
the śākinīs, yakṣas, vetālas, yoginīs, pūtanās, jackals, / the jṛmbhakas, siddhas, gandharvas, wild beasts, vidyādharas, mountains,
the guardians of the directions, the world protectors, whichever obstacle-making vināyakas there are, / the bringers of peace to the worlds, and the great sages beginning with Brahmā.
May my sin together with its obstacles, and those who oppose me, be pacified; / may the ghosts and pretas be gentle, satisfied, and bringers of happiness!"
Thus he should parade the goddess Durgā standing on her chariot through the kingdom, / or on a palanquin, O son of Pṛthā, and then bring it to a close without obstacles.
Now, should obstacles arise, he should perform an appeasement of the spirits, / by which obstacles do not arise and the procession reaches completion.
Kings and other men too who carry out the procession in this manner / on Mahānavamī, the Nandā tithi, [obtain] sons and have joyful minds;
freed from all sins, they go to the city of the Goddess.

नामाष्टत्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः॥138॥

4.138.m:
Neither the fire from a child's corpse, nor thieves, nor vināyakas / cause an obstacle for those with whom the Great Goddess is pleased, O king of kings.
Free from disease, happy, enjoying pleasures, and devoid of fear / become the men devoted to the Goddess—what more need be said?
Thus this great festival of the goddess Durgā has been fully related to you; / for those who read it and listen to it, it destroys all inauspiciousness.
Having worshipped Durgā on the navamī—who stands on the back of Mahiṣāsura pierced by the tip of her trident, whose arm-staffs have splendid armlets and a brandished sword, and who is followed by the five-faced [Śiva]—mortals cross over the most impassable depths.
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Mahānavamī Vrata', in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira, in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa. 138

तां दृष्ट्वा दानवा नष्टा भयादेव रणे हताः ॥
गता रसातलं दैत्या देवाश्चापि दिवि स्थिताः ॥ 3 ॥
4.139.m: with her white parasol, bells, and baskets, and bubbles strung with small bells. / Seeing it, the dānavas perished, slain in battle out of sheer terror; / the daityas went to Rasātala, and the gods remained in heaven.

4.139.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tāṃ divyāmiṃdrayaṣṭiṃ yajaṃti te ..
devāḥ sarve gaṇāḥ sarve hṛṣṭāstuṣṭā yudhiṣṭhira .. 4 ..
4.139.d:
ततः प्रभृति तां दिव्यामिंद्रयष्टिं यजंति ते ॥
देवाः सर्वे गणाः सर्वे हृष्टास्तुष्टा युधिष्ठिर ॥ 4 ॥
4.139.m: From that time forth, all the gods and all the hosts, / joyous and satisfied, worship that divine Indra-pole, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

4.139.s:
ataḥ svargaṃ gato rājā bhūripuṇyavaśādvasuḥ ..
indraloke mahābhāgo vasudevaiḥ supūjitaḥ .. 5 ..
4.139.d:
अतः स्वर्गं गतो राजा भूरिपुण्यवशाद्वसुः ॥
इन्द्रलोके महाभागो वसुदेवैः सुपूजितः ॥ 5 ॥
4.139.m: Consequently, King Vasu went to heaven by virtue of his abundant merit; / the illustrious one was well worshipped in the world of Indra by the Vasus and gods.

4.139.s:
tasmai datā mahendreṇa vasuyaṣṭiḥ pragṛhyatām ..
pūjayitvā mahābhāga sarvadaityāpanuttaye .. 6 ..
4.139.d:
तस्मै दता महेन्द्रेण वसुयष्टिः प्रगृह्यताम् ॥
पूजयित्वा महाभाग सर्वदैत्यापनुत्तये ॥ 6 ॥
4.139.m: The pole of Vasu was given to him by Mahendra, [who said:] "Let it be accepted, / and after worshipping it, O illustrious one, for the dispelling of all daityas,

4.139.s:
avatārya varṣāsamaye sarvairnṛpatibhiḥ saha ..
mahyāṃ saṃpūjayāmāsa cakre ceṃdramahaṃ vasuḥ .. 7..
4.139.d:
अवतार्य वर्षासमये सर्वैर्नृपतिभिः सह ॥
मह्यां संपूजयामास चक्रे चेंद्रमहं वसुः ॥ 7॥
4.139.m: having brought it down at the time of the rains, Vasu, along with all the kings, / worshipped it on the earth and celebrated the festival of Indra.

4.139.s: mahena maghavā prīto dadau puṇyaṃ vasorvaram .. 8 ..
4.139.d: महेन मघवा प्रीतो ददौ पुण्यं वसोर्वरम् ॥ 8 ॥
4.139.m: Pleased by the festival, Maghavan granted a holy boon to Vasu:

4.139.s:
yeṣu deśeṣu manujā bhaktibhāvapuraḥsarāḥ ..
pūjayiṣyaṃti varṣānte mayā dattaṃ mahādhvajam .. 9 ..
4.139.d:
येषु देशेषु मनुजा भक्तिभावपुरःसराः ॥
पूजयिष्यंति वर्षान्ते मया दत्तं महाध्वजम् ॥ 9 ॥
4.139.m: "In whatever lands men, preceded by the sentiment of devotion, / worship the great banner given by me at the end of the rains,

4.139.s:
teṣu deśeṣu muditāḥ prajā rogavivarjitāḥ ..
prabhūtānnā dharmayuktā vṛṣamedhā mahotsavāḥ .. 4.139.10 ..
4.139.d:
तेषु देशेषु मुदिताः प्रजा रोगविवर्जिताः ॥
प्रभूतान्ना धर्मयुक्ता वृषमेधा महोत्सवाः ॥ 4.139.10 ॥
4.139.m: in those lands the subjects will be joyful, free from disease, / with abundant food, endowed with righteousness, [performing] bull-sacrifices and great festivals,

4.139.s: bhaviṣyaṃti suveṣāśca subhāṣāśca subhūṣaṇāḥ .. 11 ..
4.139.d: भविष्यंति सुवेषाश्च सुभाषाश्च सुभूषणाः ॥ 11 ॥
4.139.m: and they will have fine dress, fine speech, and fine ornaments."

4.139.s:
śrutvaitadvacanaṃ rājā vasurvasumatāṃ varaḥ ..
viśeṣeṇa tataścakre varṣevarṣe mahotsavam .. 12 ..
4.139.d:
श्रुत्वैतद्वचनं राजा वसुर्वसुमतां वरः ॥
विशेषेण ततश्चक्रे वर्षेवर्षे महोत्सवम् ॥ 12 ॥
4.139.m: Having heard this speech, King Vasu, the best of the wealthy, / thereafter celebrated that great festival especially, year after year.

4.139.s:
śravaṇe sthāpayedyaṣṭiṃ snānavastraiḥ prapūjitām ..
dairghyeṇa viṃśatikarāṃ sāradārumayīṃ śubhām .. 13 ..
4.139.d:
श्रवणे स्थापयेद्यष्टिं स्नानवस्त्रैः प्रपूजिताम् ॥
दैर्घ्येण विंशतिकरां सारदारुमयीं शुभाम् ॥ 13 ॥
4.139.m: Under Śravaṇa he should erect the pole, worshipped with baths and garments, / twenty cubits in length, made of sound timber, and auspicious,

4.139.s:
indrasthāne puroddiṣṭe indramātṛkasaṃjñake ..
tasminyaṣṭiṃ nṛpo bhoktā svayaṃ yatnena yojayet .. 14 ..
4.139.d:
इन्द्रस्थाने पुरोद्दिष्टे इन्द्रमातृकसंज्ञके ॥
तस्मिन्यष्टिं नृपो भोक्ता स्वयं यत्नेन योजयेत् ॥ 14 ॥
4.139.m: at the place of Indra designated previously, known as the shrine of Indra's mothers. / The king, as ruler, should himself diligently fit the pole therein,

4.139.s:
vastrairvicitraiḥ saṃvītāṃ piṭikālaṃkṛtāṃ tathā ..
piṭikānāṃ mahārāja kramaṃ ca kathayāmi te .. 15 ..
4.139.d:
वस्त्रैर्विचित्रैः संवीतां पिटिकालंकृतां तथा ॥
पिटिकानां महाराज क्रमं च कथयामि ते ॥ 15 ॥
4.139.m: covered with variegated cloths and decorated with baskets. / And I will tell you the sequence of the baskets, O great king.

4.139.s:
prathamaṃ lokapālākhyaṃ caturasraṃ sakarṇikam ..
yamendradhanadairyuktaṃ varuṇena samaṃ tataḥ .. 16 ..
4.139.d:
प्रथमं लोकपालाख्यं चतुरस्रं सकर्णिकम् ॥
यमेन्द्रधनदैर्युक्तं वरुणेन समं ततः ॥ 16 ॥
4.139.m: The first is called the world-protector, square and with a pericarp, / endowed with Yama, Indra, and Dhanada, and equal with Varuṇa thereafter.

4.139.s:
vṛttaṃ khaṃḍāsrakaṃ ramyaṃ dvitīyaṃ raktacūrṇitam ..
tṛtīyaṃ śvetakaṃ citramaṣṭāsra piṭakaṃ śubham .. 17 ..
4.139.d:
वृत्तं खंडास्रकं रम्यं द्वितीयं रक्तचूर्णितम् ॥
तृतीयं श्वेतकं चित्रमष्टास्र पिटकं शुभम् ॥ 17 ॥
4.139.m: The second is round, crescent-shaped, charming, and powdered with red. / The third is white, variegated, eight-sided, an auspicious basket.

4.139.s:
caturthamindragopālavṛttaṃ mātṛsamāvṛtam ..
pañcamaṃ cāṣṭakoṇaṃ tu śuklaṃ dhātuvicitritam .. 18 ..
4.139.d:
चतुर्थमिन्द्रगोपालवृत्तं मातृसमावृतम् ॥
पञ्चमं चाष्टकोणं तु शुक्लं धातुविचित्रितम् ॥ 18 ॥
4.139.m: The fourth is round like a cochineal insect and surrounded by the mothers. / The fifth has eight corners, is white, and is decorated with mineral pigments.

4.139.s:
kṛṣṇakarṇikayā ṣaṣṭhaṃ vṛttaṃ budbuda śobhitam ..
saptamaṃ cāṣṭakoṇaṃ tu śuddhaṃ vidyādharairyutam .. 19 ..
4.139.d:
कृष्णकर्णिकया षष्ठं वृत्तं बुद्बुद शोभितम् ॥
सप्तमं चाष्टकोणं तु शुद्धं विद्याधरैर्युतम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.139.m: The sixth is round with a black pericarp and adorned with bubbles. / The seventh has eight corners, is pure, and is accompanied by vidyādharas.

4.139.s:
aṣṭamaṃ piṭakaṃ vṛttaṃ varatrāsūtraveṣṭitam ..
navagrahayutaṃ dīptaṃ navamaṃ ca sacaṃḍikam .. .. 4.139.20 ..
4.139.d:
अष्टमं पिटकं वृत्तं वरत्रासूत्रवेष्टितम् ॥
नवग्रहयुतं दीप्तं नवमं च सचंडिकम् ॥ ॥ 4.139.20 ॥
4.139.m: The eighth basket is round and bound with leathern straps and cords. / The ninth is radiant, endowed with the nine planets, and has Caṇḍikā.

4.139.s:
brahmaviṣṇvīśasahitaṃ daśamaṃ śivasaṃsthitam ..
kṛṣṇamekādaśaṃ vṛttaṃ yamayuktaṃ yudhiṣṭhira .. 21 ..
4.139.d:
ब्रह्मविष्ण्वीशसहितं दशमं शिवसंस्थितम् ॥
कृष्णमेकादशं वृत्तं यमयुक्तं युधिष्ठिर ॥ 21 ॥
4.139.m: The tenth contains Śiva together with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśa. / The eleventh is black, round, and accompanied by Yama, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

4.139.s:
chātraṃ dvādaśamaṃ śuklaṃ dhvajadīrghaṃ trayodaśam ..
sakuśaṃ puṣpasragdāmaghaṃṭācāmaracarcitam .. 22 ..
4.139.d:
छात्रं द्वादशमं शुक्लं ध्वजदीर्घं त्रयोदशम् ॥
सकुशं पुष्पस्रग्दामघंटाचामरचर्चितम् ॥ 22 ॥
4.139.m: The twelfth is a white parasol; the thirteenth is long as a banner, / equipped with kuśa grass, smeared and decorated with flower garlands, bells, and chowries.

4.139.s:
bandhayitvā candrapādai rajjubhiḥ sthūṇikāṃ naraiḥ ..
śanairutthāpayetpārtha hutvā vaiśvānaraṃ dvijān .. 23 ..
4.139.d:
बन्धयित्वा चन्द्रपादै रज्जुभिः स्थूणिकां नरैः ॥
शनैरुत्थापयेत्पार्थ हुत्वा वैश्वानरं द्विजान् ॥ 23 ॥
4.139.m: Having bound the post with ropes using men at the quarter-turns of the moon, / he should raise it slowly, O son of Pṛthā, after offering oblations to the fire and [feeding] the twice-born.

4.139.s:
dakṣiṇābhiśca saṃpūjya guḍapāyasapūpakaiḥ ..
kuryānmahotsavaṃ rājā dināni nava sapta vā .. 24 ..
4.139.d:
दक्षिणाभिश्च संपूज्य गुडपायसपूपकैः ॥
कुर्यान्महोत्सवं राजा दिनानि नव सप्त वा ॥ 24 ॥
4.139.m: And after honouring [them] with priestly gifts, jaggery, milk-rice, and cakes, / the king should hold a great festival for nine or seven days,

4.139.s:
prekṣaṇīyairmahādānairnaṭaigītaiḥ kathānakaiḥ ..
cakradolādharotsargaiḥ karkeṭairmallayodhanaiḥ .. 25 ..
4.139.d:
प्रेक्षणीयैर्महादानैर्नटैगीतैः कथानकैः ॥
चक्रदोलाधरोत्सर्गैः कर्केटैर्मल्लयोधनैः ॥ 25 ॥
4.139.m: with spectacles, great gifts, actors, songs, stories, / ferris wheels, swings, abandonment of lower garments, acrobatics, wrestling bouts,

4.139.s:
veśyāṃganānarairhṛṣṭairdyūtakrīḍāmahotsavaiḥ ..
karpūravastradānaiśca saṃmānaiśca parasparam... 26 ..
4.139.d:
वेश्यांगनानरैर्हृष्टैर्द्यूतक्रीडामहोत्सवैः ॥
कर्पूरवस्त्रदानैश्च संमानैश्च परस्परम्॥। 26 ॥
4.139.m: delighted courtesans and men, great festivals of gambling games, / gifts of camphor and garments, and mutual honours.

4.139.s:
rātrau prajāgaraḥ kāryo rakṣaṇāya prayatnataḥ ..
kākolūkakapotānāṃ yena pāto na vidyate .. 27 ..
4.139.d:
रात्रौ प्रजागरः कार्यो रक्षणाय प्रयत्नतः ॥
काकोलूककपोतानां येन पातो न विद्यते ॥ 27 ॥
4.139.m: A vigil should be kept at night with effort for protection, / so that there is no alighting of crows, owls, and pigeons.

4.139.s:
kākādbhavati durbhikṣaṃ kauśikānmriyate nṛpaḥ ..
kapotācca prajānāśastato rakṣetsadodyataḥ .. 28 ..
4.139.d:
काकाद्भवति दुर्भिक्षं कौशिकान्म्रियते नृपः ॥
कपोताच्च प्रजानाशस्ततो रक्षेत्सदोद्यतः ॥ 28 ॥
4.139.m: From a crow comes famine; from an owl the king dies; / and from a pigeon comes the destruction of the subjects; therefore he should always be intent on protecting it.

4.139.s:
śaithilyādgiribhicchakraḥ pramādānnīyate yadi ..
tasmindeśe samutthānamindraketorna kārayet .. .. 29 ..
4.139.d:
शैथिल्याद्गिरिभिच्छक्रः प्रमादान्नीयते यदि ॥
तस्मिन्देशे समुत्थानमिन्द्रकेतोर्न कारयेत् ॥ ॥ 29 ॥
4.139.m: If due to slackness or negligence the mountain-cleaver's wheel is brought down, / he should not cause the raising of Indra's banner in that region

4.139.s: yāvattu nīyate sthānādanyasmādaiṃdrato dhvajaḥ .. 4.139.30 ..
4.139.d: यावत्तु नीयते स्थानादन्यस्मादैंद्रतो ध्वजः ॥ 4.139.30 ॥
4.139.m: until the banner is brought from another site sacred to Indra.

4.139.s:
iṃdradhvajasamutthānaṃ pramādānna kṛtaṃ yadi ..
tato dvādaśame varṣe kartavyaṃ nāṃtare punaḥ .. 31 ..
4.139.d:
इंद्रध्वजसमुत्थानं प्रमादान्न कृतं यदि ॥
ततो द्वादशमे वर्षे कर्तव्यं नांतरे पुनः ॥ 31 ॥
4.139.m: If the raising of Indra's banner is not performed due to negligence, / it must then be performed in the twelfth year, not in the interval between.

4.139.s:
kathaṃcidyadi vighnaḥ syādvipākaṃ me nibodha vai ..
chatrabhaṃge cchatrabhaṃgo dhvaje rāṣṭraṃ vinaśyati .. 32 ..
4.139.d:
कथंचिद्यदि विघ्नः स्याद्विपाकं मे निबोध वै ॥
छत्रभंगे च्छत्रभंगो ध्वजे राष्ट्रं विनश्यति ॥ 32 ॥
4.139.m: If somehow an obstacle should occur, learn from me the fruition: / on the breaking of the royal parasol, the royal parasol breaks [for the king]; on [the breaking of] the banner, the kingdom perishes.

4.139.s:
mastake mantravicchedo mukhe mukhyabalakṣayaḥ ..
bāhudaṃḍe vadetpīḍāṃ jaṭhare jāṭharaṃ bhayam .. 33 ..
4.139.d:
मस्तके मन्त्रविच्छेदो मुखे मुख्यबलक्षयः ॥
बाहुदंडे वदेत्पीडां जठरे जाठरं भयम् ॥ 33 ॥
4.139.m: At the crest, [it causes] the severance of counsel; at the face, the loss of principal forces; / on the crossbar, one should declare affliction; in the belly, danger to the belly.

4.139.s:
varatrāyāṃ mitranāśaḥ sthūṇikāsu padātayaḥ ..
kṣayaṃ gacchaṃti rājendra tasmādyatnātpuraṃdaram .. 34 ..
4.139.d:
वरत्रायां मित्रनाशः स्थूणिकासु पदातयः ॥
क्षयं गच्छंति राजेन्द्र तस्माद्यत्नात्पुरंदरम् ॥ 34 ॥
4.139.m: On the rope, destruction of friends; on the small posts, the infantry / go to destruction, O king of kings. Therefore, with effort, Purandara

4.139.s:
utthāpya pūjayedbhaktyā divārātramataṃdritaḥ ..
pramādātpatite bhagne gate cendradhvaje dvidhā .. 35 ..
4.139.d:
उत्थाप्य पूजयेद्भक्त्या दिवारात्रमतंद्रितः ॥
प्रमादात्पतिते भग्ने गते चेन्द्रध्वजे द्विधा ॥ 35 ॥
4.139.m: having raised, one should worship with devotion day and night, free from sluggishness. / If through negligence Indra's banner falls, breaks, or goes in two,

4.139.s:
sauvarṇaṃ raupyakaṃ kṛtvā pūrṇamutthāpayeddhvajam ..
śāṃtikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ kṛtvā dvijebhyonnaṃ pradāpayet .. 36 ..
4.139.d:
सौवर्णं रौप्यकं कृत्वा पूर्णमुत्थापयेद्ध्वजम् ॥
शांतिकं पौष्टिकं कृत्वा द्विजेभ्योन्नं प्रदापयेत् ॥ 36 ॥
4.139.m: having made [a banner] of gold or silver, one should raise a complete banner. / Having performed peaceful and nourishing rites, he should have food given to the twice-born,

4.139.s:
trapusaiḥ karkaṭībhiśca nālikeraiḥ kapitthakaiḥ ..
bījapūraiḥ sanāraṃgairbhakṣyānnairvividhaistathā .. 37 ..
4.139.d:
त्रपुसैः कर्कटीभिश्च नालिकेरैः कपित्थकैः ॥
बीजपूरैः सनारंगैर्भक्ष्यान्नैर्विविधैस्तथा ॥ 37 ॥
4.139.m: with cucumbers, melon, coconuts, and wood-apples, / with citrons accompanied by oranges, and likewise with various edible foods.

4.139.s:
naivedyādibhirabhyarcya maṃtreṇānena toṣayet ..
vajrahasta surārighna bahunetra puraṃdara ..
kṣemārthaṃ sarvalokasya pūjeyaṃ pratigṛhyatām .. 38 ..
4.139.d:
नैवेद्यादिभिरभ्यर्च्य मंत्रेणानेन तोषयेत् ॥
वज्रहस्त सुरारिघ्न बहुनेत्र पुरंदर ॥
क्षेमार्थं सर्वलोकस्य पूजेयं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.139.m: Having worshipped with food-offerings and other gifts, he should propitiate [him] with this mantra: / 'O holder of the thunderbolt, slayer of the gods' enemies, many-eyed Purandara, / for the welfare of all the world, may this worship be accepted!'

4.139.s:
śravaṇādbharaṇīṃ yāvatpūjāṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ ..
rātrau visarjayecchakraṃ maṃtreṇānena pāṃḍava .. 39 ..
4.139.d:
श्रवणाद्भरणीं यावत्पूजां कृत्वा विधानतः ॥
रात्रौ विसर्जयेच्छक्रं मंत्रेणानेन पांडव ॥ 39 ॥
4.139.m: Having performed the worship according to rule from Śravaṇā until Bharaṇī, / one should dismiss Śakra at night with this mantra, O Pāṇḍava:

4.139.s:
sārthaṃ surāsuragaṇaiḥ puraṃdaraśatakrato ..
upahāraṃ gṛhītvainaṃ mahendradhvaja gamyatām.. 4.139.40 ..
4.139.d:
सार्थं सुरासुरगणैः पुरंदरशतक्रतो ॥
उपहारं गृहीत्वैनं महेन्द्रध्वज गम्यताम्॥ 4.139.40 ॥
4.139.m: 'Together with the hosts of gods and asuras, O Purandara, O Śatakratu, / having accepted this offering, O banner of Mahendra, depart!'

4.139.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute yātrāmindraketoryudhiṣṭhira ..
parjanyaḥ kāmavarṣī syāttasminrāṣṭre na saṃśayaḥ .. 41 ..
4.139.d:
एवं यः कुरुते यात्रामिन्द्रकेतोर्युधिष्ठिर ॥
पर्जन्यः कामवर्षी स्यात्तस्मिन्राष्ट्रे न संशयः ॥ 41 ॥
4.139.m: He who thus conducts the procession of Indra's banner, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / rain will fall according to desire in his realm, there is no doubt.

4.139.s:
ītayo na pravartaṃte tasmānmṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam ..
vijitya śatrūnsamare vaśe kṛtvā mahītalam ..
bhuktvā rājyaṃ ciraṃkālamindraloke mahīyate ..42..
4.139.d:
ईतयो न प्रवर्तंते तस्मान्मृत्युकृतं भयम् ॥
विजित्य शत्रून्समरे वशे कृत्वा महीतलम् ॥
भुक्त्वा राज्यं चिरंकालमिन्द्रलोके महीयते ॥42॥
4.139.m: Plagues do not occur, nor danger caused by death; / having conquered his enemies in battle and brought the surface of the earth under control, / having enjoyed the kingdom for a long time, he is honoured in the world of Indra.

4.139.s:
rāṣṭre pure ca nagare surarājaketoryatrotsavo nṛpajanaiḥ kriyate sametya..
duṣṭopasargajanitaṃ paracakrajaṃ vā tasminbhayaṃ bhavati pārtha na kiñcideva .. 43 ..
4.139.d:
राष्ट्रे पुरे च नगरे सुरराजकेतोर्यत्रोत्सवो नृपजनैः क्रियते समेत्य॥
दुष्टोपसर्गजनितं परचक्रजं वा तस्मिन्भयं भवति पार्थ न किञ्चिदेव ॥ 43 ॥
4.139.m: In the kingdom, castle, and city where the festival of the king of gods' banner is celebrated by the royal people together, / no danger whatsoever, O Pārtha, arises there from malicious afflictions or from an enemy army.

4.139.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇa uttaraparvaṇi śrīkṛṣṇayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvāde mahendradhvajamahotsavavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonacatvāriṃśadutaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 139 .. ..
dīpālikotsavavarṇanam
4.139.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादे महेन्द्रध्वजमहोत्सववर्णनं नामैकोनचत्वारिंशदुतरशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ 139 ॥ ॥
दीपालिकोत्सववर्णनम्
4.139.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-ninth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Great Festival of Mahendra's Banner', in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Dīpālikā Festival

4.140.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
purā vāmanarūpeṇa yācayitvā dharāmimām ..
baliyajñe hariḥ sarvaṃ krāṃtavānvikramaistribhiḥ .. .. 1 ..
4.140.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
पुरा वामनरूपेण याचयित्वा धरामिमाम् ॥
बलियज्ञे हरिः सर्वं क्रांतवान्विक्रमैस्त्रिभिः ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
4.140.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / Formerly, having begged for this earth in the form of a dwarf / at Bali's sacrifice, Hari strode across all with three strides.

4.140.s:
indrāya dattavānrājyaṃ baliṃ pātālavāsinam ..
kṛtvā daityapatervāsamahorātraṃ punarnṛpa .. 2 ..
4.140.d:
इन्द्राय दत्तवान्राज्यं बलिं पातालवासिनम् ॥
कृत्वा दैत्यपतेर्वासमहोरात्रं पुनर्नृप ॥ 2 ॥
4.140.m: He gave the kingdom to Indra, making Bali an inhabitant of the netherworld; / and again, O king, [he granted] a day and a night as the dwelling of the lord of the Daityas,

4.140.s:
ekameva hi bhogārthaṃ balirājyeticihnitam ..
sarahasyaṃ tadetatte kathayāmi narottama .. 3 ..
4.140.d:
एकमेव हि भोगार्थं बलिराज्येतिचिह्नितम् ॥
सरहस्यं तदेतत्ते कथयामि नरोत्तम ॥ 3 ॥
4.140.m: a single [day] indeed marked as 'Bali's kingdom' for the sake of enjoyment. / Together with its secret, I shall relate this to you, O best of men.

4.140.s:
kārttike kṛṣṇapakṣasya pañcadaśyāṃ niśāgame ..
yatheṣṭaceṣṭā daityānāṃ rājyaṃ teṣāṃ mahītale .. 4 .. ..
4.140.d:
कार्त्तिके कृष्णपक्षस्य पञ्चदश्यां निशागमे ॥
यथेष्टचेष्टा दैत्यानां राज्यं तेषां महीतले ॥ 4 ॥ ॥
4.140.m: In Kārttika, on the fifteenth [day] of the dark fortnight, at the arrival of night, / the actions of the Daityas are according to their desire, and the kingdom on the surface of the earth belongs to them.

4.140.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
niśśeṣeṇa hṛṣīkeśa kaumudīṃ brūhi me prabho ..
kimarthaṃ dīyate dānaṃ tasyāṃ kā devatā bhavet .. 5 ..
4.140.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
निश्शेषेण हृषीकेश कौमुदीं ब्रूहि मे प्रभो ॥
किमर्थं दीयते दानं तस्यां का देवता भवेत् ॥ 5 ॥
4.140.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Speak to me completely of Kaumudī, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O lord. / For what purpose is a gift given, and who is the deity on it?

4.140.s:
kiṃsvittasyai bhaveddeyaṃ kebhyo devaṃ janārdana ..
praharṣaḥ ko'tra nirdiṣṭaḥ krīḍā kātra prakīrtitā .. 6 ..
4.140.d:
किंस्वित्तस्यै भवेद्देयं केभ्यो देवं जनार्दन ॥
प्रहर्षः कोऽत्र निर्दिष्टः क्रीडा कात्र प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 6 ॥
4.140.m: What indeed should be given to her? To whom [should gifts be given], O divine Janārdana? / What joy is prescribed here, and what sport is proclaimed here?

4.140.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
kārttike kṛṣṇapakṣe ca caturdaśyāṃ dinodaye ..
avaśyameva kartavyaṃ snānaṃ narakabhīrubhiḥ .. 7 ..
4.140.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
कार्त्तिके कृष्णपक्षे च चतुर्दश्यां दिनोदये ॥
अवश्यमेव कर्तव्यं स्नानं नरकभीरुभिः ॥ 7 ॥
4.140.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / In Kārttika, in the dark fortnight, on the fourteenth [day] at daybreak, / a bath must certainly be taken by those who fear hell.

4.140.s:
apāmārgapallavānvā bhrābhayenmastakopari ..
sītāloṣṭasamāyuktasakaṃṭakadalānvitān .. 8 ..
4.140.d:
अपामार्गपल्लवान्वा भ्राभयेन्मस्तकोपरि ॥
सीतालोष्टसमायुक्तसकंटकदलान्वितान् ॥ 8 ॥
4.140.m: Or one should cause apāmārga shoots to be waved above the head, / joined with a clod from a furrow and possessing thorny leaves:

4.140.s:
hara pāpamapāmārga bhrāmyamāṇaṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..
āpadaṃ kilbiṣaṃ cāpi mamāpahara sarvaśaḥ ..
apāmārga namastestu śarīraṃ mama śodhaya .. 9 .. ( ityapāmārga bhramaṇa mantraḥ)
4.140.d:
हर पापमपामार्ग भ्राम्यमाणं पुनःपुनः ॥
आपदं किल्बिषं चापि ममापहर सर्वशः ॥
अपामार्ग नमस्तेस्तु शरीरं मम शोधय ॥ 9 ॥ ( इत्यपामार्ग भ्रमण मन्त्रः)
4.140.m: 'Remove sin, O apāmārga, being waved again and again! / Take away completely also my misfortune and guilt! / O apāmārga, homage be to you! Purify my body!' (Thus the mantra for the waving of the apāmārga)

4.140.s:
tataśca tarpaṇaṃ kāryaṃ dharmarājasya nāmabhiḥ ..
yamāya dharmarājāya mṛtyave cāṃtakāya ca ..
vaivasvatāya kālāya sarvabhūtakṣayāya ca ..4.140.1 0..
4.140.d:
ततश्च तर्पणं कार्यं धर्मराजस्य नामभिः ॥
यमाय धर्मराजाय मृत्यवे चांतकाय च ॥
वैवस्वताय कालाय सर्वभूतक्षयाय च ॥4.140.1 0॥
4.140.m: And then water-libation should be made with the names of the King of Dharma: / 'To Yama, to the King of Dharma, to Death, and to the Ender, / to Vaivasvata, to Time, and to the Destruction of All Beings.'

4.140.s:
narakāya pradātavyo dīpaḥ saṃpūjya devatāḥ ..
tataḥ pradoṣasamaye dīpāndadyānmanoramān .. 11 ..
4.140.d:
नरकाय प्रदातव्यो दीपः संपूज्य देवताः ॥
ततः प्रदोषसमये दीपान्दद्यान्मनोरमान् ॥ 11 ॥
4.140.m: A lamp should be offered to Naraka after worshipping the deities. / Then, at twilight, one should offer charming lamps,

4.140.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ bhavaneṣu maṭheṣu ca ..
kūṭāgāreṣu caityeṣu sabhāsu ca nadīṣu ca .. 12 ..
4.140.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादीनां भवनेषु मठेषु च ॥
कूटागारेषु चैत्येषु सभासु च नदीषु च ॥ 12 ॥
4.140.m: in the dwellings and monasteries of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others, / in upper storeys, shrines, halls, and rivers,

4.140.s:
prākārodyānavāpīṣu pratolīniṣkuṭeṣu ca ..
siddhārhabuddhacāmuṃḍābhairavāyataneṣu ca ..
maṃdurāsu viviktāsu hastiśālāsu caiva hi .. 13 ..
4.140.d:
प्राकारोद्यानवापीषु प्रतोलीनिष्कुटेषु च ॥
सिद्धार्हबुद्धचामुंडाभैरवायतनेषु च ॥
मंदुरासु विविक्तासु हस्तिशालासु चैव हि ॥ 13 ॥
4.140.m: on ramparts, in pleasure-gardens and wells, in main streets and house-gardens, / in the sanctuaries of the Siddhas, the Arhats, the Buddhas, Cāmuṇḍā, and Bhairava, / and in secluded stables and elephant-stalls.

4.140.s:
evaṃ prabhātasamaye'māvāsyāyāṃ narādhipa ..
snātvā devānpitṝnbhaktyā saṃpūjyātha praṇamya ca .. 14 ..
4.140.d:
एवं प्रभातसमयेऽमावास्यायां नराधिप ॥
स्नात्वा देवान्पितॄन्भक्त्या संपूज्याथ प्रणम्य च ॥ 14 ॥
4.140.m: Thus at dawn on the new moon day, O ruler of men, / having bathed, and having worshipped the gods and ancestors with devotion and bowed,

4.140.s:
kṛtvā tu pārvaṇaṃ śrāddhaṃ dadhikṣīraghṛtādibhiḥ ..
bhojyairnānāvidhairviprānbhojayitvā kṣamāpya ca .. 15 ..
4.140.d:
कृत्वा तु पार्वणं श्राद्धं दधिक्षीरघृतादिभिः ॥
भोज्यैर्नानाविधैर्विप्रान्भोजयित्वा क्षमाप्य च ॥ 15 ॥
4.140.m: having performed the pārvaṇa-śrāddha with curds, milk, clarified butter, and the like, / and having fed the Brahmins with various kinds of foods and asked their pardon,

4.140.s:
tato'parāhṇasamaye ghoṣayennagare nṛpaḥ ..
adya rājyaṃ balerlokā yatheṣṭaṃ modyatāmiti .. 16 ..
4.140.d:
ततोऽपराह्णसमये घोषयेन्नगरे नृपः ॥
अद्य राज्यं बलेर्लोका यथेष्टं मोद्यतामिति ॥ 16 ॥
4.140.m: then in the afternoon the king should proclaim in the city: / 'Today is Bali's kingdom; let the people rejoice as they please!'

4.140.s:
lokaścāpi pare hṛṣyetsudhādhavalitājire ..
vṛkṣacandanamālāḍhyaiścarcite ca gṛhegṛhe .. 17 ..
4.140.d:
लोकश्चापि परे हृष्येत्सुधाधवलिताजिरे ॥
वृक्षचन्दनमालाढ्यैश्चर्चिते च गृहेगृहे ॥ 17 ॥
4.140.m: And the people should greatly rejoice in courtyards whitened with plaster / and in house after house decorated and smeared with garlands of tree-flowers and sandalwood,

4.140.s:
dyūtapānaratodṛptanaranārīmanohare ..
nṛtyavāditrasaṃghuṣṭe samprajvalitadīpake .. 18 ...
anyonyaprītisaṃhṛṣṭadattalābhena vai jane ..
tāṃbūlahṛṣṭa vadane kuṅkumakṣodacarcite .. 19 ..
4.140.d:
द्यूतपानरतोदृप्तनरनारीमनोहरे ॥
नृत्यवादित्रसंघुष्टे सम्प्रज्वलितदीपके ॥ 18 ॥।
अन्योन्यप्रीतिसंहृष्टदत्तलाभेन वै जने ॥
तांबूलहृष्ट वदने कुङ्कुमक्षोदचर्चिते ॥ 19 ॥
4.140.m: delightful with proud men and women engaged in gambling and drinking, / echoing with dance and musical instruments, with lamps blazing brightly, / with people rejoicing over profit given through mutual affection, / their faces delighting in betel, smeared with saffron powder,

4.140.s:
dukūlapaṭṭanepathye svarṇamāṇikyabhūṣite ..
adbhutodbhaṭaśṛṃgārapradarśitakutūhale .. 4.140.20 ..
4.140.d:
दुकूलपट्टनेपथ्ये स्वर्णमाणिक्यभूषिते ॥
अद्भुतोद्भटशृंगारप्रदर्शितकुतूहले ॥ 4.140.20 ॥
4.140.m: attired in fine cloth and silk, adorned with gold and rubies, / with curiosity displayed in wondrous and lofty amorous adornment,

4.140.s:
yuvatījanasaṃkīrṇavastrojjvalavihāriṇi ..
dīpamālākule ramye vidhvastadhvāṃtasañcaye ..
pradoṣe doṣarahite śastadoṣāgame śubhe .. 21 ..
4.140.d:
युवतीजनसंकीर्णवस्त्रोज्ज्वलविहारिणि ॥
दीपमालाकुले रम्ये विध्वस्तध्वांतसञ्चये ॥
प्रदोषे दोषरहिते शस्तदोषागमे शुभे ॥ 21 ॥
4.140.m: walking about in clothes shining brightly amidst crowds of young women, / crowded with rows of lamps, delightful, with masses of darkness destroyed, / at twilight, free of fault, at the auspicious arrival of an excellent evening.

4.140.s:
śaśipūrṇamukhābhiśca kanyābhiḥ kṣiptataṇḍulam ..
nīrājanaṃ prakartavyaṃ vṛkṣaśākhāsu dīpakaiḥ .. 22 ..
4.140.d:
शशिपूर्णमुखाभिश्च कन्याभिः क्षिप्ततण्डुलम् ॥
नीराजनं प्रकर्तव्यं वृक्षशाखासु दीपकैः ॥ 22 ॥
4.140.m: And the lustration with raw rice thrown by maidens with faces like the full moon / should be performed with lamps placed on the branches of trees.

4.140.s:
bhrāmyamāṇo nato mūrghni manujānāṃ janādhipaḥ ..
vṛkṣaśākhāṃtadīpānāṃ nirastāddarśanādvrajet ..
nīrājanaṃ tu teneha procyate vijayapradam .. 23 ..
4.140.d:
भ्राम्यमाणो नतो मूर्घ्नि मनुजानां जनाधिपः ॥
वृक्षशाखांतदीपानां निरस्ताद्दर्शनाद्व्रजेत् ॥
नीराजनं तु तेनेह प्रोच्यते विजयप्रदम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.140.m: Being circumambulated, bowed at the head, the ruler of men / should walk away from the sight of the lamps at the ends of the tree branches as they are cast off; / therefore lustration is proclaimed here to grant victory.

4.140.s:
tasmājjanena kartavyaṃ rakṣodoṣabhayāpaham ..
yātrāvihārasañcāre jayajīveti vādinā .. 24 ..
4.140.d:
तस्माज्जनेन कर्तव्यं रक्षोदोषभयापहम् ॥
यात्राविहारसञ्चारे जयजीवेति वादिना ॥ 24 ॥
4.140.m: Therefore it should be performed by the people to remove the danger of faults and demons, / as they utter 'Victory! Live long!' during processions, diversions, and promenades,

4.140.s:
kṣudropasargarahite rājacaurabhayojjhite ..
mitrasvajanasambandhisuhatpremānuraṃjite .. 25 ..
4.140.d:
क्षुद्रोपसर्गरहिते राजचौरभयोज्झिते ॥
मित्रस्वजनसम्बन्धिसुहत्प्रेमानुरंजिते ॥ 25 ॥
4.140.m: free from petty afflictions, rid of fear of kings and thieves, / delighted by the love of friends, kin, relatives, and well-wishers.

4.140.s:
tato'rddharātrasamaye svayaṃ rājā vrajetpuram ..
avalokayituṃ ramyaṃ padbhyāmeva śanaiḥśanaiḥ .. 26 ..
4.140.d:
ततोऽर्द्धरात्रसमये स्वयं राजा व्रजेत्पुरम् ॥
अवलोकयितुं रम्यं पद्भ्यामेव शनैःशनैः ॥ 26 ॥
4.140.m: Then, at midnight, the king himself should walk through the city / on foot, very slowly, to view its beauty.

4.140.s:
mahatā tūryaghoṣeṇa jvaladbhirhastadīpakaiḥ ..
kṛtaśobhāṃ purīṃ paśyetkṛtarakṣāṃ svakairnaraiḥ .. 27 ..
4.140.d:
महता तूर्यघोषेण ज्वलद्भिर्हस्तदीपकैः ॥
कृतशोभां पुरीं पश्येत्कृतरक्षां स्वकैर्नरैः ॥ 27 ॥
4.140.m: He should see the city adorned with the loud sound of musical instruments, / with blazing hand-held torches, and guarded by his own men.

4.140.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryamṛddhiṃ caivātmanaḥ śubhām ..
balirājyapramodaṃ ca tataḥ svagṛhamāvrajet .. 28 ..
4.140.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यमृद्धिं चैवात्मनः शुभाम् ॥
बलिराज्यप्रमोदं च ततः स्वगृहमाव्रजेत् ॥ 28 ॥
4.140.m: Having beheld that great wonder, his own auspicious prosperity, / and the rejoicing under Bali's rule, he should then return to his palace.

4.140.s:
evaṃ gate niśārdhe tu jane nidrārdralocane ..
tāvannagaranārībhiḥ śūrpaḍiṃḍimavādanaiḥ ..
niṣkrāmyate prahṛṣṭābhiralakṣmīḥ svagṛhāṃgaṇāt .. 29 ..
4.140.d:
एवं गते निशार्धे तु जने निद्रार्द्रलोचने ॥
तावन्नगरनारीभिः शूर्पडिंडिमवादनैः ॥
निष्क्राम्यते प्रहृष्टाभिरलक्ष्मीः स्वगृहांगणात् ॥ 29 ॥
4.140.m: When midnight has thus passed and people's eyes are heavy with sleep, / Alakṣmī is driven out from the courtyards of their homes / by the women of the city, beating winnowing baskets and drums in high delight.

4.140.s:
tataḥ prabuddhe sakale jane jātamahotsave ..
mālyadīpakahaste ca snehanirbharalocane .. 4.140.30 ..
4.140.d:
ततः प्रबुद्धे सकले जने जातमहोत्सवे ॥
माल्यदीपकहस्ते च स्नेहनिर्भरलोचने ॥ 4.140.30 ॥
4.140.m: Then, when everyone has awakened and a great festival has begun, / with garlands and lamps in hand, their eyes full of affection,

4.140.s:
veśyā vilāsinī sārdhaṃ svasti maṃgalakāriṇī ..
gṛhādgṛhaṃ vrajantī ca pādābhyaṃgapradāyinī .. 31 ..
4.140.d:
वेश्या विलासिनी सार्धं स्वस्ति मंगलकारिणी ॥
गृहाद्गृहं व्रजन्ती च पादाभ्यंगप्रदायिनी ॥ 31 ॥
4.140.m: a courtesan and a playful woman together, bringing good fortune and auspiciousness, / going from house to house and offering foot ointments,

4.140.s:
piṣṭakodvartanapare guruśuśrūṣaṇākule ..
dvijābhivādanapare sukharājyābhivīkṣaṇe .. 32 ..
4.140.d:
पिष्टकोद्वर्तनपरे गुरुशुश्रूषणाकुले ॥
द्विजाभिवादनपरे सुखराज्याभिवीक्षणे ॥ 32 ॥
4.140.m: devoted to massaging with paste, eager in serving elders, / devoted to greeting the twice-born, looking upon a happy realm,

4.140.s:
suvāsinībhyo dāne ca dīyamāne yadṛcchayā ..
yathāprabhātasamaye rājārhamānayejjanam .. 33 ..
4.140.d:
सुवासिनीभ्यो दाने च दीयमाने यदृच्छया ॥
यथाप्रभातसमये राजार्हमानयेज्जनम् ॥ 33 ॥
4.140.m: and with gifts being freely given to married women, / the king should assemble the worthy people at daybreak.

4.140.s:
sadbhāvenaiva santoṣyā devāḥ satpuruṣā dvijāḥ ..
itare cānnapānena vākpradānena paṃḍitāḥ .. 34 ..
4.140.d:
सद्भावेनैव सन्तोष्या देवाः सत्पुरुषा द्विजाः ॥
इतरे चान्नपानेन वाक्प्रदानेन पंडिताः ॥ 34 ॥
4.140.m: The gods, virtuous men, and twice-born are to be satisfied with genuine goodwill, / the others with food and drink, and the learned with gifts of speech.

4.140.s:
vastraistāṃbūladānaiśca puṣpakarpūrakuṃkumaiḥ ..
bhakṣyairuccāvacairbhojyairantaḥpuravilāsinīḥ .. 35 ..
4.140.d:
वस्त्रैस्तांबूलदानैश्च पुष्पकर्पूरकुंकुमैः ॥
भक्ष्यैरुच्चावचैर्भोज्यैरन्तःपुरविलासिनीः ॥ 35 ॥
4.140.m: With garments, gifts of betel, flowers, camphor, and saffron, / with varied cakes and foods [he should gratify] the women of the inner apartments;

4.140.s:
grāmairviṣayadānaiśca sāmaṃtanṛpatīndhanaiḥ ..
padātīnaṅgasaṃlagnāngraiveyakaṭakaiḥ svakān .. 36 ..
4.140.d:
ग्रामैर्विषयदानैश्च सामंतनृपतीन्धनैः ॥
पदातीनङ्गसंलग्नान्ग्रैवेयकटकैः स्वकान् ॥ 36 ॥
4.140.m: with villages and land grants [he should gratify] feudatory kings, with wealth [others], / and his own foot soldiers devoted to him with necklaces and bracelets.

4.140.s:
svayaṃ rājā toṣayetsa janānbhṛtyānpṛthakpṛthak ..
yathārhaṃ toṣayitvā tu tato mallanaṭānbhaṭān ..37..
4.140.d:
स्वयं राजा तोषयेत्स जनान्भृत्यान्पृथक्पृथक् ॥
यथार्हं तोषयित्वा तु ततो मल्लनटान्भटान् ॥37॥
4.140.m: The king himself should satisfy the people and his servants one by one. / Then, having rewarded wrestlers, actors, and soldiers according to their merit,

4.140.s:
vṛṣabhānmahiṣāṃścaiva yudhyamānānparaiḥ saha ..
gajānaśvāṃśca yodhāṃśca padātīnsamalaṃkṛtān ...38..
4.140.d:
वृषभान्महिषांश्चैव युध्यमानान्परैः सह ॥
गजानश्वांश्च योधांश्च पदातीन्समलंकृतान् ॥.38॥
4.140.m: bulls and buffaloes fighting with each other, / elephants, horses, warriors, and well-adorned foot soldiers,

4.140.s:
maṃcārūḍhaḥ svayaṃ paśyennaṭanartakacāraṇān ..
kruddhāpayedānayecca gomahiṣyādikaṃ tataḥ .. 39 ..
4.140.d:
मंचारूढः स्वयं पश्येन्नटनर्तकचारणान् ॥
क्रुद्धापयेदानयेच्च गोमहिष्यादिकं ततः ॥ 39 ॥
4.140.m: he should watch in person mounted on a dais, [and view] actors, dancers, and bards. / He should incite them to anger and then bring forward cows, buffaloes, and other animals.

4.140.s:
diṣṭyā kāryaṃ payojyotiruktipratyuktikā vadet ..
tatoparāhnasamaye pūrvasyāṃ diśi bhārata .. 4.140.40 ..
4.140.d:
दिष्ट्या कार्यं पयोज्योतिरुक्तिप्रत्युक्तिका वदेत् ॥
ततोपराह्नसमये पूर्वस्यां दिशि भारत ॥ 4.140.40 ॥
4.140.m: He should say congratulations, perform libations, and speak witty banter. / Then in the afternoon, O Bhārata, in the eastern direction,

4.140.s:
mārgapālīṃ prabadhnīyāttuṃgastaṃbhe'tha pādape ..
kuśakāśamayīṃ divyāṃ saṃbhave bahubhirvṛtām .. 41 ..
4.140.d:
मार्गपालीं प्रबध्नीयात्तुंगस्तंभेऽथ पादपे ॥
कुशकाशमयीं दिव्यां संभवे बहुभिर्वृताम् ॥ 41 ॥
4.140.m: he should fasten the mārgapālī to a tall pillar or a tree, / a splendid [festoon] made of kuśa and kāśa grass, surrounded by many if available.

4.140.s:
pūjayitvā gajānvājīnsārdhe yāmatraye gate ..
gāvo vṛṣāḥ samahiṣā maṃḍitā ghaṭikotkaṭāḥ .. 42 ..
4.140.d:
पूजयित्वा गजान्वाजीन्सार्धे यामत्रये गते ॥
गावो वृषाः समहिषा मंडिता घटिकोत्कटाः ॥ 42 ॥
4.140.m: Having worshipped the elephants and horses when three and a half yāmas have passed, / cows, bulls, and buffaloes are adorned, eager for the moment.

4.140.s:
kṛte home dvijendraistu gṛhṇīyānmārgapālikām ..
rāṣṭrabhojyena dhārābhiḥ sahasreṇa śatena vā ..43..
4.140.d:
कृते होमे द्विजेन्द्रैस्तु गृह्णीयान्मार्गपालिकाम् ॥
राष्ट्रभोज्येन धाराभिः सहस्रेण शतेन वा ॥43॥
4.140.m: When the homa has been performed by the foremost twice-born, one should take hold of the mārgapālikā, / with the food of the realm, in streams of a thousand or a hundred,

4.140.s:
svaśaktyapekṣayā vāpi gṛhṇīyādvāmabhojanaiḥ ..
mātuḥ kulaṃ pitṛkulamātmānaṃ sahabaṃdhubhiḥ .. 44..
4.140.d:
स्वशक्त्यपेक्षया वापि गृह्णीयाद्वामभोजनैः ॥
मातुः कुलं पितृकुलमात्मानं सहबंधुभिः ॥ 44॥
4.140.m: or according to one's own capacity, or take hold of it with offerings of food. / He who offers the mārgapālī delivers

4.140.s:
saṃtārayetsa sakalaṃ mārgapālīṃ dadāti yaḥ ..
nīrājanaṃ ca tatraiva kāryaṃ rājñe jayapradam ..45..
4.140.d:
संतारयेत्स सकलं मार्गपालीं ददाति यः ॥
नीराजनं च तत्रैव कार्यं राज्ञे जयप्रदम् ॥45॥
4.140.m: the maternal family, the paternal family, and himself together with his kinsmen. / Right there, the wave-offering of lights bringing victory should be performed for the king.

4.140.s:
mārgapālītalenetthaṃ hayā gāvo gajā vṛṣāḥ ..
rājāno rājaputrāśca brāhmaṇā śūdrajātayaḥ .. 46 ..
4.140.d:
मार्गपालीतलेनेत्थं हया गावो गजा वृषाः ॥
राजानो राजपुत्राश्च ब्राह्मणा शूद्रजातयः ॥ 46 ॥
4.140.m: Thus beneath the mārgapālī horses, cows, elephants, bulls, / kings, princes, brāhmaṇas, and śūdras,

4.140.s:
mārgapālīṃ samullaṃghya nīrujaḥ syātsukhī sadā ..
kṛtvaitatsarvameveha rātrau daityapaterbaleḥ .. .. 47 ..
4.140.d:
मार्गपालीं समुल्लंघ्य नीरुजः स्यात्सुखी सदा ॥
कृत्वैतत्सर्वमेवेह रात्रौ दैत्यपतेर्बलेः ॥ ॥ 47 ॥
4.140.m: passing under the mārgapālī, will be free from illness and always happy. / Having done all this here, at night a man should perform

4.140.s:
pūjāṃ kuryānnaraḥ sākṣādbhūmau maṃḍalake kṛte ..
balimālikhya daityendraṃ varṇakaiḥ paṃcaraṃgakaiḥ .. 48 ..
4.140.d:
पूजां कुर्यान्नरः साक्षाद्भूमौ मंडलके कृते ॥
बलिमालिख्य दैत्येन्द्रं वर्णकैः पंचरंगकैः ॥ 48 ॥
4.140.m: the worship of Bali, king of the Daityas, directly upon the ground on a maṇḍala, / having drawn Bali, the Daitya lord, with five-coloured powders,

4.140.s:
sarvābharaṇasaṃpūrṇaṃ viṃdhyāvalyā sahāsitam..
kūṣmāṃḍabāṇajaṃghorumuradānavasaṃvṛtam .. 49 ..
4.140.d:
सर्वाभरणसंपूर्णं विंध्यावल्या सहासितम्॥
कूष्मांडबाणजंघोरुमुरदानवसंवृतम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.140.m: resplendent with all ornaments, seated with Vindhyāvalī, / surrounded by Kūṣmāṇḍa, Bāṇa, Jaṅgha, Uru, and Mura, the Dānavas,

4.140.s:
saṃpūrṇahṛṣṭavadanaṃ kirīṭotkaṭakuṇḍalam ..
dvibhujaṃ daityarājānaṃ kārayitvā nṛpaḥ svayam..4.140.50..
4.140.d:
संपूर्णहृष्टवदनं किरीटोत्कटकुण्डलम् ॥
द्विभुजं दैत्यराजानं कारयित्वा नृपः स्वयम्॥4.140.50॥
4.140.m: his face filled with joy, wearing a diadem and prominent earrings. / Having had the two-armed king of the Daityas made, the king himself,

4.140.s:
gṛhasya madhye śālāyāṃ viśālāyāṃ tato'rcayet ..
bhrātṛmaṃtrijanaiḥ sārddhaṃ saṃtuṣṭo vaṃdibhiḥ stutaḥ .. 51 ..
4.140.d:
गृहस्य मध्ये शालायां विशालायां ततोऽर्चयेत् ॥
भ्रातृमंत्रिजनैः सार्द्धं संतुष्टो वंदिभिः स्तुतः ॥ 51 ॥
4.140.m: content and praised by bards, should then worship him in the middle of the house / inside a spacious hall, accompanied by his brothers and ministers,

4.140.s:
kamalaiḥ kumudaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kahlārai raktakotpalaiḥ ..
gandhadhūpānnanaivedyairakṣatairguḍapūpakaiḥ ..52..
4.140.d:
कमलैः कुमुदैः पुष्पैः कह्लारै रक्तकोत्पलैः ॥
गन्धधूपान्ननैवेद्यैरक्षतैर्गुडपूपकैः ॥52॥
4.140.m: with lotuses, white water-lilies, kahlāra flowers, and red night-lotuses, / with perfumes, incense, food offerings, unbroken grain, and treacle cakes,

4.140.s:
madyamāṃsasurālehyadīpavartyupahārakaiḥ ..
maṃtreṇānena rājendra samaṃtrī sapurohitaḥ .. 53 ..
4.140.d:
मद्यमांससुरालेह्यदीपवर्त्युपहारकैः ॥
मंत्रेणानेन राजेन्द्र समंत्री सपुरोहितः ॥ 53 ॥
4.140.m: with gifts of wine, meat, liquor, sweetmeats, lamps, and wicks, / with this mantra, O king of kings, together with his minister and chaplain:

4.140.s:
balirāja namastubhyaṃ virocanasuta prabho ..
bhaviṣyendrasurārāte pūjeyaṃ pratigṛhyatām .. 54 ..
4.140.d:
बलिराज नमस्तुभ्यं विरोचनसुत प्रभो ॥
भविष्येन्द्रसुराराते पूजेयं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ॥ 54 ॥
4.140.m: “O King Bali, homage to you, son of Virocana, O lord, / future Indra, enemy of the gods! Please accept this worship.”

4.140.s:
evaṃ pūjāṃ nṛpaḥ kṛtvā rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ tataḥ ..
kārayetprekṣaṇīyādi naṭakṣatrakathānakaiḥ .. 55 ..
4.140.d:
एवं पूजां नृपः कृत्वा रात्रौ जागरणं ततः ॥
कारयेत्प्रेक्षणीयादि नटक्षत्रकथानकैः ॥ 55 ॥
4.140.m: Having thus performed the worship, the king should then hold a vigil at night / with spectacles and tales of actors and kṣatriyas.

4.140.s:
lokaścāpi gṛhasyāṃte śayyāyāṃ śuklataṃḍulaiḥ ..
saṃsthāpya balirājānaṃ phalaiḥ puṣpaiśca pūjayet .. 56 ..
4.140.d:
लोकश्चापि गृहस्यांते शय्यायां शुक्लतंडुलैः ॥
संस्थाप्य बलिराजानं फलैः पुष्पैश्च पूजयेत् ॥ 56 ॥
4.140.m: The people too should install King Bali on a couch in the interior of their homes / with white rice, and worship him with fruits and flowers.

4.140.s:
balimuddiśya dīyaṃte dānāni kurunandana ..
yāni tānyakṣayāṇyāhurmayaivaṃ saṃpradarśitam .. 57 ..
4.140.d:
बलिमुद्दिश्य दीयंते दानानि कुरुनन्दन ॥
यानि तान्यक्षयाण्याहुर्मयैवं संप्रदर्शितम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.140.m: Gifts given dedicated to Bali, O joy of the Kurus, / are said to be imperishable; this has been demonstrated by me.

4.140.s:
yadasyāṃ dīyate dānaṃ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu ..
tadakṣayaṃ bhavetsarvaṃ viṣṇoḥ prītikaraṃ param .. 58 ..
4.140.d:
यदस्यां दीयते दानं स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु ॥
तदक्षयं भवेत्सर्वं विष्णोः प्रीतिकरं परम् ॥ 58 ॥
4.140.m: Whatever gift is given on this day, whether little or much, / all that becomes imperishable and brings supreme delight to Viṣṇu.

4.140.s:
viṣṇunā vasudhā labdhā prītena balaye punaḥ ..
upakārakaro dattaścāsurāṇāṃ mahotsavaḥ .. 59 ..
4.140.d:
विष्णुना वसुधा लब्धा प्रीतेन बलये पुनः ॥
उपकारकरो दत्तश्चासुराणां महोत्सवः ॥ 59 ॥
4.140.m: When the earth was gained by Viṣṇu, he, being pleased, granted / to Bali once again this great festival of the Asuras, which confers benefits.

4.140.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti rājendra pravṛttā kaumudī punaḥ ..
sarvopadravavidrāvi sarvavighnavināśinī ..4.140.60..
4.140.d:
ततः प्रभृति राजेन्द्र प्रवृत्ता कौमुदी पुनः ॥
सर्वोपद्रवविद्रावि सर्वविघ्नविनाशिनी ॥4.140.60॥
4.140.m: Ever since then, O king of kings, Kaumudī has been observed again, / driving away all afflictions and destroying all obstacles,

4.140.s:
lokaśokaharī kāmyā dhanapuṣṭisukhāvahā ..
kuśabdena mahī jñeyā mudī harṣe tataḥ param .. 61 ..
4.140.d:
लोकशोकहरी काम्या धनपुष्टिसुखावहा ॥
कुशब्देन मही ज्ञेया मुदी हर्षे ततः परम् ॥ 61 ॥
4.140.m: dispelling the sorrow of the people, desirable, bringing wealth, prosperity, and happiness. / By the word 'ku' the earth is to be understood, and thereafter 'mudī' signifies joy;

4.140.s:
dhātujñairnaigamajñaiśca tenaiṣā kaumudī smṛtā ..
kau modante janā yasyāṃ nānābhāvaiḥ parasparā .. 62 ..
4.140.d:
धातुज्ञैर्नैगमज्ञैश्च तेनैषा कौमुदी स्मृता ॥
कौ मोदन्ते जना यस्यां नानाभावैः परस्परा ॥ 62 ॥
4.140.m: therefore it is remembered as Kaumudī by knowers of roots and knowers of the Vedas. / On it people rejoice (modante) mutually on earth (kau) with various sentiments;

4.140.s:
hṛṣṭāstuṣṭāḥ sukhāyattāstenaiṣā kaumudī smṛtā ..
kumudāni baleryasmāddīyante'syāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .. 63 ..
4.140.d:
हृष्टास्तुष्टाः सुखायत्तास्तेनैषा कौमुदी स्मृता ॥
कुमुदानि बलेर्यस्माद्दीयन्तेऽस्यां युधिष्ठिर ॥ 63 ॥
4.140.m: delighted, contented, and possessing happiness, therefore it is remembered as Kaumudī. / Because white water-lilies (kumuda) are offered on it to Bali, O Yudhiṣṭhira,

4.140.s:
arthārthe pārtha bhūmau ca tenaiṣā kaumudī smṛtā ..
ekamevamahorātraṃ varṣe varṣe viśāṃpate .. 64 ..
4.140.d:
अर्थार्थे पार्थ भूमौ च तेनैषा कौमुदी स्मृता ॥
एकमेवमहोरात्रं वर्षे वर्षे विशांपते ॥ 64 ॥
4.140.m: and on earth (bhūmau) for the sake of wealth, O son of Pṛthā, therefore it is remembered as Kaumudī. / Thus for a single day and night each year, O ruler of the people,

4.140.s:
dattaṃ dānavarājasya ādarśamiva bhūtale ..
yaḥ karoti nṛpo rāṣṭraṃ tasya vyādhibhayaṃ kutaḥ .. 65 ..
4.140.d:
दत्तं दानवराजस्य आदर्शमिव भूतले ॥
यः करोति नृपो राष्ट्रं तस्य व्याधिभयं कुतः ॥ 65 ॥
4.140.m: it was given to the Dānava king as a mirror upon the surface of the earth. / For the king who observes it in his realm, whence can fear of disease come?

4.140.s:
kuta īti bhayaṃ tatra nāsti mṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam ..
subhikṣaṃ kṣemamārogyaṃ sarvasampada uttamāḥ .. 66 ..
4.140.d:
कुत ईति भयं तत्र नास्ति मृत्युकृतं भयम् ॥
सुभिक्षं क्षेममारोग्यं सर्वसम्पद उत्तमाः ॥ 66 ॥
4.140.m: Whence can fear of crop pestilence arise there? There is no fear caused by death. / There is abundance of food, safety, health, and all the highest forms of prosperity.

4.140.s:
nīrujaśca janāḥ sarve sarvopadravavarjitāḥ ..
kaumudīkaraṇādrājanbhavatīha mahītale .. 67 ..
4.140.d:
नीरुजश्च जनाः सर्वे सर्वोपद्रववर्जिताः ॥
कौमुदीकरणाद्राजन्भवतीह महीतले ॥ 67 ॥
4.140.m: All the people are free from illness and rid of all afflictions, / O king, on the surface of the earth, from performing Kaumudī.

4.140.s:
yo yādṛśena bhāvena tiṣṭhatyasyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira ..
harṣadainyādirūpeṇa tasya varṣaṃ prayāti hi .. 68 ..
4.140.d:
यो यादृशेन भावेन तिष्ठत्यस्यां युधिष्ठिर ॥
हर्षदैन्यादिरूपेण तस्य वर्षं प्रयाति हि ॥ 68 ॥
4.140.m: In whatever state of mind one remains on this day, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / in the form of joy, misery, or the like, indeed such does his whole year pass.

4.140.s:
rudite roditi varṣaṃ hṛṣṭo varṣaṃ prahṛṣyati ..
bhuktau bhoktā bhavedvarṣaṃ svasthaḥ svastho bhavediti .. 69 ..
4.140.d:
रुदिते रोदिति वर्षं हृष्टो वर्षं प्रहृष्यति ॥
भुक्तौ भोक्ता भवेद्वर्षं स्वस्थः स्वस्थो भवेदिति ॥ 69 ॥
4.140.m: If he weeps, he weeps for a year; if delighted, he rejoices for a year; / if feasting, he becomes a feaster for a year; if healthy, he remains healthy. So it is.

4.140.s:
tasmātprahṛṣṭaistuṣṭaiśca kartavyā kaumudī naraiḥ ..
vaiṣṇavī dānavī ceyaṃ tithiḥ paitrī yudhiṣṭhira .. 4.140.70 ..
4.140.d:
तस्मात्प्रहृष्टैस्तुष्टैश्च कर्तव्या कौमुदी नरैः ॥
वैष्णवी दानवी चेयं तिथिः पैत्री युधिष्ठिर ॥ 4.140.70 ॥
4.140.m: Therefore, the Kaumudī festival should be observed by men full of joy and satisfaction. / This lunar day, O Yudhiṣṭhira, belongs to Viṣṇu, belongs to the Dānavas, and belongs to the ancestors.

4.140.s:
upaśamitameghanādaṃ prajvalitadaśānanaṃ ramitarāmam ..
rāmāyaṇamiva subhagaṃ dīpadinaṃ haratu vo duritam .. 71 ..
4.140.d:
उपशमितमेघनादं प्रज्वलितदशाननं रमितरामम् ॥
रामायणमिव सुभगं दीपदिनं हरतु वो दुरितम् ॥ 71 ॥
4.140.m: Having quelled the roar of clouds, with the ten quarters ablaze, delighting Rāma— / charming like the Rāmāyaṇa, which silenced Meghanāda, burned Daśānana, and delighted Rāma—may the day of lamps dispel your misfortune.

4.140.s:
kūṣmāṇḍādānaramyaṃ kuvalayakhaṇḍaiśca dhātukābhadram ..
śaradiva harigatanidraṃ dīpadinaṃ haratu vo duritam ..72..
4.140.d:
कूष्माण्डादानरम्यं कुवलयखण्डैश्च धातुकाभद्रम् ॥
शरदिव हरिगतनिद्रं दीपदिनं हरतु वो दुरितम् ॥72॥
4.140.m: Delightful with the giving of winter melons, auspicious with mineral pigments and lotus blossoms, / as autumn awakens Hari from slumber, so may the day of lamps dispel your misfortune.

4.140.s:
dīpotsave janitasarvajanapramodāṃ kurvaṃti ye sumanaso balirājapūjām ..
dānopabhogasukhavṛddhiśatākulānāṃ harṣeṇa varṣamiha pārthiva yāti teṣām ..73..
navagrahalakṣahomavidhivarṇanam
4.140.d:
दीपोत्सवे जनितसर्वजनप्रमोदां कुर्वंति ये सुमनसो बलिराजपूजाम् ॥
दानोपभोगसुखवृद्धिशताकुलानां हर्षेण वर्षमिह पार्थिव याति तेषाम् ॥73॥
नवग्रहलक्षहोमविधिवर्णनम्
4.140.m:
Those who, with delighted minds, perform the worship of King Bali during the festival of lamps, bringing joy to all people, / spend their year here in joy, O king, filled with hundreds of increases in charity, enjoyment, and happiness.
Description of the procedure for the hundred-thousand fire oblation to the nine planets

4.141.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
kathayasva mahābhāga sarvajño hyasi yādava ..
sarvakāmāptaye kṛtyaṃ kathaṃ śāṃtikapauṣṭikam ..1..
4.141.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
कथयस्व महाभाग सर्वज्ञो ह्यसि यादव ॥
सर्वकामाप्तये कृत्यं कथं शांतिकपौष्टिकम् ॥1॥
4.141.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Speak, O exalted one, for you are omniscient, O Yādava! / What rite brings about pacification and nourishment for the attainment of all desires?

4.141.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca.. ..
śrīkāmaḥ śāntikāmo vā grahayajñaṃ samārabhet ..
dṛṣṭyāyuḥ puṣṭikāmo vā tathaivābhicaranpunaḥ .. 2 ..
4.141.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच॥ ॥
श्रीकामः शान्तिकामो वा ग्रहयज्ञं समारभेत् ॥
दृष्ट्यायुः पुष्टिकामो वा तथैवाभिचरन्पुनः ॥ 2 ॥
4.141.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / One who desires prosperity, or one who desires pacification, should undertake a sacrifice to the planets, / or one who desires sight, longevity, or nourishment, or likewise one who performs sorcery.

4.141.s:
sarvaśāstrāṇyanukramya saṃkṣipya granthavistaram ..
grahaśāṃtiṃ pravakṣyāmi purāṇaśrutibhāṣitām ..3..
4.141.d:
सर्वशास्त्राण्यनुक्रम्य संक्षिप्य ग्रन्थविस्तरम् ॥
ग्रहशांतिं प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणश्रुतिभाषिताम् ॥3॥
4.141.m: Having reviewed all the scriptures and condensed the vastness of the treatises, / I shall proclaim the pacification of the planets as taught in the Purāṇas and the Vedas.

4.141.s:
puṇye'hni viprakathite kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam ..
grahāngrahādhidevāṃśca sthāpya homaṃ samārabhet .. 4 ..
4.141.d:
पुण्येऽह्नि विप्रकथिते कृत्वा ब्राह्मणवाचनम् ॥
ग्रहान्ग्रहाधिदेवांश्च स्थाप्य होमं समारभेत् ॥ 4 ॥
4.141.m: On an auspicious day declared by a Brahmin, having performed the blessing recitation by Brahmins, / and having installed the planets and their presiding deities, one should commence the fire oblation.

4.141.s:
grahayajñastridhā proktaḥ purāṇaśrutikovidaiḥ ..
prathamo'yutahomaḥ syāllakṣahomastataḥ param .. 5 ..
4.141.d:
ग्रहयज्ञस्त्रिधा प्रोक्तः पुराणश्रुतिकोविदैः ॥
प्रथमोऽयुतहोमः स्याल्लक्षहोमस्ततः परम् ॥ 5 ॥
4.141.m: The sacrifice to the planets is declared to be threefold by those skilled in the Purāṇas and the Vedas: / the first is an oblation of ten thousand, and beyond that is an oblation of a hundred thousand.

4.141.s:
tṛtīyaḥ koṭihomastu sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ ..
ayutenāhutīnāṃ ca navagrahamakhaḥ smṛtaḥ ..6..
4.141.d:
तृतीयः कोटिहोमस्तु सर्वकामफलप्रदः ॥
अयुतेनाहुतीनां च नवग्रहमखः स्मृतः ॥6॥
4.141.m: The third is an oblation of ten million, which bestows the fruit of all desires; / and a sacrifice to the nine planets is traditionally known to consist of ten thousand offerings.

4.141.s:
tasya tāvadvidhiṃ vakṣye purāṇaśrutibhāṣitam ..
gartasyottarapūrveṇa vitastidvayavistṛtām .. 7 ..
4.141.d:
तस्य तावद्विधिं वक्ष्ये पुराणश्रुतिभाषितम् ॥
गर्तस्योत्तरपूर्वेण वितस्तिद्वयविस्तृताम् ॥ 7 ॥
4.141.m: I shall first explain its procedure as taught in the Purāṇas and the Vedas. / To the northeast of the pit, measuring two spans in width,

4.141.s:
kuryādvidhānato vediṃ vitastyucchrayasaṃyutām ..
saṃsthāpanāya devānāṃ caturasrāmudakplavām .. 8 ..
4.141.d:
कुर्याद्विधानतो वेदिं वितस्त्युच्छ्रयसंयुताम् ॥
संस्थापनाय देवानां चतुरस्रामुदक्प्लवाम् ॥ 8 ॥
4.141.m: one should construct an altar according to rule, with a height of one span, / four-cornered and sloping to the north, for the installation of the deities.

4.141.s:
agnipraṇayanaṃ kṛtvā tasyāmāvāhayetsurān ..
devānāṃ tatra saṃsthāpyā viṃśatirdvādaśādhikā .. 9 ..
4.141.d:
अग्निप्रणयनं कृत्वा तस्यामावाहयेत्सुरान् ॥
देवानां तत्र संस्थाप्या विंशतिर्द्वादशाधिका ॥ 9 ॥
4.141.m: Having brought forward the sacrificial fire, one should invoke the gods upon it. / Thirty-two deities are to be installed there:

4.141.s:
sūryaḥ somo mahīputro budho jīvaḥ sitorkajaḥ ..
rāhuḥ keturiti proktā grahālokahitāvahāḥ .. 4.141.10 ..
4.141.d:
सूर्यः सोमो महीपुत्रो बुधो जीवः सितोर्कजः ॥
राहुः केतुरिति प्रोक्ता ग्रहालोकहितावहाः ॥ 4.141.10 ॥
4.141.m: Sūrya, Soma, Mahīputra, Budha, Jīva, Sita, the son of Arka, / Rāhu, and Ketu are declared to be the planets that bring welfare to the worlds.

4.141.s:
tāmrakātsphaṭikādraktacandanātsvarṇajāvubhau ..
rajatādāyasāccaiva grahāḥ kāryāḥ kramādamī .. 11 ..
4.141.d:
ताम्रकात्स्फटिकाद्रक्तचन्दनात्स्वर्णजावुभौ ॥
रजतादायसाच्चैव ग्रहाः कार्याः क्रमादमी ॥ 11 ॥
4.141.m: From copper, from crystal, from red sandalwood, two from gold, / from silver, and from iron—these planets should be made respectively [from these materials].

4.141.s:
madhye tu bhāskaraṃ vidyāllohitaṃ dakṣiṇena tu ..
uttareṇa guruṃ vidyādbudhaṃ pūrvottareṇa tu .. 12 ..
4.141.d:
मध्ये तु भास्करं विद्याल्लोहितं दक्षिणेन तु ॥
उत्तरेण गुरुं विद्याद्बुधं पूर्वोत्तरेण तु ॥ 12 ॥
4.141.m: One should know the Sun to be in the center, Mars to the south, / Jupiter to the north, and Mercury to the northeast;

4.141.s:
pūrveṇa bhārgavaṃ vidyātsomaṃ dakṣiṇapūrvake ..
paścimottarataḥ ketuṃ sthāpayecchuklataṃḍulaiḥ .. 13 ..
4.141.d:
पूर्वेण भार्गवं विद्यात्सोमं दक्षिणपूर्वके ॥
पश्चिमोत्तरतः केतुं स्थापयेच्छुक्लतंडुलैः ॥ 13 ॥
4.141.m: one should know Venus to the east, Soma to the southeast, / and one should install Ketu to the northwest with white rice grains.

4.141.s:
rājāmātyānmahārāja taṃḍulaiḥ sthāpayedatha ..
bhāskarasyeśvaraṃ vidyādumāṃ ca śaśinastathā .. 14 ..
4.141.d:
राजामात्यान्महाराज तंडुलैः स्थापयेदथ ॥
भास्करस्येश्वरं विद्यादुमां च शशिनस्तथा ॥ 14 ॥
4.141.m: Then, O great king, one should install the kings and ministers with rice grains. / One should know Īśvara as the deity of the Sun, and Umā as that of the Moon,

4.141.s:
skandamaṅgārakasyāpi budhasya ca tathā harim ..
brahmāṇaṃ ca gurorvidyācchukrasyāpi śacīpatim .. .. 15 ..
4.141.d:
स्कन्दमङ्गारकस्यापि बुधस्य च तथा हरिम् ॥
ब्रह्माणं च गुरोर्विद्याच्छुक्रस्यापि शचीपतिम् ॥ ॥ 15 ॥
4.141.m: Skanda as that of Mars, and likewise Hari as that of Mercury, / Brahmā as that of Jupiter, and Śacī's lord as that of Venus,

4.141.s:
śanaiścarasya tu yamaṃ rāhoḥ kālaṃ tathaiva ca ..
ketostu citraguptaṃ tu sarveṣāmeva devatāḥ .. 16 ..
4.141.d:
शनैश्चरस्य तु यमं राहोः कालं तथैव च ॥
केतोस्तु चित्रगुप्तं तु सर्वेषामेव देवताः ॥ 16 ॥
4.141.m: Yama as that of Saturn, and likewise Kāla as that of Rāhu, / and Citragupta as that of Ketu: these are the deities of all [the planets].

4.141.s:
agnirāpaḥ kṣitirviṣṇurindraḥ sauvarṇadevatāḥ ..
prajāpatiśca sūryaśca brahmā pratyadhidevatāḥ ..17..
4.141.d:
अग्निरापः क्षितिर्विष्णुरिन्द्रः सौवर्णदेवताः ॥
प्रजापतिश्च सूर्यश्च ब्रह्मा प्रत्यधिदेवताः ॥17॥
4.141.m: Agni, the Waters, Earth, Viṣṇu, and Indra are the golden deities. / Prajāpati, Sūrya, and Brahmā are the secondary presiding deities.

4.141.s:
vināyakaṃ tathā durgāṃ vāyumākāśameva ca ..
sāvitrīṃ ca tathā lakṣmīmumāṃ ca sahabhartṛkām .. .. 18 ..
4.141.d:
विनायकं तथा दुर्गां वायुमाकाशमेव च ॥
सावित्रीं च तथा लक्ष्मीमुमां च सहभर्तृकाम् ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
4.141.m: Vināyaka, likewise Durgā, Vāyu, and Space, / Sāvitrī, and likewise Lakṣmī, and Umā together with her consort,

4.141.s:
āvāhayedvyāhṛtibhistathaivāśvikumārakau ..
saṃsmaredraktamādityamaṃgārakasamanvitam .. 19 ..
4.141.d:
आवाहयेद्व्याहृतिभिस्तथैवाश्विकुमारकौ ॥
संस्मरेद्रक्तमादित्यमंगारकसमन्वितम् ॥ 19 ॥
4.141.m: and likewise the two Aśvins one should invoke with the sacred utterances. / One should meditate on the Sun as red, together with Mars;

4.141.s:
somaśukrau yathāśvetau budhajīvau ca piṅga lau ..
maṃdarāhū tathā kṛṣṇau dhūmraṃ ketuguṇaṃ viduḥ .. 4.141.20 ..
4.141.d:
सोमशुक्रौ यथाश्वेतौ बुधजीवौ च पिङ्ग लौ ॥
मंदराहू तथा कृष्णौ धूम्रं केतुगुणं विदुः ॥ 4.141.20 ॥
4.141.m: the Moon and Venus are white, Mercury and Jupiter are yellowish-brown, / Saturn and Rāhu are black, and they know the quality of Ketu to be smoky.

4.141.s:
grahavarṇāni deyāni vāsāṃsi kusumāni ca ..
gaṃdhāśca balayaścaiva dhūpā guggulapūrvakāḥ .. .. 21 ..
4.141.d:
ग्रहवर्णानि देयानि वासांसि कुसुमानि च ॥
गंधाश्च बलयश्चैव धूपा गुग्गुलपूर्वकाः ॥ ॥ 21 ॥
4.141.m: Garments and flowers corresponding to the colors of the planets should be offered, / as well as perfumes, offerings, and incenses headed by bdellium.

4.141.s:
guḍaudanaṃ raverdadyātsomāya ghṛtapāyasam ..
aṃgārakāya saṃyāvaṃ budhāya kṣīraṣaṣṭikam .. 22 ..
4.141.d:
गुडौदनं रवेर्दद्यात्सोमाय घृतपायसम् ॥
अंगारकाय संयावं बुधाय क्षीरषष्टिकम् ॥ 22 ॥
4.141.m: One should give jaggery-rice to the Sun, milk-rice with ghee to the Moon, / a sweet confection of wheat to Mars, and milk cooked with sixty-day rice to Mercury.

4.141.s:
dadhyannaṃ gurave dadyācchakrāya tu ghṛtaudanam ..
śanaiścarāya kṛśaraṃ meṣamāṃsaṃ tu rāhave .. 23 ..
4.141.d:
दध्यन्नं गुरवे दद्याच्छक्राय तु घृतौदनम् ॥
शनैश्चराय कृशरं मेषमांसं तु राहवे ॥ 23 ॥
4.141.m: One should give curd-rice to Jupiter, and rice with ghee to Venus, / a dish of rice and lentils to Saturn, and ram's meat to Rāhu,

4.141.s:
citraudanaṃ ketave ca sarvānbhakṣyairathārcayet ..
prāguttareṇa tasmācca dadhyakṣatavibhūṣitam .. 24 ..
4.141.d:
चित्रौदनं केतवे च सर्वान्भक्ष्यैरथार्चयेत् ॥
प्रागुत्तरेण तस्माच्च दध्यक्षतविभूषितम् ॥ 24 ॥
4.141.m: and variegated rice to Ketu; and then one should worship them all with eatables. / To the northeast of that, [one should place an unblemished jar] adorned with curd and unbroken rice,

4.141.s:
cūta pallavasaṃpannaṃ phalavastrayugānvitam ..
pañcaratnasamāyuktaṃ pañcabhaṃgayutaṃ tathā .. 25 ..
4.141.d:
चूत पल्लवसंपन्नं फलवस्त्रयुगान्वितम् ॥
पञ्चरत्नसमायुक्तं पञ्चभंगयुतं तथा ॥ 25 ॥
4.141.m: provided with mango shoots, accompanied by fruit and a pair of cloths, / endowed with the five jewels, and likewise furnished with the five leaves;

4.141.s:
sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kuṃbhaṃ varuṇaṃ tatra vinyaset ..
gaṃgāyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ samudrāśca sarāṃsi ca .. 26 ..
4.141.d:
स्थापयेदव्रणं कुंभं वरुणं तत्र विन्यसेत् ॥
गंगायाः सरितः सर्वाः समुद्राश्च सरांसि च ॥ 26 ॥
4.141.m: one should place an unblemished water jar, and install Varuṇa in it. / All the rivers [beginning with] the Gaṅgā, the oceans, and the lakes,

4.141.s:
gajāśvarathyāvalmīkātsaṃgamāddhṛdagokulāt ..
mṛdamānīya rājendra sarvauṣadhijalānvitām .. 27 ..
4.141.d:
गजाश्वरथ्यावल्मीकात्संगमाद्धृदगोकुलात् ॥
मृदमानीय राजेन्द्र सर्वौषधिजलान्विताम् ॥ 27 ॥
4.141.m: having brought earth from an elephant-track, a horse-track, an anthill, a confluence, a lake, and a cowpen, O lord of kings, / combined with water containing all medicinal herbs,

4.141.s:
snānārthaṃ vinyasettatra yajamānasya dharmavit ..
sarve samudrāḥ saritaḥ saraḥ prasravaṇāni ca .. 28 ..
4.141.d:
स्नानार्थं विन्यसेत्तत्र यजमानस्य धर्मवित् ॥
सर्वे समुद्राः सरितः सरः प्रस्रवणानि च ॥ 28 ॥
4.141.m: the one who knows dharma should place it there for the bath of the patron of the sacrifice. / "May all the oceans, rivers, lakes, and waterfalls

4.141.s:
āyāṃtu yajamānasya duritakṣayakārakāḥ ..
evamāvāhayitvā tānsarvānnṛpatisattama .. 29 ..
4.141.d:
आयांतु यजमानस्य दुरितक्षयकारकाः ॥
एवमावाहयित्वा तान्सर्वान्नृपतिसत्तम ॥ 29 ॥
4.141.m: come to destroy the misfortunes of the patron of the sacrifice!" / Having thus invoked them all, O best of monarchs,

4.141.s:
homaṃ samārabhetsarpiryavavrīhitilādinā ..
arkaḥ palāśakhadirau hyapāmārgo'tha pippalaḥ .. 4.141.30 ..
4.141.d:
होमं समारभेत्सर्पिर्यवव्रीहितिलादिना ॥
अर्कः पलाशखदिरौ ह्यपामार्गोऽथ पिप्पलः ॥ 4.141.30 ॥
4.141.m: one should commence the oblation with ghee, barley, rice, sesame, and other substances. / Calotropis, palāśa, and khadira, then apāmārga, then pippala,

4.141.s:
uduṃbara śamīdūrvākuśāśca samidhaḥ kramāt ..
ekaikasya cāṣṭaśatamaṣṭāviṃśati vā punaḥ .. 31 ..
4.141.d:
उदुंबर शमीदूर्वाकुशाश्च समिधः क्रमात् ॥
एकैकस्य चाष्टशतमष्टाविंशति वा पुनः ॥ 31 ॥
4.141.m: udumbara, śamī, dūrvā grass, and kuśa grass are the kindling sticks respectively. / For each one, one hundred and eight, or twenty-eight,

4.141.s:
hotavyā madhusarpibhyāṃ dadhnā vā pāyasena vā ..
prādeśamātrā ṛjavo viśākhā viphalāḥ śubhāḥ .. 32 ..
4.141.d:
होतव्या मधुसर्पिभ्यां दध्ना वा पायसेन वा ॥
प्रादेशमात्रा ऋजवो विशाखा विफलाः शुभाः ॥ 32 ॥
4.141.m: kindling sticks should be offered with honey and ghee, or with curd, or with milk-rice. / Measuring a span in length, straight, unbranched, without fruit, and auspicious—

4.141.s:
kalpyaṃte samidhaḥ prājñaiḥ sarvakarmasu sarvadā ..
devānāmapi sarveṣāmupāṃśu paramārthavit .. 33 ..'
4.141.d:
कल्प्यंते समिधः प्राज्ञैः सर्वकर्मसु सर्वदा ॥
देवानामपि सर्वेषामुपांशु परमार्थवित् ॥ 33 ॥'
4.141.m: such kindling sticks are prepared by the wise in all rites at all times. / For all the deities as well, in a low voice, the knower of the supreme truth

4.141.s:
svena svenaiva maṃtreṇa hotavyāḥ samidhaḥ pṛthak ..
ākṛṣṇena imaṃ devā agnirmūrddhā divaḥ kramāt .. 34 ..
4.141.d:
स्वेन स्वेनैव मंत्रेण होतव्याः समिधः पृथक् ॥
आकृष्णेन इमं देवा अग्निर्मूर्द्धा दिवः क्रमात् ॥ 34 ॥
4.141.m: should offer the kindling sticks separately, each with its own mantra: / "By the dark [path]," "These, O gods," and "Agni is the head of heaven," in order,

4.141.s:
udbudhyasveti bodhyaśca yathāsaṃkhyamudāhṛtāḥ ..
bṛhaspate atiyadastathaivānnātparisutaḥ .. 35 ..
4.141.d:
उद्बुध्यस्वेति बोध्यश्च यथासंख्यमुदाहृताः ॥
बृहस्पते अतियदस्तथैवान्नात्परिसुतः ॥ 35 ॥
4.141.m: and "Awaken"—these are recited in their respective order— / "O Bṛhaspati, that which is transcendent," and likewise "From food distilled,"

4.141.s:
śannodevīti ca kayā ketuṃ kṛṇvannitīti ca ..
hotavyaṃ yadvadājyaṃ caruṃ bhakṣyāṇi vā punaḥ .. 36 ..
4.141.d:
शन्नोदेवीति च कया केतुं कृण्वन्नितीति च ॥
होतव्यं यद्वदाज्यं चरुं भक्ष्याणि वा पुनः ॥ 36 ॥
4.141.m: "May the divine waters be propitious to us," and "With what [aid]," and "Making a banner." / Clarified butter, sacrificial porridge, or eatables should be offered in the same way.

4.141.s:
maṃtrairdaśāhutīrdattvā homo vyāhṛtibhistataḥ ..
udaṅmukhāḥ prāṅmukhāśca kuryurbrāhmaṇapuṃgavāḥ .. 37 ..
4.141.d:
मंत्रैर्दशाहुतीर्दत्त्वा होमो व्याहृतिभिस्ततः ॥
उदङ्मुखाः प्राङ्मुखाश्च कुर्युर्ब्राह्मणपुंगवाः ॥ 37 ॥
4.141.m: Having offered ten oblations with these mantras, the oblation is then performed with the sacred utterances / by the foremost Brahmins facing either north or east.

4.141.s:
maṃtravaṃtastu kartavyāścaravaḥ pratidaivatam ..
apo rājeti rudrasya balihomaṃ samārabhet .. 38 ..
4.141.d:
मंत्रवंतस्तु कर्तव्याश्चरवः प्रतिदैवतम् ॥
अपो राजेति रुद्रस्य बलिहोमं समारभेत् ॥ 38 ॥
4.141.m: The sacrificial caru offerings, accompanied by mantras, are to be prepared for each deity. / With 'apo rājan,' one should begin the offering-oblation to Rudra.

4.141.s:
āpo hiṣṭetyumāyāstu śyeneti svāminastathā ..
viṣṇoridaṃ viṣṇuriti svamiccheti svayaṃbhuvaḥ .. .. 39 ..
